column2: Practices: ci-tests
column3: > **Original request:** > <!-- mahler:practices-audit:09e47f3e6d11a7b8e37256d93c8c7ecc4cefa14e402abe74ddd6f79af3124f1d --> > > Audit report: https://github.com/mkny13/mahler/issues/780 > > ## Evidence > > **ci-tests: unknown** — No proven unconditional PR test execution; workflow semantics need review. > > - .github/workflows/macos-tests.yml:23 job=macos-test run: swift test > - .github/workflows/test.yml:29 job=test run: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest > > ## Recommended repository change > > Add explicit test execution to pull-request CI, not just a build. > > ## Done when > > The read-only check passes; review heuristic candidates locally without publishing credential values. Run from the root of the worktree containing your changes, with Mahler installed. > > ```sh > python3 -c 'import json; from mahler.practices_audit import scan_project; from mahler.gh import GH; from pathlib import Path; p=json.loads('"'"'{"name": "phish-in", "repo": "mkny13/couch-tour", "verify": "JAVA_HOME=\\"/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home\\" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest && swift test --package-path macos/Packages/CouchTourKit"}'"'"'); p['"'"'path'"'"']=str(Path.cwd()); r=scan_project(p, GH(p['"'"'repo'"'"'])); f=next(f for f in r.findings if f.check == '"'"'ci-tests'"'"'); print(f); assert f.state == '"'"'pass'"'"', f.reason' > ``` ## Problem / goal The cross-project practices audit flagged `ci-tests: unknown` ("No proven unconditional PR test execution; workflow semantics need review"). In Couch Tour: - Android unit tests run via `.github/workflows/test.yml` (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`), path-filtered to `app/**`, Gradle files, and scripts. - macOS unit tests run via `.github/workflows/macos-tests.yml` (`swift test` and `xcodebuild ... test`), path-filtered to `macos/**`. - The path filters are an intentional performance optimization benchmarked in #506/#515 (`docs/PERF_CI_DURATIONS.md`) saving ~10 runner hours per 300 runs on Android and conserving expensive macOS-14 runner quota. - However, the Mahler practices audit scanner (`scan_project`) marks any PR workflow `unknown` if it has `paths:` filters, `${{` expressions (such as SPM build caching in `macos-tests.yml`), `working-directory:`, or if scripts like `./gradlew` contain shell control flow. - A mechanical `assert f.state == 'pass'` cannot be achieved without stripping these intentional path filters (running 5+ minutes of Android and macOS suites on every PR, including docs-only or single-platform changes) and removing build caching. ## Plan Files: - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Awaiting owner decision on whether to accept path-filtered PR CI as intentional (recording the rationale and benchmark evidence in `DECISIONS.md`) or to rework the workflows to run unconditionally on all PRs to pass the scanner. - If accepted: allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`, document the path-filtered CI rationale and reference to #506/#515 in `DECISIONS.md`, and verify test suites pass. - If reworking workflows: remove `paths:` filters, adjust runner steps, and ensure `scan_project` passes. Test: JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest && swift test --package-path macos/Packages/CouchTourKit ## Done when - [ ] Owner decision resolved on whether to retain path-filtered CI or rework workflows to satisfy scanner. - [ ] If accepted: `DECISIONS.md` documents why PR CI uses platform path filtering (#506/#515, `docs/PERF_CI_DURATIONS.md`) and why `ci-tests: unknown` is expected for this repository. - [ ] If reworked: `PYTHONPATH=~/Mahler python3 -c '... assert f.state == "pass", f.reason'` passes. - [ ] Existing local test suites pass cleanly: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest && swift test --package-path macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` ## Needs a human to check - The decision on whether to accept path-filtered CI or rework workflows to pass the scanner. ## Context - Issue #506 / #515 (Part 3 of #502) benchmarked CI durations across 300 runs and introduced path filtering for Android tests, documenting the ~10 runner-hour savings in `docs/PERF_CI_DURATIONS.md`. - `macos-tests.yml` uses macOS-14 runners which are constrained and billed at higher rates than Linux runners. - The Mahler practices audit (`practices_audit.py`, mahler#780) uses strict static checks that flag any dynamic expressions, shell script expansion (`./gradlew`), or path filtering as `unknown`. - Related issues: #556 (mahler-guidance), #557 (verify-command), #558 (tracked-secrets), #561 (branch-protection). ## Out of scope - Modifying test suite implementations or assertions. - Removing required app code or breaking CI functionality just to satisfy static regexes.

In `scripts/*.py`, look for `open()` without `with`, sockets or HTTP servers never closed, and `subprocess.Popen` never waited on. Fix each local one. 2. Dead code: unused exports and functions in `sync/src` (`npm run typecheck` plus grep of each export), and unused functions in `scripts/*.py` and `scripts/smoke/*.sh`. Remove them. 3. Each finding gets a file:line and what was done, plus a top-10 longest-functions table. 5. Anything bigger gets its own issue (`mahler add couch-tour`), linked from the report. column2: Android: exported MainActivity lets any app persist a sync base-URL override (syncBaseUrl intent extra)
column3: > **Original request:** Android: exported MainActivity lets any app persist a sync base-URL override (syncBaseUrl intent extra) ## Problem / goal `MainActivity` is an exported launcher and currently persists the `syncBaseUrl` intent extra in both `onCreate` and `onNewIntent`. Any installed app can redirect future sync traffic, including pairing, to a host it controls. Keep host overrides available to developers in debug and beta builds, but prevent release builds from accepting an override supplied by another app. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SyncTest.kt` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` - `scripts/test_sync_base_url_intent_guard.sh` - `.github/workflows/test.yml` Steps: 1. Gate handling of `syncBaseUrl` on `BuildConfig.DEBUG` for both initial launch and `onNewIntent`, preferably through one shared path so the two lifecycle routes cannot diverge. Leave the existing URL validation and token-host change behavior intact. 2. Add regression coverage proving a release/non-debug caller's override is ignored and debug/beta builds still accept valid overrides through the shared policy. 3. Add a source guard script and run it in the Android test workflow to catch an exported component forwarding an intent-provided sync URL to persistent configuration without the debug-only gate. 4. Correct the Android override examples in the README to describe debug/beta builds only, and append a DECISIONS entry superseding D314's Android override policy. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`; run `scripts/test_sync_base_url_intent_guard.sh` (also wired into `.github/workflows/test.yml`). ## Done when - [ ] Release/non-debug builds ignore `syncBaseUrl` both on cold launch and when an existing `MainActivity` receives a new intent; the configured release URL is not replaced or persisted. - [ ] Debug and beta builds still accept valid overrides through both lifecycle paths, and existing host-change token protections continue to work. - [ ] `SyncTest` has regression coverage for rejected release overrides and accepted debug overrides, and the source guard runs in CI. - [ ] README commands no longer imply that an installed production build can be redirected with an intent extra; DECISIONS.md records the chosen release boundary while preserving D314's history. ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context Technical decision: use the existing `BuildConfig.DEBUG` boundary rather than a hostname allowlist. Overrides are a developer/test facility and debug/beta builds need to switch between production, staging, and local/custom hosts; release builds should ignore untrusted intent extras entirely. Preserve macOS override behavior and existing Android URL validation/token-host protections. Escape cause: the exported launcher treated a caller-controlled intent extra as trusted configuration and persisted it in release builds. Check that now catches it: the new `SyncTest` regression tests and `scripts/test_sync_base_url_intent_guard.sh` run by `.github/workflows/test.yml`. ## Out of scope Changing sync backend behavior, adding a production Settings UI for host selection, changing macOS override handling, or restricting debug/beta overrides to a hostname allowlist.

column2: Part 2 of #473: Scripts & CI workflows security audit (subprocess args, uat-server CSRF, workflow permissions gate)
column3: > **Original request:** Security & Surface Area Audit — credential boundaries (`.env` leaks, unpooled URLs), subshell executions (`subprocess.run` argument sanitization), permission boundaries, denial list checks, dependency scans. Part of #473 ## Problem / goal Audit the developer scripts and CI workflows for command-injection risk, credential exposure and over-broad permissions, and add a check that keeps workflow permissions tight. The last scripts pass was #221. Since then these have been added: `scripts/beta_guard.py`, `scripts/contracts/*`, `scripts/smoke/*`, `scripts/smoke-sync-reset.sh`, `scripts/checks/*`, and a much larger `scripts/uat-server.py`, which now calls `subprocess.run(["gh", ...])` from a local HTTP server. CI workflows have never been audited. ## Plan Files: - `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_SCRIPTS_CI.md` - `scripts/uat-server.py` - `scripts/test_uat_server.py` - `scripts/beta_guard.py` - `scripts/contracts/shape_check.py` - `scripts/contracts/record.sh` - `scripts/smoke-sync-reset.sh` - `scripts/smoke/lib.sh` - `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` - `macos/scripts/install.sh` - `macos/scripts/install-beta.sh` - `.github/workflows/checks.yml` - `.github/workflows/macos-tests.yml` - `.github/workflows/sync-deploy.yml` - `.github/workflows/test.yml` - `.github/workflows/build-debug-apk.yml` - `.github/workflows/macos-release.yml` - `.github/workflows/beta-guard.yml` - `.github/workflows/contract-check.yml` - `scripts/checks/check-workflow-permissions.sh` - `scripts/checks/test_check_workflow_permissions.sh` - `.gitignore` Steps: - Python `subprocess.run` call sites (`uat-server.py`, `beta_guard.py`, `contracts/shape_check.py`): confirm list-form args, no `shell=True`, and that request- or issue-derived values can't become `gh` flags (add a `--` separator or validate them). For `uat-server.py`: it binds `127.0.0.1`, but check whether a web page in the owner's browser could POST to it (localhost CSRF) and trigger `gh` writes. If so, require a per-run token or check the `Origin` header, and add a test in `scripts/test_uat_server.py`. - Shell scripts (`scripts/**/*.sh`, `macos/scripts/*.sh`): look for unquoted expansions, `eval`, and `curl | sh`. Run `shellcheck` if it's available and record the result. - Workflows: give every workflow a top-level `permissions:` block with least privilege. `checks.yml`, `macos-tests.yml`, `sync-deploy.yml` and `test.yml` have none today. Confirm there is no `pull_request_target`, that `${{ github.event.* }}` / `inputs.*` are never interpolated straight into `run:` (pass them through `env:`), and that secrets (`DEBUG_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) are scoped to the steps that need them and never echoed. - Add `scripts/checks/check-workflow-permissions.sh`, which fails if any `.github/workflows/*.yml` has no top-level `permissions:`. Add its test and wire it into `checks.yml`, the same way `check-mockup-data.sh` is wired. - Tracked stray files at repo root: check `build_output.log`, `stderr.txt`, `stdout.txt`, `test_output.log`, `fix.patch`, `issue.txt`, `report.md` and similar for secrets, tokens, or absolute home paths. `git rm` the ones nothing references (grep first) and add ignore patterns for build/test logs to `.gitignore`. Record which were removed. - Note in the report that `.github/dependabot.yml` is missing. Don't add it here (see Out of scope). - Write `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_SCRIPTS_CI.md`: one row per script and per workflow, with result and evidence. Test: `python3 -m pytest scripts/` (or `python3 scripts/test_*.py` as CI runs them), `bash scripts/checks/test_check_workflow_permissions.sh`, and `scripts/checks/check-workflow-permissions.sh` all pass. The new check fails when run against a temp workflow file that has no `permissions:`. ## Done when - [ ] Every `.github/workflows/*.yml` has a top-level `permissions:` block, and `checks.yml` runs `scripts/checks/check-workflow-permissions.sh` - [ ] The new check has a test that proves it fails on a workflow missing `permissions:` - [ ] No workflow interpolates `github.event.*` or `inputs.*` directly in a `run:` script - [ ] `uat-server.py` rejects cross-origin/unauthenticated state-changing requests, with a test, or the report explains with evidence why it can't be reached - [ ] Unreferenced stray log/patch files at repo root are removed and log patterns are gitignored - [ ] `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_SCRIPTS_CI.md` exists with per-file results and evidence - [ ] Existing script tests still pass ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context Prior pass: #221 (all scripts quoted, no `eval`, at that time no `subprocess`). The "gates, not guidance" practice applies: a finding that could recur should become a failing check, not just a note. CI-only changes to workflow `permissions:` take effect on the next run, so watch that `build-debug-apk.yml` (creates releases) and `macos-release.yml` keep `contents: write`. ## Out of scope - `sync/` source and the Android/macOS apps (sibling sub-issues) - Adding Dependabot or Renovate, which would open PRs on a schedule (a separate product choice) - Rewriting scripts in another language

column2: macOS: On This Date caches a partial load (failed artist / swallowed period errors) for the day
column3: > **Original request:** Found by the #445 sweep. > > **Where:** `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` — `OnThisDate.load` caches whenever `!shows.isEmpty`. `showsOnDate` swallows per-period failures with `try? await src.shows` (line ~113) and only throws if every artist failed, so a partial list gets cached for the day. Android avoids this with `Fetched.complete` (`OnThisDate.kt:142,284`). > > **Done when:** incomplete results are returned but not cached, with a test using `assertErrorNotCachedAsEmpty`-style assertions. > > **Check that now catches it:** none yet; the fix adds the test. **Escape cause:** #391 fixed only the all-empty case on macOS. Part of #403 ## Problem / goal `OnThisDate.load` can cache a non-empty but incomplete list after one or more favorited artists or phish.in period requests fail. The Home shelf then serves that partial list for the rest of the day without retrying the failed requests. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/OnThisDateTests.swift` Steps: 1. Track whether every participating artist and every phish.in period request completed successfully, while preserving successful shows in the returned partial result. 2. Keep throwing when all artists fail, and return partial results when some succeed, but cache only complete, non-empty results. 3. Add tests for mixed artist success/failure and phish.in period success/failure. Verify partial shows are returned, the incomplete result is fetched again on the next load, and a subsequent complete result is cached. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test --filter OnThisDateTests` ## Done when - [ ] A failed Relisten artist alongside a successful artist returns the successful artist's shows without caching the partial result. - [ ] A failed phish.in period alongside a successful period returns available shows without caching the partial result. - [ ] The next load retries failed requests, and a complete non-empty result is cached. - [ ] Existing all-failed error behavior and complete-result cache behavior remain covered and pass. ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context This was identified by the #445 failed-load-cache sweep. The issue is limited to macOS; Android's `Fetched.complete` already prevents incomplete On This Date results from being cached. The all-empty case was fixed in #391, but non-empty partial results still pass the cache gate. ## Out of scope Android behavior, other discovery caches, and changing which On This Date shows are displayed.

column2: macOS: Next Tour Stops caches a partial load (failed artist / swallowed period errors) for the day
column3: > **Original request:** Found by the #445 sweep. > > **Where:** `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/NextStop.swift` — `NextStop.load` caches `shows` whenever non-empty. `currentTours` only throws if every artist failed, and `tourFor` swallows each period's failure with `try?` (lines ~82-111), so a failed period/artist yields a partial non-empty list that is cached under the day's key until the date or favorites change. > > **Done when:** a failed artist or period fetch makes the result "incomplete" and it is not cached (mirror Android `OnThisDate`'s `Fetched.complete`), with a test using `assertErrorNotCachedAsEmpty` (see `CacheErrorAssertions.swift`). > > **Check that now catches it:** none yet; the fix adds the test. **Escape cause:** #391 fixed only the all-empty case. Part of #403 ## Problem / goal `NextStop.load` currently caches any non-empty result, even when one or more artist or period requests failed. Since `tourFor` suppresses period errors and `currentTours` accepts partial success from multiple artists, a partial load can be reused for the rest of the day and hide shows that become available on retry. Treat any failed required fetch as an incomplete load and never cache that load's result. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/NextStop.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/NextStopTests.swift` Steps: 1. Track whether all artist and required period requests succeeded, keeping successful empty responses distinct from failed requests. 2. Carry completeness through the tour-loading path to `NextStop.load`; preserve any partial shows for the current return value, but cache only complete, non-empty results. 3. Add regression coverage for a partial multi-artist result and a failed period request. On retry with the same day, favorites, and preferences, assert that the failed request runs again and newly available shows are returned; retain checks for successful caching and empty-result behavior. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test --filter NextStopTests` ## Done when - [ ] A failure for any participating artist or required period marks the load incomplete, even if other requests returned shows. - [ ] An incomplete non-empty result is returned without entering the day cache; a same-key retry fetches again and can return the now-available shows. - [ ] Complete non-empty results still cache, and successful empty results retain their existing uncached behavior. - [ ] `swift test --filter NextStopTests` passes with regression tests for artist-level and period-level failures. - [ ] The new regression tests are the check that catches this class of bug; the escape cause is recorded as the former all-empty-only failure handling. ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context The existing macOS `NextStopTests.swift` tests caching, empty results, and preference resolution but not partial failures. The issue's `CacheErrorAssertions.swift` reference does not exist in this checkout; verify non-caching by asserting request counts and retry results in `NextStopTests.swift`. Android's `OnThisDate` completeness handling is a useful pattern, not a request to change Android. Preserve the existing one-day cache key and behavior for successful loads. ## Out of scope Android changes, UI redesign, and changing how the Home screen presents partial results or fetch errors.

column2: Android: Next Tour Stops caches a partial load (one artist failed) for the day
column3: > **Original request:** Found by the #445 sweep. > > **Where:** `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStop.kt` — `NextStop.load` writes `cached = key to shows` whenever `shows.isNotEmpty()`. `currentTours` only throws if *every* artist failed; if one favorite's fetch fails and another succeeds, the partial list is cached under the day's key and the failed artist's tour stays missing until the date or favorites change. > > **Repro:** two favorited artists on different backends; first load with one backend returning 500 → Home shows only the other's stop; retry/refresh keeps returning the cached partial list. > > **Done when:** a partial result is returned but not cached (compare `OnThisDate`'s `Fetched.complete` from #391), with a test using `assertErrorNotCachedAsEmpty`-style assertions (see `CacheErrorAssertions.kt`). > > **Check that now catches it:** none yet; the fix adds the test. **Escape cause:** #391 fixed only the all-empty case in this cache. Part of #403 ## Problem / goal `currentTours` intentionally returns successful artists' shows when another artist fetch fails, but it does not report that the result is incomplete. `NextStop.load` therefore caches any non-empty partial result for the day, so the failed artist is not retried until the cache key changes. Preserve useful partial results for the current load while preventing incomplete results from entering the daily cache. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStop.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStopTest.kt` Steps: 1. Carry a completion flag alongside the aggregated `currentTours` result, marking it incomplete if any participating artist fetch fails while preserving the successful artists' shows and the existing all-failed error behavior. 2. Update `NextStop.load` to cache a non-empty result only when all participating fetches completed successfully. 3. Add a regression test where one artist fails on the first load and succeeds on retry; assert the first load returns the other artist's result, does not cache the partial result, and the retry fetches and returns both artists' shows. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` (including the `NextStopTest` regression). ## Done when - [ ] Mixed success/failure still returns shows from successful artists but leaves the daily cache unset for that incomplete load. - [ ] A second load with the same date, favorites, and preferences retries the failed artist and returns the complete result. - [ ] Fully successful, non-empty results continue to be cached; the existing all-failed behavior remains unchanged. - [ ] The Android unit-test suite passes. ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context `OnThisDate.kt` already models the same distinction with `Fetched<T>.complete` and caches only complete results. This issue is the Next Tour Stops instance found in the #445 error-cached-as-empty sweep. The checkout has `NextStopTest.kt` as the focused fake-`MusicSource` test suite; the regression should assert the retry behavior directly. ## Out of scope - Changing whether partial results are displayed during the load that encountered a failure. - Changes to the Next Tour Stops UI, cache key, macOS behavior, or other discovery caches.

column2: Part 3 of #426: Sync backend test suite health audit
column3: Part of #426 ## Problem / goal Audit the sync backend's test suite (`sync/test/sync.test.ts`, vitest against real Miniflare D1) for test isolation, false-green tests, execution-time creep and leaked resources. Fix what's local and record the results. This suite was not in the first pass (#199). ## Plan Files: - `docs/TEST_HEALTH_SYNC.md` - `sync/test/sync.test.ts` - `sync/vitest.config.ts` - `README.md` - `CLAUDE.md` Steps: 1. Run `cd sync && npm install && npm run typecheck && npm test`. Record the test count and the duration of each test. 2. **Isolation:** check that each test starts from a clean D1 state (fresh schema, or unique users/devices per test) and doesn't depend on rows or order from earlier tests. Run with `--sequence.shuffle` a few times to prove it. 3. **False greens:** look for tests with no `expect`, un-awaited `expect(...).rejects`/promises, status-only assertions that would pass on a wrong body, and `it.skip`/`it.todo`. For each suspect, temporarily break the handler locally, confirm the test still passes, then tighten the assertion. 4. **Time creep:** list the slowest tests and remove real-time waits. 5. **Leaked resources:** confirm the Miniflare/D1 instances are disposed and vitest exits without hanging handles (`--reporter=hanging-process` if needed). 6. Write `docs/TEST_HEALTH_SYNC.md` with findings per category (fixed or filed as #N) and run times. Update the README/CLAUDE.md test count (currently "14 tests") only if the count changed. CLAUDE.md is a system-rule file, so change only that number. Test: `npm test` passes, and also passes with `--sequence.shuffle` three times. Each tightened test fails when its handler is broken. ## Done when - [ ] `docs/TEST_HEALTH_SYNC.md` is committed and covers all four categories - [ ] Every finding is either fixed in this PR or linked to a newly filed issue (`mahler` label, `type:`, `size:`) - [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass, including three shuffled runs - [ ] Documented test counts match the suite ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context This is the second run of the recurring `pass:tests` audit. The first run (#199, split into #211, #212/#244/#245 and #213) fixed Android file-DB isolation (PR #288), repaired false-green tests on both clients (#290, #289), and profiled run time (#296, D243). D243's baseline: Android ~13s for 535 tests, macOS `swift test` 0.81s for 381 tests. About 39 commits have touched test code since 2026-09-17, and README now lists 781 Android, 473 macOS and 14 sync tests, so concentrate on tests added or changed after then, though a full sweep is fine. "ResourceWarning" in the original request is a Python term. In this repo it means resources a test leaves open: servers, DB handles, coroutine or `Task` scopes, registered URLProtocols, temp files, timers. Each finding is either fixed in this PR (when the fix is local to test code or a test seam) or filed as its own issue: label `mahler`, a `type:`, a `size:`, in the standard body shape. The report records both kinds. ## Out of scope - Deploying (CI-only, never by hand), touching production D1, and the Android and macOS suites

Look for shared mutable state such as `object` singletons, companion caches, static `Room` instances, `Dispatchers.setMain` without `resetMain`, and file-backed DBs without per-test temp dirs. Flag anything that passes alone but fails in the suite (or the other way round). Fix it with `@Before`/`@After` resets or temp dirs. 3. **False greens:** grep for tests with no assertions, `assert*` calls inside swallowed `try/catch` or `runCatching`, `assertTrue(true)`, `@Ignore` without a reason, and coroutine tests whose `launch` bodies never run before the test ends (no `advanceUntilIdle`/`join`). For each suspect, temporarily break the code under test locally, confirm the test still passes, then repair the test. 4. **Time creep:** compare against the D243 baseline (~13s, 535 tests). List the 10 slowest classes. Remove `Thread.sleep` and real-time `delay` in favour of `runTest` virtual time or the existing clock seams. 5. **Leaked resources:** check that every `MockWebServer` is `shutdown()`, every in-memory/Room DB is `close()`d, `OkHttpClient` dispatchers and coroutine scopes are cancelled, and temp files are deleted. 6. Write `docs/TEST_HEALTH_ANDROID.md` with run-time numbers, findings per category (file:line, fixed or filed as #N), and the 10 slowest classes. Update README test counts if the count changed. Test: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes on three consecutive runs. Each repaired false-green test fails when its code under test is broken and passes when the code is restored (note how in the report). ## Done when - [ ] `docs/TEST_HEALTH_ANDROID.md` is committed and covers all four categories, with a before/after wall time and test count - [ ] Every finding is either fixed in this PR or linked to a newly filed issue (`mahler` label, `type:`, `size:`) - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes three times in a row - [ ] No `Thread.sleep` is left in `app/src/test` unless the report justifies it - [ ] The README test count matches the suite ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context This is the second run of the recurring `pass:tests` audit. The first run (#199, split into #211, #212/#244/#245 and #213) fixed Android file-DB isolation (PR #288), repaired false-green tests on both clients (#290, #289), and profiled run time (#296, D243). D243's baseline: Android ~13s for 535 tests, macOS `swift test` 0.81s for 381 tests. About 39 commits have touched test code since 2026-09-17, and README now lists 781 Android, 473 macOS and 14 sync tests, so concentrate on tests added or changed after then, though a full sweep is fine. "ResourceWarning" in the original request is a Python term. In this repo it means resources a test leaves open: servers, DB handles, coroutine or `Task` scopes, registered URLProtocols, temp files, timers. Each finding is either fixed in this PR (when the fix is local to test code or a test seam) or filed as its own issue: label `mahler`, a `type:`, a `size:`, in the standard body shape. The report records both kinds. ## Out of scope - macOS and sync suites (sibling sub-issues of #426) - Adding coverage for untested features, or refactoring production code beyond small test seams - Instrumented/device tests and `scripts/smoke/`

column2: Escaped bugs: CI check that fails on mockup/placeholder data in shipping code
column3: > **Original request:** "**Mockup/placeholder CI check:** a script under `scripts/checks/` plus a step in `test.yml` (or a new small workflow) that runs on every PR. It includes an allowlist and passes on current `main` (fix or allowlist existing hits, each allowlist entry with a reason)." Part of #403 ## Problem / goal Mockup/design data has shipped to beta/prod (#347 hardcoded sidebar artists, #355 placeholder jam-chart notes, #356 Ledger redesign audit). Add a cheap CI gate that fails a PR when known mockup/placeholder markers appear in shipping code. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/checks/check-mockup-data.sh` - `scripts/checks/mockup-allowlist.txt` - `scripts/checks/test_check_mockup_data.sh` - `.github/workflows/checks.yml` - `README.md` Decisions made by the sort run (technical — don't re-ask): - **New small workflow `checks.yml`, not a step in `test.yml`.** `test.yml` sets up Java/Gradle; a grep needs none of that and should fail in seconds. Trigger: `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch`, `ubuntu-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 5`. - **Scanned paths (shipping code only):** `app/src/main/**/*.kt`, `macos/CouchTour/**/*.swift`, `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/**/*.swift`. Not scanned: `app/src/test`, `app/src/androidTest`, `macos/**/Tests/**`, fixtures, docs. - **Preview code is skipped:** in Kotlin, skip any function annotated `@Preview` (simplest robust approach: skip lines from an `@Preview` annotation to the end of the following top-level function — or skip files whose name ends `Preview.kt`; pick one and document it). In Swift, skip `#Preview { ... }` blocks and `struct …_Previews: PreviewProvider` blocks. Brace-counting in awk/python is fine; a small Python 3 script called from the `.sh` wrapper is also fine (Python 3 is on ubuntu-latest). - **Patterns (case-insensitive, regex):** `lorem`, `ipsum`, `TODO: ?real data`, `mock(up)? ?data`, `placeholder (text|data|note|copy)`, `fake data`, `dummy data`, and the #347 mockup artist names as **string literals**: `"Goose"`, `"Grateful Dead"`, `"pgroove"`, `"TAB"`, `"WSP"`, `"Widespread Panic"`, `"Perpetual Groove"`. Bare `placeholder` is **not** a pattern: it hits Compose's `placeholder =` parameter, `CoverArtPlaceholder`, and `ArtworkView`'s artwork placeholder, all legitimate (checked on `main` at c608213). - **Allowlist format** (`mockup-allowlist.txt`): one entry per line, `path:pattern  # reason`; reason is mandatory (script fails on an entry without `# `). Expected entries on current main: `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/ArtistAbbreviations.kt` (real artist→abbreviation table), `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Artwork.swift` (per-artist artwork palette). Also allowlist the macOS twin of ArtistAbbreviations if it hits. Any other hit: fix it if it is real mockup data in shipping code (file an issue instead if the fix is non-trivial and allowlist it with `# tracked in #N`). - Output on failure: `path:line: matched '<pattern>' — remove mockup data or add to scripts/checks/mockup-allowlist.txt with a reason`, exit 1. Steps: 1. Write `check-mockup-data.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, repo-root relative like `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh`). 2. Run it on main; triage every hit into fix vs. allowlist-with-reason. 3. Write `test_check_mockup_data.sh`: builds a temp dir with fixture `.kt`/`.swift` files and asserts (a) a planted `"Goose"` literal in main code fails, (b) the same inside `@Preview` / `#Preview` passes, (c) an allowlisted hit passes, (d) an allowlist line without a reason fails. The script must accept a root dir override (e.g. `REPO_ROOT` env) to make this possible. 4. Add `.github/workflows/checks.yml` running the self-test then the check. 5. Mention the check in README (a line under the CI/tests section). Test: `scripts/checks/test_check_mockup_data.sh` passes locally; `scripts/checks/check-mockup-data.sh` exits 0 on the branch; the `checks` workflow is green on the PR. ## Done when - [ ] `scripts/checks/check-mockup-data.sh` exits 0 on the branch and exits 1 with a path:line message when a `"Goose"` string literal is added to a non-preview Kotlin or Swift file - [ ] Hits inside `@Preview` / `#Preview` / `PreviewProvider` code and under test directories are ignored - [ ] Every line in `mockup-allowlist.txt` has a `# reason`; the script rejects one that doesn't - [ ] `scripts/checks/test_check_mockup_data.sh` covers the four cases above and passes - [ ] `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs both on `pull_request` and is green on the PR ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context - Escapes: #347 (`SidebarView.swift` `fallbackFavoriteArtists`), #355, #356. - Existing check-script style: `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh`. - Mahler-wide generalization: mkny13/mahler#611. ## Out of scope - Error-cached-as-empty sweep and bug-template/CLAUDE.md process changes (sibling sub-issues of #403). - Wiring `check-ax-ids.sh` / `check-fixtures.sh` into the new workflow.

column2: Contract tests: weekly live shape check that files a drift issue
column3: Part of #405 Depends on: #441 > **Original request (from #405):** **Scheduled live check:** a weekly `schedule:` workflow that re-records and diffs structure (keys and types, not values). On a shape change it opens or updates one `mahler`-labelled issue naming the endpoint and diff. It never fails PR CI. ## Problem / goal Recorded fixtures (#441) go stale the moment upstream changes. A weekly job re-records into a temp dir, compares the **shape** (keys and JSON types, not values) with the committed `contract_*.json` files, and reports drift as one GitHub issue. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/contracts/shape_check.py` - `scripts/contracts/test_shape_check.py` - `.github/workflows/contract-check.yml` Steps: 1. `shape_check.py` (stdlib only):    - `shape(value)` reduces JSON to a structure of `{key: shape}` for objects, `[union of element shapes]` for arrays, and type names (`string`, `number`, `bool`, `null`, `object`, `array`) for leaves. Fields that are sometimes null show as a union like `string|null`. Merging array elements means trimming and reordering don't count as changes.    - `diff(old, new)` returns readable lines per endpoint: `+ key.path (type)`, `- key.path`, `~ key.path: string -> number`.    - CLI: `shape_check.py --committed app/src/test/resources/fixtures --fresh DIR` compares every `contract_*.json` and prints a markdown report. Exit code 0 means no drift, 1 means drift.    - `--report-issue`: if drift, find an open issue titled `Contract drift: upstream API shape changed` (label `mahler`) via `gh`. Comment the report on it if one exists, otherwise create it with labels `mahler` and `type:bug`. Exactly one open issue at a time. Follow `scripts/beta_guard.py`'s `gh` pattern.    - A fetch failure (5xx, timeout) is not drift. Report it in the job log and skip that endpoint, so a phish.in outage doesn't file an issue. 2. `test_shape_check.py` (unittest, like `scripts/test_beta_guard.py`): same values → no drift; added, removed and retyped key → each reported with its path; nullable field and array-length differences → no drift; the issue-upsert logic with `gh` calls stubbed (create vs comment). 3. `.github/workflows/contract-check.yml`: `on: schedule` (weekly, e.g. `cron: "17 7 * * 1"`) + `workflow_dispatch` only, **no** `pull_request`/`push`. `permissions: contents: read, issues: write`. Steps: checkout, setup-python 3.12, `python3 scripts/contracts/record.py --out-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/fresh"`, then `python3 scripts/contracts/shape_check.py --committed app/src/test/resources/fixtures --fresh "$RUNNER_TEMP/fresh" --report-issue` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. The job succeeds even when it finds drift; the issue is the signal. Test: `python3 -m unittest scripts/contracts/test_shape_check.py` passes, and a local run of shape_check against a fresh record prints no drift (or a real one, which goes in the PR description). ## Done when - [ ] `shape_check.py` + unit tests exist and pass - [ ] `contract-check.yml` triggers only on `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`, never on PRs - [ ] On drift it creates or comments on a single `mahler`-labelled issue naming each endpoint and its key/type diff; no issue on no-drift or fetch failure ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context - Recorder and `--out-dir` flag come from #441 (`scripts/contracts/record.py`). - Precedent scheduled-issue job: `.github/workflows/beta-guard.yml` + `scripts/beta_guard.py`. - Mahler-wide version of this idea: mkny13/mahler#611. ## Out of scope - Automatically committing re-recorded fixtures or opening PRs. - Any check that runs on PR CI.
