column2: Contract tests: recorder script + recorded phish.in/Relisten fixtures + Android decode tests
column3: Part of #405 > **Original request (from #405):** a `scripts/contracts/record.sh` that fetches a small, representative set of real responses (phish.in show/year/song/search/on-date; Relisten artist/year/show/on-date; the curated-match JSON the app loads) into fixture dirs used by *both* Android (MockWebServer tests) and CouchTourKit tests. Each client gets at least one decode test per endpoint over those recorded files. … Keep the fetch polite (a handful of requests, a User-Agent identifying Couch Tour) and within phish.in's API terms. ## Problem / goal Today's fixtures (`show.json`, `relisten_show.json`, …) are trimmed or hand-shaped, so upstream drift passes CI and breaks on devices (#353, #388). This issue adds a recorder that captures **real** responses from the endpoints the clients actually call, commits them to both fixture dirs, and adds Android decode tests over them. The macOS tests are #442 (separate issue); the weekly live check is #443. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/contracts/record.sh` - `scripts/contracts/record.py` - `app/src/test/resources/fixtures/contract_*.json` (new, recorded) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/Fixtures/contract_*.json` (new, byte-identical copies) - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/ContractFixturesTest.kt` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: 1. `scripts/contracts/record.py` (stdlib only, Python 3) holds one table of endpoints → output name. Use the endpoints the clients really call (`Api.kt`, `Relisten.kt`), not the issue's loose list:    - phish.in (`https://phish.in/api/v2`): `years` → `contract_phishin_years.json`; `shows?year=1997&audio_status=complete_or_partial&sort=date:asc&per_page=1000` → `contract_phishin_shows_year.json`; `shows/1997-11-22` → `contract_phishin_show.json`; `search/tweezer?audio_status=complete_or_partial` → `contract_phishin_search.json`; `playlists?sort=likes_count:desc&per_page=100` → `contract_phishin_playlists.json`. (phish.in has no song or on-date endpoint in our clients; On This Date uses `shows?year_range=`, which the year fetch covers.)    - Relisten (`https://api.relisten.net/api`): `v3/artists` → `contract_relisten_artists.json`; `v3/artists/{phish uuid}/years` → `contract_relisten_years.json`; `v3/artists/{uuid}/years/{1997 year uuid}` → `contract_relisten_year.json`; `v2/artists/phish/shows/1997-11-22` → `contract_relisten_show.json`; `v2/artists/phish/shows/on-date?month=11&day=22` → `contract_relisten_on_date.json`; `v3/search?q=tweezer` → `contract_relisten_search.json`. Resolve the uuids from the artists/years responses at record time, not hard-coded.    - Every request sends `User-Agent: CouchTour-contract-recorder (+https://github.com/mkny13/couch-tour)`, runs sequentially with a ~1 s pause, ~11 requests total.    - To keep fixtures small, trim every JSON array to its first 3 elements, recursively. Values stay real and the shape is unchanged. Write pretty-printed with sorted keys so re-records diff cleanly.    - Write each file to **both** fixture dirs so `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh` passes unchanged. Take `--out-dir DIR` (default: both repo fixture dirs) so #443 can record into a temp dir. 2. `record.sh` is a thin wrapper: `exec python3 "$(dirname "$0")/record.py" "$@"`. 3. Run it and commit the recorded files. 4. Curated-match JSON is a bundled asset (`app/src/main/assets/curated_releases.json`, `heuristic_matches.json`, copied into CouchTourKit `Resources/`), not fetched. Don't record it. The contract is that the shipped files decode, so test them where they are. 5. `ContractFixturesTest.kt`: one test per `contract_*.json`, decoding it with the production `Json` config and DTO the client uses (`List<Period>`, `ShowsPage`, `Show`, `SearchResults`, `PlaylistsPage`, `List<RelistenArtist>`, `List<RelistenYear>`, `RelistenYearWithShows`, `RelistenShowWithSources`, `List<RelistenShowSummary>`, `RelistenSearchResults`), plus one non-empty assertion per test (e.g. show has tracks). Serve at least the phish.in show and the Relisten show through `MockWebServer` via the real `PhishInApi`/`RelistenApi` with `baseUrl` pointed at it, so the request path is exercised too. Add a test that `CuratedMatches` and `HeuristicMatches` load their real bundled assets with non-zero entries (Robolectric context). 6. If a recorded response fails to decode, that's a real bug. Fix the DTO (and its Swift twin, if the same field is wrong there) in this PR, or file an issue and `@Ignore` that one test with the issue number. 7. Log a `D` entry (`mahler next-id couch-tour D`): recorded contract fixtures, the `contract_` prefix, trimming arrays to 3 elements, and how to re-record. 8. Update the Android test count in `README.md`. Test: `JAVA_HOME=… ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes with the new tests, and `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh` prints "Fixtures match." ## Done when - [ ] `scripts/contracts/record.sh` runs from repo root and (re)writes 11 `contract_*.json` files to both fixture dirs, with a Couch Tour User-Agent and sequential polite requests - [ ] Recorded fixtures are committed; `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh` passes - [ ] `ContractFixturesTest.kt` has ≥1 decode test per recorded file plus curated/heuristic asset load tests; `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green - [ ] README Android test count updated; D-entry added to DECISIONS.md ## Needs a human to check Nothing ## Context - Existing fixture loaders: `ApiParsingTest.kt` (`fixture()`), CouchTourKit `Fixture.swift`. Parity guard: `macos/scripts/check-fixtures.sh` (D35). - Precedent for offline fetch scripts: `scripts/generate_heuristic_matches.py`. - Motivating drift: #353, #388. ## Out of scope - CouchTourKit decode tests (#442), weekly scheduled check (#443). - Replacing or deleting the existing hand-shaped fixtures.

column2: Triage four unmerged agent branches rescued from stale Antigravity worktrees
column3: > **Original request:** Four branches were pushed 2026-09-30 from deleted Antigravity worktrees (~/.gemini/antigravity/worktrees/phish-in-app) so no work was lost. None was ever merged or had a PR. Decide for each: still wanted, already superseded on main, or discard. > > Branches (commits not on main at push time): > - add_theme_settings_modes: 3 commits (light/dark/auto theme setting for Android and macOS, D216) > - fix-mac-home-markup-feedback: 2 commits, the second is a WIP commit of uncommitted screenshots and scripts/markup-tool.html (Home Screen markup feedback, D217) > - macos-home-screen-fixes-144: 1 commit (remove unwired filter pills and carousel buttons from Home, #144, D230) > - organize_project_directory_assets: 1 commit (design handoff, branding assets, specs, D213) > > Done looks like: one checklist comment on this issue, one line per branch with the verdict and evidence (is the change already on main? does it still apply? does verify pass after rebase?). For branches worth keeping, rebase onto main, open a PR with Fixes #N for the relevant issue, and let CI decide. For superseded or abandoned ones, delete the remote branch and say so. Watch for decision-number (D2xx) collisions in DESIGN or docs when rebasing. Deliverable is the triage comment plus any resulting PRs; do not merge anything that fails verify. ## Problem / goal The sort run finished the triage and posted it as the checklist comment on this issue. Three branches were already on main, and their remote branches are deleted: - `add_theme_settings_modes` landed via #137. - `macos-home-screen-fixes-144` (D230) is on main. - `organize_project_directory_assets` (D213) is on main. On `fix-mac-home-markup-feedback`, D217 landed via #138, and its WIP screenshots already match main byte for byte. The only work left is `scripts/markup-tool.html`, a standalone HTML page for marking up macOS screens (359 lines). It exists only on that branch. This build salvages that one file onto main, then deletes the branch. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/markup-tool.html` Steps: 1. `git fetch origin fix-mac-home-markup-feedback`. 2. `git checkout origin/fix-mac-home-markup-feedback -- scripts/markup-tool.html`. Take only this file. Do not bring in the screenshots or anything else from that branch. 3. Open the file and check it for anything that shouldn't be committed: absolute paths under `/Users/…`, tokens, or personal data. If you find any, replace it with a relative path or a placeholder. Leave everything else as it is. It's a dev helper and has no app code. 4. Commit it as "Salvage scripts/markup-tool.html from rescued fix-mac-home-markup-feedback branch (#438)", with `Fixes #438` in the commit body, and push. 5. After your push succeeds, delete the rescued branch with `git push origin --delete fix-mac-home-markup-feedback`. Its only unique content is now on your branch. Its tip SHA `9c5a097` is recorded in the triage comment, so it can be recovered. Test: `git diff origin/fix-mac-home-markup-feedback -- scripts/markup-tool.html` shows nothing, unless step 3 scrubbed something. The file opens as valid HTML (`python3 -c "import html.parser,sys; html.parser.HTMLParser().feed(open('scripts/markup-tool.html').read())"` exits 0). No app code changes, so the Android and macOS test suites aren't needed. ## Done when - [ ] `scripts/markup-tool.html` exists on the pushed branch and matches the rescued branch's version, apart from any documented scrubs. - [ ] The diff touches no other file. - [ ] `git ls-remote --heads origin fix-mac-home-markup-feedback` returns nothing. - [ ] Of the four rescued branches, none is left on the remote: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -E 'add_theme_settings_modes|fix-mac-home-markup-feedback|macos-home-screen-fixes-144|organize_project_directory_assets'` is empty. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context - The per-branch triage and its evidence are in the agent comment on this issue. - None of D213, D216, D217 or D230 collides with another entry. Each appears once in DECISIONS.md, and this build adds no decision entry. - The markup tool was created during the D217 Home Screen markup-feedback round (#138). ## Out of scope - Re-applying any code from the three superseded branches. All of it is already on main. - The screenshots in the WIP commit, which are identical to main. - Wiring the markup tool into `uat-server.py`, or writing docs for it.

column2: macOS: Settings diagnostics viewer with Copy and Clear
column3: > **Original request:** > > macOS Settings (or an About surface) provides a way to view, copy, and clear diagnostics. Part of #430 Depends on: #433 ## Problem / goal On macOS, there is currently no UI to inspect or clear the on-device diagnostics log. The user cannot see what the app recorded or clear old logs when troubleshooting. This sub-issue adds a Diagnostics viewer in macOS Settings (accessible from `PlaybackSettingsView` as a dedicated sheet): - Header showing summary lines (total entries, on-disk size, and marked values). - Monospace scrollable viewer showing the latest 200 log entries (`DiagnosticsLog.tailLines(200)`). - "Copy Diagnostics" button that copies the export text (`exportText()`) to the system pasteboard (`NSPasteboard.general`). - "Clear Diagnostics" button that removes both log files and resets marks, protected by a confirmation alert. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/PlaybackSettingsView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/DiagnosticsView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` - `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Create `DiagnosticsView.swift` in `macos/CouchTour/` with summary card, monospace tail log list, Copy button, and confirmable Clear button. - In `PlaybackSettingsView.swift`, add a "Diagnostics" button/row in the About section that presents `DiagnosticsView` in a sheet. - Ensure all file I/O operations (`tailLines`, `exportText`, `clear`) run asynchronously off the main thread so UI stays responsive. - Register accessibility identifiers in `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` and verify with `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh`. - Regenerate Xcode project with `cd macos && xcodegen generate` and verify build with `xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`. - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and record viewer choices in `DECISIONS.md`. Test: - `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh` passes. - `xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` succeeds. ## Done when - [ ] Settings -> Playback (About section) provides an entry point to open the Diagnostics viewer. - [ ] Diagnostics viewer shows summary header with entry count, disk size, and recent marks. - [ ] Viewer displays the last 200 lines in monospace format. - [ ] "Copy Diagnostics" copies export text to `NSPasteboard.general`. - [ ] "Clear Diagnostics" prompts for confirmation, then deletes log files and clears the display. - [ ] All disk I/O runs asynchronously without blocking SwiftUI rendering or the main runloop. - [ ] Accessibility identifiers are declared in `AXIdentifiers.swift` and verified by `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh`. - [ ] Xcode build succeeds. - [ ] DECISIONS.md has a new entry. ## Needs a human to check - Open Settings (⌘,), open Diagnostics, confirm monospace log lines are legible, Copy puts text on clipboard, and Clear deletes log lines after confirmation. ## Context - Android precedent: #376 and D293. - `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` already hosts the "Software Updates" and version info section. - Accessibility identifier conventions: `settings.diagnostics.*` in `AXIdentifiers.swift`. ## Out of scope - FeedbackButton integration. - Auto-refreshing live tail or search/filter inside the viewer.

column2: macOS: Core on-device rotating diagnostics log in CouchTourKit
column3: > **Original request:** > > Issue #344 implemented on-device diagnostics on Android: DiagnosticsLog.kt (in-memory circular log buffer with crash capture), DiagnosticsScreen.kt (viewer in Settings -> About -> Diagnostics with Share, Copy, and Clear), and FeedbackButton.kt (copies diagnostic tail to clipboard and embeds summary into GitHub issue URL). Issue #344 explicitly noted macOS diagnostics as out of scope: "macOS diagnostics (separate issue; there is a parallel gap there)." > > On macOS, there is no in-app diagnostics log buffer, no diagnostics viewer in Settings, and FeedbackButton.swift cannot attach or copy recent app diagnostic logs. > > CouchTourKit gains an in-memory/on-disk diagnostics logger capturing key events (API timings, sync cycles, playback errors) with redacting for auth tokens/secrets. Unit tests cover log rotation, sizing, and secret sanitization. Part of #430 ## Problem / goal There is no on-device diagnostics logger in `CouchTourKit` on macOS. When errors occur or when the app behaves unexpectedly, there is no persistent local log history to inspect or attach to feedback reports. This sub-issue implements the core diagnostics logging foundation: a thread-safe, rotating, append-only logger in `CouchTourKit` with bounded disk footprint, credential redaction, startup retention pruning, summary marks, and inspection APIs. Design decisions (mirroring Android D292/D294): - **Storage Location**: `~/Library/Application Support/dev.mike.couchtour/diagnostics/` (or a directory passed during initialization for testing). Two log files: `diagnostics.log` (current) and `diagnostics.log.1` (previous generation). - **Bounded Footprint & Rotation**: 1 MiB cap per file, bounding on-disk footprint to 2 MiB total. When `diagnostics.log` reaches 1 MiB, rotate: delete `diagnostics.log.1`, rename `diagnostics.log` to `diagnostics.log.1`, start a fresh `diagnostics.log`, and write a `log.rotated` entry. - **Retention**: On `init`, prune entries older than 7 days from both generations. If a file is still over 1 MiB after date pruning, truncate down to the last 2000 lines. - **Line Format**: Tab-separated `<ISO-8601 UTC timestamp>\t<LEVEL>\t<event>\t<key>=<value> ...` matching Android D292. - **Redaction Denylist**: Key names matching `token`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `auth`, `credential`, `cookie`, `pairing`, `code`, `key` (as word or compound like `access_token`, `syncKey`, but excluding bare `key` and `code` identifiers) redact values to `***`. - **Concurrency & Non-blocking writes**: Thread-safe logging (`actor DiagnosticsLog` or serial-queue backed) that never throws or blocks caller threads. Disk I/O failures latch logging off rather than propagating exceptions. - **Marks & Inspection APIs**:   - `mark(key:value:)`: stores latest marker values (e.g. `Last sync`) for `summaryLines()`.   - `summaryLines() -> String`: human-readable summary of marks, total line count, and on-disk size.   - `tailLines(_ n: Int) -> [String]`: returns the last `n` lines (bounded read from tail, up to 256 KiB).   - `exportText() -> String`: exports full log text (generation `.1` then current).   - `clear()`: deletes both log files and resets marks.   - `onDiskBytes() -> Int64`: returns total size on disk. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/DiagnosticsLog.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/DiagnosticsLogTests.swift` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Implement `DiagnosticsLog` in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/DiagnosticsLog.swift`. - Provide initialization with a configurable directory (defaulting to App Support diagnostics directory). - Implement formatted line writing with redaction denylist and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. - Implement rotation at 1 MiB cap and startup retention (7 days / 2000 lines). - Implement `mark`, `summaryLines`, `tailLines`, `exportText`, `clear`, and `onDiskBytes`. - Add comprehensive unit tests in `CouchTourKitTests/DiagnosticsLogTests.swift`. - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and record storage, rotation, retention, and redaction choices in `DECISIONS.md`. - Update README.md test count. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` ## Done when - [ ] `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes with new diagnostics tests. - [ ] On-disk diagnostics footprint is bounded at 2 MiB, proven by rotation tests. - [ ] Sensitive credential keys (`token`, `secret`, `password`, `syncKey`, `accessToken`, `pairingCode`) have values redacted to `***`. - [ ] Retention prunes entries older than 7 days and limits over-cap files to the last 2000 lines. - [ ] `tailLines(n)` returns the last `n` lines in chronological order without reading entire multi-megabyte files into memory. - [ ] `summaryLines()` reports recent marked values, entry count, and byte size. - [ ] Logging operations never throw or block caller execution; I/O failures fail closed safely. - [ ] DECISIONS.md has a new `Dnnn` entry and README.md test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing (pure package logic verified by unit tests). ## Context - Android precedent: #373 and D292. - Log directory on macOS should be in `~/Library/Application Support/dev.mike.couchtour/diagnostics/` alongside `phishin.db` (D171). - Package test execution: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test`. ## Out of scope - UI diagnostics viewer (handled in separate sub-issue). - Feedback button integration (handled in separate sub-issue). - Instrumenting API/sync/playback call sites (handled in separate sub-issue). - Uploading diagnostics to any server or remote service.

column2: macOS: PlaybackSettings lacks Audio Quality (FLAC vs MP3) and Gapless playback preferences
column3: > **Original request:** > ## Problem / goal >  > Android supports user preferences for audio streaming quality and gapless playback in `PlaybackSettings.kt`: >  > 1. `audioQuality` (`AudioQuality.LOSSLESS` vs `AudioQuality.COMPRESSED`), surfaced in `SettingsScreen.kt` via a radio picker dialog ("FLAC (lossless)" vs "MP3") and respected at queue construction time (`MediaItems.kt:231`). > 2. `gapless` playback toggle, applied to player preloading. >  > On macOS, `PlaybackSettings.swift` only models `skipFiller` and `levelVolume`. `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` has no control for selecting audio quality or configuring gapless playback. As noted in `docs/MODEL_PARITY_AUDIT.md:115`, macOS lacks these settings entirely. >  > ## What done looks like >  > • `PlaybackSettings.swift` adds `audioQuality` (`.lossless` / `.compressed`) and `gapless` preferences backed by `UserDefaults`. > • `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` in the Settings (⌘,) window renders controls for Audio Quality and Gapless playback. > • Stream resolution honors the audio quality preference when selecting between `flacUrl` and `mp3Url`. > • Unit tests in `PlaybackSettingsTests.swift` cover persistence and default values. >  > ## Context >  > • Found during the baseline feature parity audit (#292, `docs/PARITY_AUDIT.md`). > • Identified previously in `docs/MODEL_PARITY_AUDIT.md:115` as a model and UI discrepancy. > • Android counterpart: `PlaybackSettings.kt:53`, `SettingsScreen.kt:144,166`, `MediaItems.kt:231`. > • macOS target files: >   • `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PlaybackSettings.swift` >   • `macos/CouchTour/PlaybackSettingsView.swift` >   • `macos/CouchTour/Player.swift` ## Problem / goal Android supports user preferences for audio streaming quality and gapless playback in `PlaybackSettings.kt` (D228, #141): 1. `audioQuality` (`AudioQuality.LOSSLESS` vs `AudioQuality.COMPRESSED`, default lossless), surfaced in `SettingsScreen.kt` via radio picker ("FLAC (lossless)" vs "MP3") and respected at queue construction time. 2. `gapless` playback toggle (default true), controlling player preloading. On macOS, `PlaybackSettings.swift` only models `skipFiller` and `levelVolume`. `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` has no controls for selecting audio quality or toggling gapless playback, and `Player.swift` always defaults to `flacUrl` if present regardless of user preference. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PlaybackSettings.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/PlaybackSettingsTests.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlaybackSettingsView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/Player.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlayerRailView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` - `DECISIONS.md` - `ROADMAP.md` Steps: - In `PlaybackSettings.swift`, declare `public enum AudioQuality: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Sendable` with cases `lossless` ("lossless") and `compressed` ("compressed"), matching Android's storage values. - Add `@Published public var audioQuality: AudioQuality` to `PlaybackSettings` (default `.lossless`, backed by `UserDefaults` key `"audio_quality"`). - Add `@Published public var gapless: Bool` to `PlaybackSettings` (default `true`, backed by `UserDefaults` key `"gapless"`). - In `PlaybackSettingsTests.swift`, test defaults (`audioQuality == .lossless`, `gapless == true`), test persistence across instances for both keys, and test fallback for unknown/nil stored values. - In `PlaybackSettingsView.swift`, add a Toggle for "Gapless playback" bound to `$settings.gapless` and a Picker for "Audio Quality" bound to `$settings.audioQuality` offering "FLAC (lossless)" and "MP3". - In `Player.swift`, respect `playbackSettings.audioQuality` during stream resolution: when `.compressed`, play `track.url` (MP3) unless `track.url` is empty, falling back to `track.flacUrl` so a tape is never unplayable; when `.lossless`, prefer `track.flacUrl` if present, falling back to `track.url`. - In `Player.swift`, respect `playbackSettings.gapless`: when `gapless` is true, preload upcoming queue items into `queuePlayer`; when `gapless` is false, do not preload upcoming queue items ahead of track end. - In `PlayerRailView.swift` and `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift`, ensure the "FLAC" quality badge reflects the stream format actually being played (suppressed when `.compressed` selects MP3). - Record architectural decision in `DECISIONS.md` and update `ROADMAP.md` entry. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes all tests. ## Done when - [ ] `AudioQuality` enum (`lossless`, `compressed`) is defined in `CouchTourKit` with display titles. - [ ] `PlaybackSettings` stores `audioQuality` (default `.lossless`, key `"audio_quality"`) and `gapless` (default `true`, key `"gapless"`) in `UserDefaults`. - [ ] `PlaybackSettingsTests.swift` passes unit tests for defaults and persistence across instances. - [ ] `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` displays "Audio Quality" picker and "Gapless playback" toggle in Settings > Playback. - [ ] `Player.swift` honors `audioQuality` preference at queue construction time. - [ ] `Player.swift` honors `gapless` preference for player queue preloading. - [ ] `swift test` in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` passes cleanly. ## Needs a human to check - Open Settings (⌘,) in macOS app, verify "Audio Quality" picker and "Gapless playback" toggle appear in the Playback tab and update values. - Verify playback of a Relisten show with FLAC sources honors the selected quality (FLAC vs MP3). ## Context - Baseline feature parity audit #292 (`docs/PARITY_AUDIT.md:126`). - Noted in `docs/MODEL_PARITY_AUDIT.md:115` as a model and UI discrepancy. - Android counterpart: `PlaybackSettings.kt:53`, `SettingsScreen.kt:144,166`, `MediaItems.kt:231`, `PlaybackService.kt:230` (D228, #141). - ROADMAP.md Phase 2 tracking: "macOS Audio Quality Control — unbuilt, untracked (#141 closed)". ## Out of scope - Offline caching or downloads (closed in #65). - Crossfade playback or variable segue duration. - Per-artist or cellular/Wi-Fi adaptive bitrate rules.

column2: Add Android search field testTag for smoke tests
column3: > **Original request:** The Android smoke runner scripts/smoke/run-android.sh currently locates the search field via android_parse "center_class" "android.widget.EditText", which violates the resource-id selection rule. A11yTags.kt lacks a testTag for the search input field on SearchScreen. Add a testTag (e.g., search.field) to the OutlinedTextField in SearchScreen.kt and expose it via A11yTags so the smoke runner can select the field by resource-id instead of class. Depends on: #370 ## Problem / goal In Couch Tour's smoke testing framework, runners select UI elements strictly by stable accessibility identifiers / resource-ids rather than class names or heuristics. During the development of the Android smoke runner (#370), `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` temporarily used `android_parse "center_class" "android.widget.EditText"` to tap the search input field in `search-artist-hit` and `search-result-sections`. That class-based tap was removed because `A11yTags.kt` and `SearchScreen.kt` lacked a dedicated `testTag` for the search input field. Goal: Add `const val SEARCH_FIELD = "search.field"` (matching macOS `AXIdentifiers.searchField`) to `A11yTags.kt`, tag the `OutlinedTextField` in `SearchScreen.kt` with `Modifier.testTag(A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD)`, verify it via unit tests in `A11yTagsTest.kt`, and update `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` to select and tap the search field by resource-id before typing search queries. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SearchScreen.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt` - `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` Steps: - In `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt`:   - Add `const val SEARCH_FIELD = "search.field"` under the search constants section (matching macOS `AXIdentifiers.searchField`). - In `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SearchScreen.kt`:   - Import `androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag`.   - Add `.testTag(A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD)` to the modifier chain on `OutlinedTextField`. - In `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt`:   - Add a unit test verifying `A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD` equals `"search.field"` and resolves when queried via `compose.onNodeWithTag(A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD)`. - In `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh`:   - In `android_run_search_artist_hit` and `android_run_search_result_sections`: tap `search.field` using `android::tap "search.field" "$TIMEOUT"` after navigating to `nav.search` and before typing search terms (`android::text`).   - In `run_self_tests`: add a test node with `resource-id="dev.mike.couchtour.beta:id/search.field"` and assert `android_parse "count" "search.field"` returns 1. - Run test suites to prove:   - Unit tests: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`   - Smoke runner self-tests: `bash scripts/smoke/run-android.sh --test` Test: - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests 'dev.mike.couchtour.A11yTagsTest'` - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` - `bash scripts/smoke/run-android.sh --test` ## Done when - [ ] `A11yTags.kt` defines `SEARCH_FIELD = "search.field"`. - [ ] `SearchScreen.kt` applies `Modifier.testTag(A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD)` to `OutlinedTextField`. - [ ] `A11yTagsTest.kt` contains test assertions confirming `A11yTags.SEARCH_FIELD` semantics and tag resolution. - [ ] `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` selects and taps `search.field` via `android::tap "search.field"` in `search-artist-hit` and `search-result-sections`. - [ ] `bash scripts/smoke/run-android.sh --test` passes. - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes. ## Needs a human to check - On a connected Android device or emulator with Couch Tour Beta installed: run `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh --tag <tag> search-artist-hit` and verify that the search field is successfully tapped and focused by `resource-id` (`search.field`) without class fallback. ## Context - #364 added `A11yTags.kt` and tagged navigation items, Home sections, favorites, and search result sections using `Modifier.testTag(...)`. - macOS equivalent is `AXIdentifiers.searchField = "search.field"` in `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift`. - In #370 / PR #422, the Android smoke runner (`scripts/smoke/run-android.sh`) was reviewed and required to eliminate class-based selection (`center_class` / `android.widget.EditText`) in favor of deterministic resource-id lookup. - #421 enables `testTagsAsResourceId = true` on the Compose tree root so that `Modifier.testTag` is mapped to Android `AccessibilityNodeInfo` `viewIdResourceName` / `resource-id` for `uiautomator dump`. ## Out of scope - Tagging other search surfaces or search result items beyond the search input field. - Modifying macOS search accessibility identifiers (`macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` already defines `searchField`). - Changes to the Google TV surface (`TvMainActivity`).

column2: Android: testTag does not populate resource-id in uiautomator dump without testTagsAsResourceId
column3: > **Original request:** In #364, Modifier.testTag was added to Android surfaces (nav, home sections, favorites, search). > However, testing against an Android device/emulator during #370 confirmed that `adb shell uiautomator dump` yields empty `resource-id=""` for all Compose nodes. Only native Android view containers (e.g. `android:id/content`) populate resource-id. >  > In Jetpack Compose, testTag is only mapped to `AccessibilityNodeInfo.viewIdResourceName` (which uiautomator surfaces as `resource-id`) when `Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true }` is set on the root Compose tree or components. >  > Without `testTagsAsResourceId = true`, uiautomator cannot locate Compose nodes by resource-id alone. >  > Done when: >  > • Compose UI enables `testTagsAsResourceId = true` (or equivalent semantics) so Modifier.testTag maps to AccessibilityNodeInfo resource-id. > • `adb shell uiautomator dump` exposes A11yTags values in resource-id attributes. ## Problem / goal In Jetpack Compose, `Modifier.testTag` sets the Compose semantics `TestTag` property, but Compose does not expose these tags to Android's `AccessibilityNodeInfo.viewIdResourceName` (which `uiautomator` inspects as `resource-id`) by default. As observed during smoke testing in #370, `adb shell uiautomator dump` returns empty `resource-id=""` for all Compose nodes despite `A11yTags` being applied across Android navigation, Home sections, favorites, and search in #364. Goal: Enable `testTagsAsResourceId = true` on the root Compose hierarchy in `MainActivity.kt` so that all descendants tagged with `Modifier.testTag(...)` map their tag values to `AccessibilityNodeInfo` `viewIdResourceName` / `resource-id`, and add a unit test in `A11yTagsTest.kt` ensuring semantics configuration sets `testTagsAsResourceId`. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt` Steps: - In `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt`:   - Import `androidx.compose.ui.ExperimentalComposeUiApi`, `androidx.compose.ui.semantics.semantics`, and `androidx.compose.ui.semantics.testTagsAsResourceId`.   - In `MainActivity.onCreate`'s `setContent` block, configure the root `Surface` modifier with `.semantics { @OptIn(ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class) testTagsAsResourceId = true }`. - In `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt`:   - Add a unit test verifying that `Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true }` sets `SemanticsProperties.TestTagsAsResourceId` to `true` in the Compose semantics configuration. - Run unit tests to confirm the suite passes:   `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests 'dev.mike.couchtour.A11yTagsTest'`   and the full `testDebugUnitTest` suite. Test: - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` ## Done when - [ ] `MainActivity.kt` enables `testTagsAsResourceId = true` on the root Compose tree via `Modifier.semantics`. - [ ] `A11yTagsTest.kt` includes a test verifying `testTagsAsResourceId` semantics configuration. - [ ] `testDebugUnitTest` passes: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. ## Needs a human to check - On a connected Android device or emulator with the app running: run `adb shell uiautomator dump /dev/stdout` (or `adb shell uiautomator dump && adb shell cat /sdcard/window_dump.xml`) and confirm that tagged Compose nodes (such as `nav.home`, `home.section.in-progress`) contain their tag values in `resource-id="..."` rather than `resource-id=""`. ## Context - #364 added `A11yTags` and tagged navigation items, Home sections, favorites, and search result sections using `Modifier.testTag(...)`. - In Android Compose UI, `testTagsAsResourceId` is an experimental API (`@ExperimentalComposeUiApi`) on `SemanticsPropertyReceiver`. When set on an ancestor node (such as the root `Surface`), Compose propagates it down the subtree and assigns `viewIdResourceName` on the corresponding `AccessibilityNodeInfo` objects exposed to accessibility services and UIAutomator. - Smoke testing runner (#370) consumes `uiautomator dump` XML for end-to-end journey assertions on Android. Populating `resource-id` allows deterministic node resolution matching the macOS smoke contract without relying on text/content-description fallbacks. ## Out of scope - Tagging additional surfaces or adding new constants to `A11yTags.kt` (already completed in #364). - The Google TV surface (`TvMainActivity.kt`, `TvBrowse.kt`, `TvNowPlaying.kt`), which does not use `A11yTags` or uiautomator smoke testing. - macOS accessibility identifiers (`AXIdentifiers.swift` / #365). - Modifying `scripts/smoke/run-android.sh` parser logic (#370).

column2: Android: Now Playing scrubber renders a fake 41% progress when track duration is unknown
column3: > **Original request:** Found during the Ledger redesign audit (#356). Leftover design-mockup data from the visual-fidelity reconcile commit 68d179a (D215, #134). ## Problem / goal In `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt:452-456`: ```kotlin val progressFraction = if (state.durationMs > 0) {     (state.positionMs.toFloat() / state.durationMs.toFloat()).coerceIn(0f, 1f) } else 0.41f ``` When track duration is unknown or buffering (`state.durationMs <= 0`), the scrubber progress fraction falls back to hardcoded `0.41f`. This causes `WaveformScrubber` to draw a fake 41% played gradient and needle cursor, misleading users into seeing active playback at ~41% on cold or buffering tracks. This was a design-mockup artifact introduced during the visual reconcile pass (commit `68d179a`, D215). At runtime, `durationMs == 0` is the default initial state in `PlayerViewModel.kt:40, 65` and occurs while ExoPlayer is buffering or before track metadata is resolved (cf. `TvNowPlaying.kt:55-57`). The goal is to eliminate this fake progress: when `durationMs <= 0`, progress fraction must be `0f`, suppressing the played gradient and needle until real playback progress exists, matching macOS (`ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:93` and `WaveformScrubber.swift:92`). ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LedgerLayoutTest.kt` - `README.md` - `UAT.md` Steps: - In `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt`:   - Replace the inlined `val progressFraction = if (state.durationMs > 0) ... else 0.41f` with a call to `progressFraction(state.positionMs, state.durationMs)` from `Format.kt` (which returns `0f` when `durationMs <= 0L` and clamps between `0f` and `1f`).   - In `WaveformScrubber`'s `onSeek` callback, guard seek execution with `if (state.durationMs > 0)` to prevent seeking against an unset/buffering duration. - In `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LedgerLayoutTest.kt`:   - Add unit tests verifying `progressFraction` returns `0f` when `durationMs` is 0 or negative, and never returns `0.41f`. - In `README.md`:   - Update the Android unit test count to reflect any new test cases. - In `UAT.md`:   - Add a manual check under a new UAT item for cold-launch / buffering Now Playing playback to confirm no 41% needle or progress flash appears before track duration resolves. Test: what proves it - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes. - `git grep "0.41f"` returns zero occurrences across the codebase. ## Done when - [ ] `0.41f` is removed from `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` and `git grep "0.41f"` returns no hits across the repository - [ ] `NowPlaying.kt` uses `progressFraction(state.positionMs, state.durationMs)` from `Format.kt` (returning `0f` when `durationMs <= 0`) - [ ] Scrubber seek in `NowPlaying.kt` is guarded so seeks do not fire when `state.durationMs <= 0` - [ ] Unit test in `LedgerLayoutTest.kt` verifies that unknown duration (`durationMs <= 0`) yields `0f` progress and not fake mockup progress - [ ] All Android unit tests pass: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` - [ ] Test count in `README.md` is updated to reflect new tests - [ ] `UAT.md` has an entry for owner verification of cold-launch Now Playing scrubber behavior - [ ] Branch pushed with `Fixes #385` in the commit/PR body ## Needs a human to check - Confirm on a real Android device that opening Now Playing during initial track buffer/load displays a clean, unplayed waveform with no needle flash at 41%. ## Context - Redesign reconcile commit `68d179a` (D215, #134) introduced `else 0.41f` in `NowPlaying.kt:454` alongside other mockup literals (such as the hardcoded "268" likes count resolved in #347). - macOS counterpart: `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:93` computes `let progressFrac = duration > 0 ? (currentPos / duration) : 0.0` and `WaveformScrubber.swift:92` renders the needle cursor only when `playedWidth > 0`. On Android, `DesignComponents.kt:292` also uses `if (playedWidth > 0f)` to render the needle, so returning `0f` naturally suppresses the needle and played gradient in parity with macOS. - Sibling issue #386 also touches `NowPlaying.kt` (artwork and header indicators); Mahler's `Files:` check serializes builds to prevent collision. ## Out of scope - Modifying `WaveformScrubber` vector waveform silhouette or amplitude drawing (`DesignComponents.kt`). - Restoring artwork or audio format chips in `NowPlaying.kt` (tracked separately in #386). - macOS player changes.

column2: Android: Ledger Now Playing dropped artwork, audio-format display, and the "Casting to …" indicator
column3: > **Original request:** Found during the Ledger redesign audit (#356) as a diff between pre-redesign `2a6b2cc^` and HEAD. Owner decision needed: these losses may be intentional Ledger design choices, but they are unrecorded and leave dead state. >  > ## What the redesign dropped from Android Now Playing (all confirmed absent at HEAD) >  > 1. Artwork. Pre-redesign showed `ArtworkBox` (artwork with the procedural vintage-cassette fallback for missing/failed art, `NowPlaying.kt:155-169`). HEAD renders no artwork image at all — `state.artUrl` is only passed into `AddToPlaylistButton`'s playlist ref (`NowPlaying.kt:512`). The procedural fallback in `Artwork.kt` still exists but is no longer used by this screen. The redesigned screen's dark hero is a fixed decorative gradient (hardcoded `0xFFD97706` / `0xFF991B1B` /radial accents at `NowPlaying.kt:100-151`) that bypasses `LocalLedgerColors` tokens. > 2. Audio format display. Pre-redesign showed `AudioQualityBadge(format: state.audioFormat, isFlac:)` (`NowPlaying.kt:230`). HEAD dropped the composable entirely (zero references app-wide); FLAC survives only via the lineage-chip fallback (`state.tapeLineage ?: "SBD · Soundboard"`) and a FLAC chip. `state.audioFormat` is now consumed only by the notification builder (`MainActivity.kt:4223-4225`). > 3. "Casting to " header indicator. Pre-redesign header title showed `"Casting to $castDevice"` while casting (`NowPlaying.kt:108`, collecting `Casting.deviceName` at `:68`). HEAD no longer collects `castDevice` at all; `CastButton` remains but there is no in-screen indication of what is being cast to. >  > ## Fix / decision >  > • If the drops are intentional: say so here (and in DECISIONS.md), then clean up — remove or repurpose the unused `artUrl` / `audioFormat` state paths, and reconsider the hardcoded gradient colors in favor of ledger tokens. > • If not: restore artwork (`ArtworkBox` still exists), surface `state.audioFormat` (the FLAC chip exists as a pattern), and restore the cast-device indicator. >  > Related: the macOS rail and expanded player both kept artwork (`ConicGlowArtwork`), so Android is the outlier between the two platforms. ## Problem / goal During the Ledger design overhaul (D214 / D215), Android Now Playing (`NowPlaying.kt`) was updated to match the Screen 1c/1D handoff mockup (`design/handoff/Couch Tour Android.dc.html`), which dropped: 1. Cover artwork tile and procedural vintage cassette fallback (`ShowArtwork`) from Android Now Playing (`NowPlaying.kt`). 2. Audio format display (`state.audioFormat`, e.g. MP3 vs FLAC; currently only FLAC is surfaced via a chip, MP3 is omitted). 3. "Casting to $castDevice" header indicator during active Google Cast sessions. 4. Left `state.artUrl` and `state.audioFormat` as unconsumed/dead state paths in `NowPlayingScreen`. Goal: Restore cover artwork (with procedural cassette fallback via `ShowArtwork`), audio format display (both MP3 and FLAC), and the active cast session device indicator in Android Now Playing while maintaining the Ledger design system styling, per owner decision. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LedgerLayoutTest.kt` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` - `UAT.md` Steps: - Restore artwork display in `NowPlaying.kt`:   - Integrate `ShowArtwork` with `artUrl = state.artUrl`, `artistName = state.artistName`, `date = state.showDate`, `venue = state.venueName`, and `contentDescription = state.trackTitle`.   - Place the artwork tile in the upper Now Playing layout with rounded corners (`RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)` or `16.dp`), adjusting the hero spacing/padding so the tile fits cleanly on standard mobile screens in both Dark and Light themes. - Restore audio format display:   - Surface `state.audioFormat` alongside tape lineage info. When FLAC, display the FLAC badge with amber accent (`ledger.ratingAmber`); when MP3 (or non-FLAC format), display the format badge with outline/muted styling (`ledger.controlOutline` / `ledger.textSecondary`) matching Ledger design tokens. - Restore Google Cast indicator:   - Collect `val castDevice by Casting.deviceName.collectAsState()` in `NowPlayingScreen`.   - In the top bar header, display `"Casting to $castDevice"` when `castDevice != null`, matching pre-redesign behavior and complementing the cast action button. - Record the architecture decision in `DECISIONS.md` using the next sequential D-number (allocated via `mahler next-id couch-tour D`), documenting the restoration of artwork and playback indicators within the Ledger design system. - Add unit tests in `LedgerLayoutTest.kt` verifying:   - Format badge text and styling logic for both FLAC and MP3 formats.   - Cast header display formatting logic when a cast device is connected vs null. - Update `README.md` test counts to reflect the new tests. - Update `UAT.md` with manual test steps for verifying visual layout on Android phone (light and dark mode) and cast status indication during active streaming. Test: - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` ## Done when - [ ] `NowPlaying.kt` renders `ShowArtwork` with remote artwork image and procedural cassette fallback. - [ ] `NowPlaying.kt` displays the audio format badge for both FLAC and MP3 formats. - [ ] `NowPlaying.kt` displays `"Casting to $castDevice"` in the top bar when an active cast session is connected. - [ ] Architectural decision is recorded in `DECISIONS.md` under an allocated sequential D-number. - [ ] Unit tests in `LedgerLayoutTest.kt` cover audio format formatting and cast header logic. - [ ] Test count in `README.md` is updated. - [ ] Manual verification items are added to `UAT.md`. - [ ] All Android unit tests pass: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. ## Needs a human to check - Visual balance and spacing of artwork tile and track details in both Dark and Light themes on a real phone screen or emulator. - Chromecast device name displays accurately in the Now Playing top bar during an active Cast session. ## Context - Pre-redesign baseline: commit `2a6b2cc^` (NowPlaying.kt had `ArtworkBox`, `"Casting to $castDevice"`, and `AudioQualityBadge`). - Redesign commits: `2a6b2cc` (#128, D214) and `68d179a` (D215, #134). - Design handoff spec: `design/handoff/Couch Tour Android.dc.html` Screen 1c/1D and `design/handoff/README.md`. - Parity: macOS expanded player / player rail use `ConicGlowArtwork`, and Google TV (`TvNowPlaying.kt`) uses `ShowArtwork`. - Owner decision: Confirmed in issue comment (`Restore artwork & indicators`). ## Out of scope - Scrubber 41% unknown-duration bug (resolved in #385). - macOS player layout or changes. - Mini-player artwork changes.

column2: macOS: ⌘F no longer focuses search, and clearing the query never closes the Search route
column3: > **Original request:** Found during the Ledger redesign audit (#356). Regression from the redesign commits (2a6b2cc / 28fa02c / 68d179a, D214/#133): both behaviors worked at `2a6b2cc^` and are broken at HEAD. ## Problem / goal Two pieces of search chrome wiring were lost when `RootView.swift` was deleted during the Ledger redesign (2a6b2cc / 28fa02c / 68d179a, D214/#133): 1. **⌘F does nothing:** `CouchTourApp.swift:55` (Find menu item) sets `appModel.focusSearchField = true` and `AppModel.swift:58` publishes it, but no view consumes the flag. Pre-redesign `RootView.swift:61-64` had an `.onChange(of: appModel.focusSearchField)` that set `searchFieldFocused = true` and reset the flag. `ThreePaneRootView.swift:15` declares `@FocusState private var searchFieldFocused: Bool` and line 136 attaches `.focused($searchFieldFocused)` to the toolbar field, but lacks the `.onChange` handler for `appModel.focusSearchField`. The comment in `CouchTourApp.swift:52-54` also carries stale claims. 2. **Clearing search query never closes the Search route:** Pre-redesign `RootView.syncSearchRoute()` popped `.search` off the navigation path when the query was cleared and `.search` was the top of the path (so drilling into a hit did not yank the user back upon clearing). HEAD `ThreePaneRootView.swift:79-85` only appends `.search` for non-empty queries and never removes it, leaving the user stranded on an empty Search view with stale count tabs when clearing the field. Goal: Restore ⌘F focusing the search field, restore `syncSearchRoute()` push/pop semantics in `ThreePaneRootView`, update the stale comment in `CouchTourApp.swift`, and document manual verification in `UAT.md`. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/ThreePaneRootView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/CouchTourApp.swift` - `UAT.md` Steps: - In `macos/CouchTour/ThreePaneRootView.swift`:   1. Add `.onChange(of: appModel.focusSearchField)` modifier that sets `searchFieldFocused = true` and resets `appModel.focusSearchField = false` when triggered, matching pre-redesign `RootView.swift`.   2. Implement `syncSearchRoute()` helper (or call it from `.onChange(of: appModel.searchQuery)`):      - When `term.count >= 3`, if `appModel.path.last != .search`, append `.search` to `appModel.path`.      - When `term.isEmpty` and `appModel.path.last == .search`, pop `.search` (`appModel.path.removeLast()`). - In `macos/CouchTour/CouchTourApp.swift`:   Update comment above Find menu item to remove stale "sidebar gone" wording and accurately describe `ThreePaneRootView` consuming `appModel.focusSearchField`. - In `UAT.md`:   Add a UAT entry under the Ledger redesign / macOS section verifying ⌘F focus and search route dismissal on query clear. Test: - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes. - `cd macos && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` compiles cleanly without errors. ## Done when - [ ] ⌘F keyboard shortcut sets `appModel.focusSearchField`, which `ThreePaneRootView` consumes to focus the toolbar search field and clear the flag. - [ ] Typing a query of ≥3 characters pushes `.search` onto `appModel.path` if not already on the Search route. - [ ] Clearing the search query (via clear button or backspacing) when `.search` is top of `appModel.path` pops `.search` and returns to the previous view. - [ ] Clearing the search query when drilled into a child destination (e.g. `.show`) does not pop the child view. - [ ] Comment in `CouchTourApp.swift` is updated and accurate. - [ ] `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes. - [ ] `cd macos && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` succeeds. - [ ] `UAT.md` contains a checkable item for ⌘F search focus and search dismissal. ## Needs a human to check - Launch CouchTour macOS app:   1. Press ⌘F from any screen; verify toolbar search field gains keyboard focus with blinking cursor.   2. Type a search term (≥3 chars); verify app navigates to Search route with results.   3. Click the "x" clear button or delete text; verify Search route closes and returns to the preceding screen.   4. From Search results, click into a show; clear the search query and verify the show detail screen remains active. ## Context - Regressed during the Ledger redesign in commits `2a6b2cc`, `28fa02c`, `68d179a` (D214 / #133) when `RootView.swift` was replaced by `ThreePaneRootView.swift`. - Baseline reference: `git show 2a6b2cc^:macos/CouchTour/RootView.swift` (lines 60-65 and 155-165). - `SearchView.swift:212` and `:269` requires ≥3 characters for search results. ## Out of scope - Any changes to search backend, ranking, or network fanout. - Changes to Android search behaviors. - Visual redesign of search results or filter chips.

column2: C: phish.in account content in the Library: playlists, liked shows, liked tracks (Android)
column3: > **Original request:** > > I have mostly favorited tracks but my library only displays shows, says 0 tracks. And looks more like history of shows I've played than things I've added to my library. History should be separated from library with different tracking and views. Part of #343 Depends on: #372 Depends on: #380 ## Problem / goal The owner's headline symptom is `Tracks 0` on a Library whose contents are mostly favorited tracks. After #B the Library shows only *local* saved things — local playlists, local playlist tracks, and `SavedShows`. It still shows none of what the owner actually saved, because **phish.in's likes are server-side and the client mirrors nothing.** The data all exists and is already fetched, one screen over. The phish.in account views sit behind Home → "Your phish.in account" (`MainActivity.kt:638-663`), reachable only when signed in, on three separate screens: - `mine/playlists` → `PlaylistsScreen` with `playlists(filter = "mine") + playlists(filter = "liked")`,   deduped by slug (D32), at `MainActivity.kt:300-306` - `mine/shows` → `MyShowsScreen`, `PhishInApi.likedShows()` (`MainActivity.kt:3615-3641`) - `mine/tracks` → `MyTracksScreen`, `PhishInApi.likedTracks()` (`MainActivity.kt:3643-3690`) That is the owner's own follow-up: *"The Library should surface them directly: account playlists under Playlists, liked shows under Shows, liked tracks under Tracks. That fixes both this report and the original 'Tracks 0'."* The Library should be the one place you go to see what you saved, not a place you have to remember is behind a Home row that only exists when you happen to be signed in. This issue folds those three sources into the Library's existing three tabs, plus the Relisten liked tracks that #372 has just made listable. Design decision, recorded rather than asked: **fetch live, mirror nothing.** phish.in returns no like timestamp, no like id, and no incremental feed — so a Room mirror would be a snapshot with invented metadata and a migration to maintain, in exchange for nothing the API does not already give. The app already fetches all three lists on demand (`Api.kt:287,326,336`) and discards them on exit via `loadOnce` (`MainActivity.kt:4537-4542`). Reuse that shape, fetch once per Library entry, and keep the local sources local. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibrarySources.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibraryScreen.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibraryAccountTest.kt` (new) - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: - In `LibrarySources.kt` (created by #B — extend it, do not re-open the screen for this), add the   account half of the model:   - `data class LibraryAccountData(val playlists: List<Playlist>, val shows: List<Show>, val tracks: List<Track>, val loaded: Boolean)`   - `suspend fun loadLibraryAccount(): LibraryAccountData` — **only** when     `Session.username.value != null`. When signed out, return `loaded = true` with three empty     lists and let the screen say so. Never call `playlists(filter = …)` unauthenticated: the API     silently ignores the filter and returns all 2,504 public playlists (D26, documented at     `Api.kt:282-286`). This gate is the whole reason the function is safe to write this way.   - `fun accountPlaylistItems(account: List<Playlist>): List<LibraryItem>` — the `mine` + `liked`     merge and `distinctBy { it.slug }` from D32, title `name`, subtitle     `"phish.in · $tracksCount tracks"`, target `LibraryTarget.Playlist(slug)`,     `addedAt = null`.   - `fun accountShowItems(account: List<Show>): List<LibraryItem>` — title `formatShowDate(date)`,     subtitle `venueName · location` (omit the parts that are null), target     `LibraryTarget.Show(date)`, `addedAt = null`. `likedShows()` already arrives `sort=date:desc`     (`Api.kt:331`).   - `fun accountTrackItems(account: List<Track>): List<LibraryItem>` — title `title`, subtitle     `showDate · venueName · venueLocation` minus nulls (the shape `MyTracksScreen` already     renders at `MainActivity.kt:3668-3671`), trailing `fmt(duration)`, `addedAt = null`.   - `fun relistenLikedTrackItems(entries: List<LikedTrackRef>): List<LibraryItem>` — same row     shape, subtitle from the ref's `artistName` / `showDate` / `venueName`, target     `LibraryTarget.Recording`. Read from `LikedTracks.entries` (#372), newest `likedAt` first —     this is the one source with a real timestamp, and it should carry `addedAt = ref.likedAt`.   Every account item gets `addedAt = null`: the API returns no like time. The #B sort helper   already sorts null-`addedAt` last, so local saves and Relisten likes lead and account items   follow in the order phish.in returned them. Say so in `DECISIONS.md` — it is the reason a   "Recently added" Library is not strictly chronological across backends, and the next person to   look will otherwise assume a bug. - Dedupe. A show can be both locally saved and phish.in-liked, and a track can be liked through   both `LikedTracks` and a phish.in account. Dedupe **after** the merge, on the target, keeping   the dated item (so the row keeps a real `addedAt` and a real sort position): one Shows row per   date, one Tracks row per `(backend, trackId)`, one Playlists row per slug — local and account   playlists can never collide since one is a uuid and the other a slug, so they simply coexist. - In `LibraryScreen.kt`: hold the account data in a `produceState` keyed on   `Session.username.collectAsState()` (signing in or out re-runs the fetch — `Session.logout()`   sets the flow to `null`, `Auth.kt:109-114`) that calls `loadLibraryAccount()`. Fold the three   account item lists into the same three `remember` blocks that build `filteredPlaylists` /   `filteredShows` / `filteredTracks`, so the chip counts (`LibraryScreen.kt:127-130`) and the   visible rows can never disagree. On a network failure, keep the local items on screen and add   a single line above the list — do not blank the Library, and do not navigate away. - Row taps, matching what each source already does elsewhere in the app:   - account playlist → `nav.navigate("playlist/${slug}")` (same as `PlaylistsScreen`)   - account show → `nav.navigate("show/${date}")` (same as `MyShowsScreen`)   - account track → `vm.playTrack(track)`, so one tap plays the liked track inside its show.     This is `MyTracksScreen`'s behaviour (`MainActivity.kt:3683`) and is the least surprising     thing for a row labelled "track". The subtitle carries the date and venue, so it is obvious     what is about to play. Do **not** add a per-row like/unlike button: unliking belongs on the     show page, and the row is a list entry, not a control.   - Relisten liked track → the same "tap plays" behaviour is *not* available here; open the     recording via `openQueueKey(recordingQueueKey(artistSlug, showDate, recordingId))`, the same     key the show page builds. When the ref's `recordingId` is null (#372 writes null for shuffle     and local-playlist queues) fall back to `LibraryTarget.Show(showDate)` rather than     constructing a key that cannot play. - Badge the source. The fixed-width 44dp type badges stay `LIST` / `SHOW` / `TRACK` (D214,   uat-checked widths). Put the backend in the subtitle instead — `phish.in · 42 tracks`,   `Grateful Dead · 1977-05-08 · Cow Palace` — so a local and an account row are distinguishable   without inventing a fifth badge. - Signed-out Library still works: local playlists, local playlist tracks and `SavedShows` all   render with no token, and under the chips show one line — "Sign in to phish.in to see your liked   shows, tracks and playlists" — which navigates to the account screen. Signed in with nothing   liked yet, keep the existing per-tab empty states from #B; do not show the sign-in line. - `DECISIONS.md`: new entry via `mahler next-id couch-tour D` recording (a) the Library is the one   place saved items live, merging local and phish.in-account sources; (b) account likes are   fetched live and not mirrored, and why (no like timestamp or id in the API, so a mirror would   be a snapshot with invented metadata); (c) a null `addedAt` sorts last under "Recently added",   so account items are grouped last rather than interleaved by a guess. - `README.md`: update the test count. The bullets "Log in to your phish.in account to see your   liked shows, liked tracks, and playlists" and "A History screen lists everything you've played"   already read correctly — add that the Library lists saved items across both backends. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. `LibraryAccountTest.kt` is a plain JVM test over the pure merge functions (same style as `LedgerLayoutTest.kt`): `loadLibraryAccount` with no username performs **zero** requests and returns three empty lists (this is the D26 guard — assert it, it is the one way this feature can leak 2,504 rows into someone's Library); the playlist merge dedupes a slug present in both `mine` and `liked`; a show saved locally *and* liked on phish.in produces one row, keeping the dated `addedAt`; a track liked on both backends produces one row per `(backend, trackId)`; a null-`addedAt` account row sorts after a dated local row under `RECENTLY_ADDED` but is still reached by `TITLE_ASC`; and every `LibraryItem` produced from a `Show`/`Track`/`Playlist` carries a non-blank title that does not start with a queue prefix. If a network-shaped case needs `MockWebServer`, follow `ApiRequestTest.kt`; the merges themselves must not need it. ## Done when - [ ] Signed in, with the owner's account: Library chips read like `All N · Playlists P · Shows S       · Tracks T` with **T > 0**, and every liked track appears under Tracks. `Tracks 0` on a       populated account is gone. - [ ] Your phish.in playlists (created *and* liked, deduped by slug) appear under Playlists;       liked shows under Shows; liked tracks under Tracks. Opening each navigates to the right       place, and tapping a liked track plays it in its show. - [ ] Relisten liked tracks (from `LikedTracks.entries`, #372) appear under Tracks alongside the       phish.in ones, newest-liked first, with title/date/venue filled in. - [ ] A show that is both locally saved and phish.in-liked shows as exactly one row, not two. - [ ] Signed out: no account request is made, every local source still renders, the counts match       the local items only, and the sign-in line appears. Sign in while the app is running and       the Library refetches without a restart; sign out and it drops back. - [ ] The Library's Shows tab still contains nothing that was merely played — #B's separation       from History is not regressed. - [ ] Every Library row has a real title. No row renders `relisten:…`, `show:…`, `playlist:…`,       `local-playlist:…` or `youtube:…`. - [ ] Search, the four chips, the sort dropdown and the counts still agree with each other over       the merged lists. - [ ] A failed account fetch leaves the local Library usable and shows one error line; it does       not show an empty Library. - [ ] No Room migration and no schema JSON change: `PhishInDb` version is still 14 and       `Progress.kt` is untouched. - [ ] `Api.kt`, `Sync.kt` and `sync/` are untouched — no new endpoint, no wire-format change. - [ ] `LibraryAccountTest.kt` passes, the full `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green, and       `README.md`'s test count matches. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new `Dnnn` entry (id from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`). ## Needs a human to check - Sign into phish.in on the device, open Library, and confirm Tracks / Shows / Playlists match   what you see under Home → Your phish.in account. The owner reported "mostly favorited tracks",   so Tracks is the one to check first. - Tap a liked track row and confirm it plays the right track in the right show. - Sign out and back in and confirm the Library updates each way without a restart. - Open the Library on cellular with a weak signal and confirm the local items still render. ## Context - All three endpoints already exist and are already covered for request shape by   `ApiRequestTest.kt:298-305,368-388`; this issue consumes them, it does not add them. - `Session.username` is a `StateFlow` (`Auth.kt:88-89`) — that is the reactive key, not a   re-read of `PhishInApi.authToken`. - D26 is the hazard: an unauthenticated `filter=mine` returns every public playlist rather than   erroring. Gate on the username, not on "the fetch succeeded". - D32 (`mine` + `liked`, deduped by slug) is the existing precedent for what "my playlists"   means; copy it rather than re-deriving. - `MyTracksScreen` and `MyShowsScreen` stay exactly as they are — they remain reachable from   Home and are not deprecated by this. `MainActivity.kt:4298` already marks those routes as part   of the Library tab, so tab selection survives navigating in and back out. - #380 created `LibrarySources.kt` and moved the screen's data model into it; #372 created the   `LikedTrackRef` records this issue reads. Both land first. ## Out of scope - Deleting or deprecating My shows / My tracks / My playlists screens. They keep working. - Syncing likes, playlists or favorites across devices. `sync/` moves playback progress only;   server-side likes already follow the account, and local stores are another question. - A Room table mirroring phish.in likes, and a `MIGRATION_14_15`. - Relisten *shows* you liked — Relisten has no like API, and `SavedShows` (phish.in dates plus   recording keys) is the whole of that story today. - The macOS Library. `macos/CouchTour/LocalPlaylistsView.swift` has the same local-only behaviour   and its own account view in `AccountView.swift`; a separate macOS parity issue covers it. - Removing the "Your phish.in account" Home section.

column2: B: Library lists saved things, not what you played (Android)
column3: > **Original request:** > > I have mostly favorited tracks but my library only displays shows, says 0 tracks. And looks more like history of shows I've played than things I've added to my library. History should be separated from library with different tracking and views. Part of #343 Depends on: #372 ## Problem / goal `LibraryScreen.kt` reads three local sources (`LibraryScreen.kt:85-87`): - `localPlaylistDao.playlists()` — local playlists, correct - `progressDao.inProgress()` — **this is the bug** - `localPlaylistDao.allTracks()` — local playlist tracks, correct `inProgress()` is the `progress` table, i.e. the playback ledger, filtered to unfinished rows and capped at 25. So the Library's "Shows" tab is a Continue-Listening list wearing a Library label — which is exactly the owner's complaint, "looks more like history of shows I've played than things I've added to my library." History is already its own screen (`HistoryScreen`, `MainActivity.kt:3970-4015`, `composable("history")` at `MainActivity.kt:223`, reachable from the Home "Continue listening" header and count chip at `MainActivity.kt:405,426`). The separation the owner asked for is a one-line source change: the Library stops reading the playback ledger. This piece fixes the **local** half only. phish.in account content (liked shows/tracks, your playlists) lands in #381, and Relisten liked tracks need the record store from #372 first. Three consequences to handle in the same change: 1. **The Shows tab needs a real source.** With `inProgress()` gone, the tab is fed by    `SavedShows.keys` — Android's own bookmark store (`SavedShows.kt`, written from the show    pages at `MainActivity.kt:1144,1738`). It stays a `Set<String>` of show keys, no record    change: a row only needs a date, and tapping it opens the show page, which loads everything    else. (This deliberately departs from #372's Context, which floated giving `SavedShows` the    same record treatment as `LikedTracks`; that is not needed to render a row and would grow the    change for nothing.) 2. **The raw-ID-as-title bug.** `LibraryScreen.kt:342` does    `item.queueKey.removePrefix("show:").removePrefix("recording:relisten:")`. The real prefix    constant is `RECORDING_PREFIX = "relisten:"` (`Queue.kt:97`), not `"recording:relisten:"`, so    for a Relisten key both removals are no-ops, `formatShowDate` cannot parse the string and    returns it verbatim (`Format.kt:94`) — the row title becomes    `relisten:grateful-dead/1977-05-08/abcd-…`. `playlist:`, `local-playlist:` and `youtube:`    keys fail the same way. `SavedShows` stores exactly those kinds of keys, so parsing is now    required, not optional. Use `parseQueueKey` (`Queue.kt:53`) / `parseRecordingId` (`Queue.kt:87`)    — never string surgery on prefixes. A key that does not parse is **dropped from the list**,    not rendered as a title. 3. **The row actions are for the wrong screen.** The SHOW rows' long-press menu    (`LibraryScreen.kt:355-400`) is Resume playback / Open / Mark completed / Remove from In    Progress / Delete from history — every one of them a `Progress` mutation, i.e. the ledger    controls that moved out. They go, replaced by Open show and Remove from Library    (`SavedShows.toggle`). The `N:NN elapsed` trailing text (`LibraryScreen.kt:344`) goes with    them: a saved show has no position. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibrarySources.kt` (new) - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibraryScreen.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibrarySourcesTest.kt` (new) - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: - Create `LibrarySources.kt` as the pure, testable seam the whole Library data model moves into.   It is pure functions only — no Composable, no DAO, no Context — so #381 can extend it without   touching the screen again. Start it with:   - `data class LibraryItem(val key: String, val badge: String, val title: String, val subtitle: String, val addedAt: Long?, val sortKey: String, val onOpen: ...)`.     Keep the navigation target out of the model: return a sealed `LibraryTarget`     (`LocalPlaylist(id)`, `Show(date)`, `Recording(RecordingId)`) and let `LibraryScreen` turn it     into a `nav.navigate` / `openQueueKey` call. That keeps the merge functions free of     `NavHostController` and unit-testable.   - `fun savedShowItems(keys: Set<String>): List<LibraryItem>` — parse each key with     `parseQueueKey`/`parseRecordingId`; `QueueKind.SHOW` → the date; `QueueKind.RECORDING` →     `RecordingId.date`; anything else, or a key that fails to parse, is dropped. Title is     `formatShowDate(date)`, subtitle `"Saved show"`, `addedAt = null` (`SavedShows` carries no     timestamp and adding one is not worth a schema change for a bookmark set). Sort by date     descending.   - `fun playlistItems(local: List<LocalPlaylistEntity>): List<LibraryItem>` — wrap what     `LibraryScreen.kt:321-336` already renders, with `addedAt = it.updatedAt`.   - `fun trackItems(local: List<LocalPlaylistTrackEntity>): List<LibraryItem>` — wrap what     `LibraryScreen.kt:406-419` renders, `addedAt = null`, ordered by `rowId` descending (which is     what `LocalPlaylistDao.allTracks()` already returns and what the current code sorts on —     `LocalPlaylistTrackEntity` has no timestamp column, and adding one means a Room migration     for a sort nobody complained about). `sortKey` is the title so the A–Z modes still work. - In `LibraryScreen.kt`: delete the `progressDao.inProgress()` collection and the whole   `rawInProgressList` → `filteredShows` → "Shows from in-progress history" block. Feed   `filteredShows` from `SavedShows.keys.collectAsState()` (init'd in `CouchTourApp.kt:18`) run   through `savedShowItems`. Counts (`LibraryScreen.kt:127-130`) are unchanged in shape — they   are derived from the filtered lists, so they follow automatically. - Sorting: one `when (sortMode)` helper over `LibraryItem` instead of three duplicated blocks   (`LibraryScreen.kt:92-125`) — `RECENTLY_ADDED` puts items with a non-null `addedAt` first,   descending, then the rest in the order the source produced them; `TITLE_ASC`/`TITLE_DESC` sort   on `sortKey`. Null-last is the honest answer for sources with no timestamp, and it is   deterministic — write it down in `DECISIONS.md`. - Show rows: title `formatShowDate(date)`, subtitle `Saved show`, no trailing elapsed text, tap →   the show (`openQueueKey` for a recording key, `nav.navigate("show/$date")` for a phish.in   date). Long-press menu becomes two items: Open show, Remove from Library   (`SavedShows.toggle(key)`). - Empty states per tab, and they must be honest (D227): a tab with no saved items says what to   do — "Like a show to save it here", "Save a show from its page", "Create a playlist". When the   Shows tab is empty *and* `progressDao.historyCount() > 0`, add one line under the chips:   "Shows you've played are in History" with a tap through to `nav.navigate("history")`. That is   the visible half of the separation the owner asked for. - `MainActivity.kt`, `HistoryScreen` (`:3970-4015`): the rows already use the denormalized   `Progress.title`, which `PlaybackService.saveNow()` populates (`PlaybackService.kt:428`) — so   the Library's raw-key bug does not bite here. Still, the owner's acceptance says *no Library or   History row* shows an internal id: add a small guard so a `title` that is blank **or** starts   with a known queue prefix (`show:`, `relisten:`, `playlist:`, `local-playlist:`, `youtube:`)   falls back to the date parsed out of `queueKey` via `parseQueueKey`, and a key that will not   parse falls back to `"Removed show"`. Do not change `formatShowDate` itself — it is used   elsewhere and its raw-passthrough is correct for that use. - `DECISIONS.md`: new entry via `mahler next-id couch-tour D` recording (a) Library is the   saved-items view and the playback ledger is History, superseding the "Library shows" reading   that D214/D215/D220 built; (b) null `addedAt` sorts last under "Recently added"; (c)   unparseable saved keys are dropped rather than rendered. Note it revises D220's "Library   bookmark parity" uat item. - `README.md`: update the test count and the Library/History bullet ("A History screen lists   everything you've played" is already correct; add that Library lists saved items). Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. `LibrarySourcesTest.kt` is a plain JVM test in the style of `LedgerLayoutTest.kt` / `QueueTest.kt` (no Robolectric needed — the functions are pure): `savedShowItems` on `show:1997-11-17` yields that date as a `YYYY-MM-DD` title; on `relisten:grateful-dead/1977-05-08/abc-123` yields `1977-05-08` and **not** the raw key; on `playlist:foo`, `local-playlist:abc` and garbage, the recording-shape cases drop or parse without ever producing a title containing `relisten:`; `playlistItems` sorts newest `updatedAt` first; `trackItems` preserves `rowId` order; and the shared sort helper puts a null-`addedAt` item after a dated one under `RECENTLY_ADDED` while `TITLE_ASC` ignores the timestamps entirely. ## Done when - [ ] The Library "Shows" tab no longer reads `progressDao.inProgress()`; a show that has been       played but not saved appears in History (and the Home Continue listening shelf) and **not**       in Library. - [ ] A show saved with `SavedShows` appears under Library → Shows with a `YYYY-MM-DD` title and       opens that show on tap; un-saving it (long-press → Remove from Library) removes the row. - [ ] No row in Library or History ever renders `relisten:…`, `show:…`, `playlist:…`,       `local-playlist:…` or `youtube:…` as a title. Grep the diff for `removePrefix` on a queue       key — there should be none left in `LibraryScreen.kt`. - [ ] The "Shows you have played are in History" line appears when the Shows tab is empty and       history is not, and tapping it navigates to History. - [ ] The in-progress long-press menu (Resume / Mark completed / Remove from In Progress /       Delete from history) is gone from Library rows and nothing in `LibraryScreen.kt` calls       `vm.resume` / `vm.dismiss` / `vm.forget` / `vm.markCompleted` any more. - [ ] A show row carries no `N:NN elapsed` trailing text. - [ ] Library search, all four chips, the sort dropdown and the counts still work over the new       sources (the counts are derived from the filtered lists, so they must track the search       box exactly as they do today). - [ ] `SavedShows` and the `PhishInDb` schema are unchanged — no Room migration, no schema JSON       churn (per AGENTS.md, destructive migrations are never permitted and none is wanted here). - [ ] `LibrarySourcesTest.kt` passes, the full `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green, and       `README.md`'s test count matches. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new `Dnnn` entry (id from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`). ## Needs a human to check - Open Library on the real device and confirm it no longer looks like your listening history:   play a show, never save it, and it should not be in Library. Check it *is* in History and on   the home Continue listening shelf. - Save a show from its page, then confirm the row and the count in Library → Shows, and that   the title reads as a date rather than an id. ## Context - `MainActivity.kt:4298` already folds the `mine/shows`, `mine/tracks`, `mine/playlists` and   `local-playlists` routes into the Library tab's selected set, so the account screens keep their   highlight when you come back. #381 builds on that. - `SavedShows` is initialized in `CouchTourApp.kt:18` and has two writers, both passing a bare   date (`MainActivity.kt:1144`, `:1738`). A Relisten show page saving a recording key is a   possibility to tolerate, not one to assume — hence the defensive parse. - D229 removed Save in favour of Likes on **macOS**; Android's `SavedShows` was kept as   deliberate deferred work. This issue is that deferred work, on the Android Library only. - #381 owns everything phish.in-account-shaped. Do not add a network call to this issue. - #372 (`LikedTracks` record store) is a prerequisite in the file sense too — it also edits   `MainActivity.kt`, `DECISIONS.md` and `README.md`. ## Out of scope - phish.in liked shows/tracks and your playlists in the Library — #381. - Relisten liked tracks in the Library — blocked on #372 and shipped with #381. - Changing `SavedShows` to a record store; keys stay, the row just parses them. - The macOS Library (`macos/CouchTour/LocalPlaylistsView.swift` has the same local-only   behaviour — it does *not* have the raw-key bug, because it reads the denormalized title). A   separate macOS issue covers parity; this one is Android-only. - Sync. `sync/` stores playback progress only; saved items are device-local or upstream on   phish.in, and mirroring likes across devices is its own problem.

column2: Jam chart note shows placeholder text on macOS (real notes + source link)
