column3: > **Original request:** Jam chart badge/note is placeholder text — no real notes or source link (Android + macOS). ## Problem / goal On macOS the Jam Chart badge is correctly tag-driven (`isJamChart` in `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:260`, `PlayerRailView.swift:220`, `ShowDetailView.swift:631`), but the note card still shows the hardcoded `"Jam chart entry available for this track."` (`ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:302`, `PlayerRailView.swift:262`), `showJamChartNote` defaults to `true` (`ExpandedNowPlayingView:16`, `PlayerRailView:14`) instead of collapsed (design/handoff/README.md:75), and there is no source link. Real notes already survive: phish.in's `tags[].notes` decodes onto `Tag.notes` (`CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift:72`) and survives into `PlayableTrack.tags`, pinned by `TagTests.swift:91`. The only missing data is the track `slug`: the phish.in `Track` DTO has no `slug` field (`PhishInAPI.swift:134-152`) and `PlayableTrack` (`Catalog.swift:521-543`) has no slug, so the per-track source URL `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` (owner-confirmed #355) cannot be built on macOS today. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PhishInAPI.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlayerRailView.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/PhishInParsingTests.swift` Steps: 1. Add `slug: String?` to the phish.in `Track` DTO in `PhishInAPI.swift` (stored property,    `CodingKeys` case, and `init`). The show.json fixture already carries `"slug"` on tracks. 2. Add `slug: String?` to `PlayableTrack` (and its `init`) in `CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift`, and    populate it in the `Track` -> `PlayableTrack` mapping so it reaches `Player.currentTrack`    (`Player.swift:123`). 3. Add `trackSourceUrl(date: String, slug: String) -> String` returning    `https://phish.in/$date/$slug` in `CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift`. 4. In `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` and `PlayerRailView.swift`: read the jam-chart tag's `notes`    from `player.currentTrack?.tags`, feed it into `JamChartNoteCard(note:)` (replacing the    placeholder), hide the card when notes are blank, set `showJamChartNote = false` by default, and    add a "View on phish.in" link beside the card that opens `trackSourceUrl(date:slug:)` via    `NSWorkspace.shared.open` (mirrors `ExternalLinkButton.swift:58-63`). 5. Extend `PhishInParsingTests` to assert `Track` decodes `slug`. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` — slug decoding + URL builder assertions pass and existing Tag/Catalog tests have no regressions. ## Done when - [ ] The note card shows the jam-chart tag's real `notes` (not the placeholder sentence). - [ ] The card is hidden when the jam-chart tag has no notes. - [ ] `showJamChartNote` defaults to `false` (collapsed). - [ ] A "View on phish.in" link opens `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>`. - [ ] `PhishInParsingTests` asserts `Track.slug` decodes from the fixture. ## Needs a human to check - Expanded Now Playing + mini rail show real jam-chart notes and a working source link on macOS. ## Context - Part of #355. Source destination decided by the owner: the phish.in per-track page   `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` (#355). - Source-link open pattern follows `ExternalLinkButton`'s `NSWorkspace.shared.open`   (`DesignSystem/ExternalLinkButton.swift:58-63`) and `FeedbackButton`'s open call. - No macOS share-URL builder exists today; this adds one alongside track playback. ## Out of scope - A Relisten per-track source link (Relisten has no per-track page). - Changes to Show Detail's existing tag badge (already tag-driven and correct). Part of #355

column2: Jam chart note shows placeholder text on Android (real notes + source link)
column3: > **Original request:** Jam chart badge/note is placeholder text — no real notes or source link (Android + macOS). ## Problem / goal On Android the Jam Chart badge and note card are placeholders that never bind to real data: - `NowPlaying.kt:396` gates the JAM CHART badge on `state.backend == Backend.PHISHIN.id ||   state.backend == null`, so the badge renders on **every** phish.in track, not just tagged ones. - `NowPlaying.kt:443-448` renders `JamChartNoteCard(noteText = "Notable version from phish.in   archive records.")` — a fixed sentence, not the tag's `notes`. - `showJamChartNote` defaults to `true` (`NowPlaying.kt:75`) instead of collapsed   (design/handoff/README.md:75). - No source link exists at all. The real data is decoded upstream but dropped on the way to the player: - `Tag.notes` is present (`Api.kt:45`) but `Tag.toTagRef()` (`Catalog.kt:53`) discards it because   `TagRef` (`Catalog.kt:23-28`) has no `notes` field. - `Track.slug` is present (`Api.kt:87`) but `Track.toPlayableTrack()` (`Catalog.kt:715-728`)   discards it — `PlayableTrack` (`Catalog.kt:300-318`) has no slug. - `PlayerState` (`PlayerViewModel.kt:22-58`) carries no jam-tag info, and `mediaItemExtras`   (`MediaItems.kt:240-281`) plus `Keys` (`PlaybackService.kt:39-65`) carry neither notes nor slug, so   nothing can reach `NowPlayingScreen`. `trackShareUrl` (`Catalog.kt:760-764`) already builds the correct `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` per-track page (owner-confirmed #355), so it is reused for the card's source link rather than introducing a second URL builder. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlayerViewModel.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MediaItems.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlaybackService.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CatalogTest.kt` Steps: 1. Add `notes: String?` to `TagRef` and set it in `Tag.toTagRef()` (`Catalog.kt`), so the jam tag's    notes survive the API -> model mapping. 2. Add `slug: String?` to `PlayableTrack` and set it in `Track.toPlayableTrack()` (`Catalog.kt`). 3. Add `Keys.TRACK_SLUG` and `Keys.JAM_CHART_NOTES` (and register in `Keys.ALL`) in    `PlaybackService.kt`. 4. Thread `slug` + jam-chart tag `notes` through `coreMediaItem` + `mediaItemExtras` in    `MediaItems.kt` (derive the jam tag's notes from `PlayableTrack.tags`). 5. Add `trackSlug: String?` and `jamChartNotes: String?` to `PlayerState` in `PlayerViewModel.kt`;    populate both from the MediaItem extras bundle. 6. In `NowPlaying.kt`: gate the badge on `state.jamChartNotes != null` (a real jam-chart tag with    notes), feed `state.jamChartNotes` into `JamChartNoteCard`, hide the card when notes are blank, set    `showJamChartNote = false` by default, and add a source link built via `trackShareUrl`. 7. Extend `CatalogTest` to assert `toTagRef` carries `notes`, `toPlayableTrack` carries `slug`, and    `trackShareUrl` builds `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` for `Backend.PHISHIN`. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` — new `CatalogTest` assertions pass and no existing tests regress. ## Done when - [ ] The JAM CHART badge in Now Playing shows only for phish.in tracks carrying a Jam Chart tag,       not every phish.in track. - [ ] The note card renders the tag's real `notes` (verified against the show.json fixture note at       `fixtures/show.json:66`). - [ ] The card is hidden when the jam-chart tag has no notes. - [ ] `showJamChartNote` defaults to `false` (collapsed). - [ ] A source link opens `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` via `trackShareUrl`. - [ ] `CatalogTest` covers notes/slug plumbing and the source URL builder. ## Needs a human to check - Now Playing shows the badge only on jam-charted tracks and displays the real phish.in note text. - Collapsing/expanding the card works and the source link opens the per-track phish.in page. ## Context - Part of #355 (jam chart badge/note placeholders, Android + macOS). Source destination decided by   the owner: the phish.in per-track page `https://phish.in/<date>/<slug>` (#355). - Badge gating reuses the tag-name predicate already used in `MainActivity.kt:4072`. - `NowPlayingScreen` cannot be constructed under Robolectric today, so coverage lives in `CatalogTest`   (pure functions); `ArtistScreenTest.kt:30-60` is the Compose + MockWebServer pattern to copy if UI   coverage is later needed. ## Out of scope - Extracting an isolated `JamChartSection` composable for Robolectric Now Playing UI tests. - Relayout/theming of the card. Part of #355

column2: E: Feedback copies the diagnostics tail and prefills a summary (Include diagnostics, on by default)
column3: > **Original request:** > > Feedback includes diagnostics. The Feedback flow offers "Include diagnostics" (on by default). Because a GitHub URL can't carry a large body, share or copy the last ~200 lines as a text file the owner can attach, and put a short summary in the prefilled body (last crash, last sync result, library counts). Part of #344 Depends on: #373, #374, #375 Needs from #375: the `mark`ed values this issue quotes (library counts, last sync). From #374: the last-crash summary. From #373: `summaryLines` and `exportText`. The Settings viewer is independent of this one. ## Problem / goal `launchFeedback` (FeedbackButton.kt:21) opens a prefilled GitHub issue with version, screen route and device. That is the whole handover. The owner's request was explicit: press Feedback, and the resulting issue should already carry the evidence. Goal: on pressing Feedback, the app copies the recent diagnostics tail to the clipboard and puts a short summary in the prefilled issue body, with an "Include diagnostics" setting that is on by default. Design decisions (made here, recorded in DECISIONS.md): - **A GitHub URL cannot carry 200 lines.** The prefilled `body` gets only the short summary from `DiagnosticsLog.summaryLines()` — a few hundred characters. The full 200-line tail goes to the **clipboard**, and the prefilled body tells the owner to paste it. This is the "share or copy" the owner asked for, and it works on any device without a `FileProvider`. - **The clipboard write is the useful part, so it is loud**: show a Toast/Snackbar saying diagnostics were copied. - **The setting is per-install, in `SharedPreferences`, defaulting to on**, matching how `PlaybackSettings`, `ThemeSettings`, `Favorites`, `LikedTracks` and `SavedShows` already store their flags. It is a plain `object` with a `StateFlow`, not a Room table. - **"Include diagnostics" off means total silence**: no clipboard write, no summary section, no toast. The owner may be reporting something unrelated to a bug and does not want their log pasted anywhere. - Keep the existing env block (version, route, device, OS) exactly as it is — `bug_report.md` and the #295 template-name fix depend on that URL shape. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/FeedbackButton.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SettingsScreen.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/FeedbackDiagnosticsTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: - `FeedbackButton.kt`:   - Extract the body construction into a testable function, e.g. `fun buildFeedbackBody(routeName: String?, includeDiagnostics: Boolean, summary: String): String`. Keep the `## Environment` block byte-identical to today so the existing URL behaviour does not regress.   - When diagnostics are included, append a `## Diagnostics` section to the body: the `summaryLines()` text (last crash, last sync result, library counts, entry count, on-disk size) and a line telling the owner the full tail is on the clipboard and to paste it under a `## Log` heading.   - In `launchFeedback(context, routeName)`: read the toggle, and when on, read the summary and the 200-line tail **off the main thread** before building the URL, put the tail on the clipboard via `ClipboardManager`, and show a Toast. Then open the same `https://github.com/mkny13/couch-tour/issues/new?template=bug_report.md&…` intent as today.   - Since `launchFeedback` is called from three places — `FeedbackButton` (used in `SettingsScreen.kt:90-95`, `LibraryScreen.kt:162-167` and `MainActivity.kt:4170-4178`) — do the clipboard work in one place, inside `launchFeedback`, so all three callers get it. Do not duplicate it per call site.   - Guard the URL length: the summary must stay short (cap it at ~1000 characters; truncate older lines if a pathological log makes it longer). A URL past a few thousand characters gets truncated or rejected by the browser. - `SettingsScreen.kt`: add a `SettingsToggleRow(label = "Include diagnostics", checked = …, onCheckedChange = …)` in the ABOUT block (next to the row #376 adds), with `help = "Copies the recent app log to your clipboard and adds a summary to Feedback issues. Stays on this device."`. - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`; record the summary-vs-clipboard split and the default-on choice. - Bump the test count in README.md. Test: `FeedbackDiagnosticsTest` (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [34])`). - With the toggle on, `buildFeedbackBody` contains the `## Environment` block unchanged *and* a `## Diagnostics` section carrying the last crash, the last sync result and the library counts from seeded `mark`ed values. - With the toggle off, the body is byte-identical to today's output and the clipboard is untouched. - The summary is truncated at the cap and the resulting URL stays under a sane length. - A seeded log with a line that looks like a credential does not put that line in the URL body (the clipboard copy keeps the raw text; the summary does not). - The toggle round-trips through `SharedPreferences` and defaults to on for a fresh install. - The three call sites all go through `launchFeedback`, so the clipboard write is not duplicated. ## Done when - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green with the new tests. - [ ] Pressing Feedback anywhere in the app copies the diagnostics tail to the clipboard and opens the same prefilled issue URL as before. - [ ] The prefilled body gains a short `## Diagnostics` section with last crash, last sync result and library counts — and gains nothing when the toggle is off. - [ ] "Include diagnostics" exists in Settings, defaults to on, and turning it off produces byte-identical behaviour to today. - [ ] The clipboard write and log read happen off the main thread. - [ ] The URL stays under a few thousand characters no matter how large the log summary is. - [ ] The `## Environment` block and the `template=bug_report.md` parameter are unchanged, so #295 stays fixed. - [ ] DECISIONS.md records the summary-vs-clipboard split; README.md's test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - On the phone: favorite a track, reopen Library, press Feedback, paste into the issue — the pasted text should show the favorite write and the Library counts. This is the acceptance check from #344 and it needs a real device. - Confirm the Toast is visible enough to notice that the clipboard was written, and that it is not annoying enough to want the default off. - Confirm the summary reads well pasted into a GitHub issue body (not just in the log viewer). ## Context - Part of #344. The event names the summary quotes come from #375; the last-crash value comes from #374. - `launchFeedback` is called from `FeedbackButton`'s own `onClick` (FeedbackButton.kt:57-61), and `FeedbackButton` is used in `SettingsScreen.kt:90-95`, `LibraryScreen.kt:162-167` and `MainActivity.kt:4170-4178`. All three therefore get this for free. - The comment at FeedbackButton.kt:35-37 explains that blank issues are disabled on the repo, so the template name must be kept. Do not "simplify" that away. - `SettingsScreen.kt` already uses `SettingsToggleRow(label, checked, onCheckedChange, help)` — reuse it; do not invent a new row. - `Favorites`, `LikedTracks`, `SavedShows`, `PlaybackSettings` and `ThemeSettings` are the precedent for a `SharedPreferences` flag object with an `init(context)` and a `StateFlow`. - Sharing on Android is done in `Share.kt` for shows and tracks; the clipboard route here is intentionally different because a GitHub issue is filled in a browser, not in an app that accepts `EXTRA_TEXT`. ## Out of scope - Attaching a real `.txt` file via `FileProvider` and `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE`. Pasting covers it; revisit only if UAT says otherwise. - Changing the `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md` template. - Attaching diagnostics to anything other than the Feedback issue. - Automatic upload of diagnostics to the sync Worker or anywhere else. Nothing leaves the device without an explicit press. - macOS-side Feedback integration. - Collecting the owner's email or any account information.

column2: D: Settings → About → Diagnostics viewer (Copy, Share, Clear, crash notice)
column3: > **Original request:** > > A viewer in Settings: Settings → About → Diagnostics shows recent entries, with Share and Clear. Part of #344 Depends on: #373 Needs from #374: `CrashCapture.consumePreviousCrash` and `CrashCapture.lastCrashNotice`. It needs from #373: `tailLines`, `exportText`, `clear`, `onDiskBytes`, `summaryLines`. The Feedback sub-issue is independent of this one. ## Problem / goal The log fills up and stays invisible. The owner needs a way to read it, hand it over, and delete it — without a computer and without `adb`. Goal: Settings → ABOUT → Diagnostics opens a screen listing recent entries, with Copy, Share and Clear, and a one-shot notice when the previous run crashed. Design decisions (made here, recorded in DECISIONS.md): - **Share is plain text, not a file attachment.** `exportText` output goes out via `ACTION_SEND` with `EXTRA_TEXT`, and "Copy" puts the same text on the clipboard. Attaching a real `.txt` to a GitHub issue would need a `FileProvider`, a `<paths>` XML and a manifest change for a benefit pasting into the issue body already delivers. If UAT says pasting is not good enough, that is a follow-up. - **Show the last 200 lines, not the whole file.** A 1 MiB log is unreadable on a phone. 200 lines is roughly a session or two. - **Never block the main thread**: read on `Dispatchers.IO` and hand the lines to the composable as state. - **Clear is confirmable** and also clears `last_crash.txt`, so a cleared log cannot still smuggle a crash trace out through the Feedback summary. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/DiagnosticsScreen.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SettingsScreen.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CrashCapture.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/DiagnosticsScreenTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: - New `DiagnosticsScreen.kt` in the flat `dev.mike.couchtour` package:   - Reads `DiagnosticsLog.tailLines(200)` on `Dispatchers.IO` in a `LaunchedEffect`/`produceState`, renders a `LazyColumn` of the lines in monospace, timestamp column dimmed, `WARN`/`ERROR` lines tinted. Do not parse the tab structure into objects — the raw line is what gets pasted into an issue and it should look the same on screen.   - Top bar: back, plus a `Refresh` action that re-reads.   - Overflow or footer actions: **Copy** (clipboard = `DiagnosticsLog.exportText(context)`), **Share** (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`, `type = "text/plain"`, `EXTRA_SUBJECT = "Couch Tour diagnostics"`, `EXTRA_TEXT` = the same text), **Clear** (a confirmation dialog, then `DiagnosticsLog.clear()` and `CrashCapture.consumePreviousCrash()`, then re-read).   - A summary header: entry count, on-disk size, and the `mark`ed values from `DiagnosticsLog.summaryLines()` — those are what the owner will actually read first.   - Empty state: "No diagnostics yet. They appear after you use the app for a while." Not an error. - `SettingsScreen.kt`: in the `SectionEyebrow("ABOUT")` block (currently `Version` and `Show & tape data` at lines 244-257), add a `SettingsValueRow(label = "Diagnostics", value = "<n> entries · <size>", showChevron = true, onClick = { nav.navigate("diagnostics") })`. Follow the existing `SettingsValueRow(label, value, showChevron, onClick)` signature exactly. Read the count/size off `DiagnosticsLog` on `Dispatchers.IO` so Settings does not do disk I/O in composition. - `MainActivity.kt`: add a `composable("diagnostics") { DiagnosticsScreen(onBack = { nav.popBackStack() }) }` to the `NavHost` (routes are declared inline at lines 216-314). The screen needs a `NavController` for the back action — pass it in the same way `SettingsScreen` does today. - `CrashCapture.kt`: consume the previous crash here. On first composition of `DiagnosticsScreen`, if `CrashCapture.lastCrashNotice.value != null`, show it as a dismissible card with the timestamp and the first line of the trace, and call `consumePreviousCrash()` on dismiss (not on open — the owner should get a second chance to copy it). - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`; record plain-text share (no `FileProvider`) and the 200-line window. - Bump the test count in README.md. Test: `DiagnosticsScreenTest` (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [34])`). There is no `androidTest/`, so this is a unit test — assert behaviour, not pixels: - With seeded log lines, the screen's read path returns them newest-last in order and the summary header carries the entry count and size. - Copy puts `exportText` on the clipboard, and Share builds an `ACTION_SEND` intent with the same text and `text/plain`. - Clear calls through to `DiagnosticsLog.clear()` and `consumePreviousCrash()`: after it, the file and `last_crash.txt` are gone and the screen shows the empty state. - A `lastCrashNotice` that has been consumed does not reappear on a second composition. - If Compose UI testing is too heavy for a unit test here, cover the read/clear/copy actions as plain functions called from the composable and test those directly — do not add an `androidTest/` source set for this. ## Done when - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green with the new tests. - [ ] Settings → About → Diagnostics opens, lists the last 200 lines, and shows a summary header with count, size and the marked values. - [ ] Copy and Share both yield the same text the owner would paste into a GitHub issue, and neither requires a file picker. - [ ] Clear removes both log generations *and* `last_crash.txt`, behind a confirmation. - [ ] A previous-run crash is surfaced once, is dismissible, and does not come back after dismissal. - [ ] No disk I/O happens in composition or on the main thread. - [ ] The Google TV surface still builds: `TvMainActivity` shares the `:app` module, so run `assembleDebug` and confirm both launcher entries still resolve. - [ ] DECISIONS.md records the plain-text-share decision and the 200-line window; README.md's test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - On the phone: is the viewer actually readable on a small screen? Are the monospace lines legible without horizontal scrolling? - Does Share land somewhere useful (mail, Notes, Slack) on the owner's phone, and does the text survive the paste into a GitHub issue body? - Is "Clear" discoverable without being one tap away from deleting something the owner wanted? ## Context - Part of #344. The log format and APIs come from #373; the crash notice comes from #374. - `SettingsScreen.kt` already hosts the Feedback button (lines 90-95) and the ABOUT block (244-257) with the `SectionEyebrow` / `SettingsValueRow` / `SettingsActionRow` / `SettingsToggleRow` helpers. Match their signatures and visual style; the design system lives in `DesignComponents.kt`. - `SettingsScreen` receives a `NavController` already (it navigates to `sync` and `login` from rows), so reuse that rather than inventing a new navigation path. - Test config: `testOptions.unitTests.isIncludeAndroidResources = true` is already set in `app/build.gradle.kts`, and `SyncTest.kt` is the model for a Robolectric test. - `Share.kt` already builds share intents for shows and tracks — follow its shape for the Share action instead of hand-rolling a second one. ## Out of scope - Filtering or searching the log, or a severity filter. - Live tailing or auto-refresh on a timer. Refresh is manual. - Exporting to a different format (JSON, zip). - Attaching a real `.txt` file via `FileProvider`. Explicitly deferred; pasting covers it. - Any change to how the log is written — no new events, no new rotation behaviour. - macOS-side diagnostics UI.

column2: C: instrument library, playback, sync, API and navigation events into the diagnostics log
column3: > **Original request:** > > Log: > - Library and favorites changes: favorite or unfavorite a track or show (source: phish.in or Relisten, id), add to library, and what the Library screen counted when it loaded (the playlists, shows and tracks counts). > - History and playback: play start, resume, progress saves. > - Sync: start and end, counts pushed and pulled, errors. > - API calls: path, status, duration (feed from `TimingEventListener`), failures and timeouts. > - Screen navigation (route names only). Part of #344 Depends on: #373 Needs from #373: `DiagnosticsLog.log` and `DiagnosticsLog.mark`. ## Problem / goal `DiagnosticsLog` exists and writes nothing useful yet. This issue wires the event sources the owner asked for into it, so that a future bug report ("my favorited tracks aren't in Library", #343) comes with evidence instead of a guess. Deliberately **no new UI** in this issue. The point is that the log fills up; #376 and #377 make it visible and shareable. Rules for every call site: - One line per event, using the tab-separated format from #373. Event names are stable, lowercase, dot-separated: `library.favorite`, `library.counts`, `playback.start`, `sync.end`, `api.call`, `nav.route`. - **Route names, ids, counts, statuses and timings only.** Never a full URL with a query string, never a header, never a token. `TimingEventListener` already logs `encodedPath` for this reason — keep it that way. - `DiagnosticsLog.log` is fire-and-forget and cheap, so it is safe on hot paths, but do not log per-frame or per-list-item. Aggregate: one `library.counts` line per Library load, one `api.call` line per request, one `nav.route` line per navigation. - Anything the Feedback summary should quote (`library.counts`, sync result, last crash) goes through `DiagnosticsLog.mark`, not just `log`. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LikedTracks.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SavedShows.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Favorites.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LocalPlaylist.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LibraryScreen.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/ApiTiming.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Sync.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlayerViewModel.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlaybackService.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/DiagnosticsInstrumentationTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: Library and favorites: - `LikedTracks.toggle(id)` → `library.favorite kind=track id=<id> on=<true|false>`. Also `mark("Library counts")` is not needed here; keep favorites as plain log lines. - `SavedShows.toggle(key)` → `library.favorite kind=show key=<key> on=…`. - `Favorites.toggle(key)` → `library.favorite kind=artist key=<key> on=…`. - `LocalPlaylistDao.addTrack(track, now)` / `removeTrack(rowId, playlistId, now)` → `library.playlist action=add|remove track=<id> playlist=<playlistId>`. - `LibraryScreen.kt:127-130` (`playlistCount` / `showCount` / `trackCount` / `totalCount`) → after a successful load, one `library.counts playlists=… shows=… tracks=… total=…` **and** `DiagnosticsLog.mark("Library counts", "…")`. This is the line that answers "Tracks 0" in #343. It must log on *every* completed load, including the zero case — a count of zero is the bug. Playback and history: - In the play state layer, emit `playback.start` (track id, show, source, and `resume=<bool>` distinguishing start from resume) and `playback.stop`. - Progress save at `PlaybackService.kt:445` (`progressDao().put(progress)`) → `playback.progress track=<id> pct=<0-100> saved`. Do not log on every progress tick — the save is already debounced, so this is a low-frequency line. If it turns out to be chatty in the log, rate-limit it to once per track per minute rather than removing it. Sync: - `SyncSession.sync(progressDao)` → `sync.start`; on return, `sync.end pushed=<n> pulled=<n> ms=<n> pushed_upto=<watermark> pulled_seq=<seq>` and `DiagnosticsLog.mark("Last sync", "…")`. - Every branch that sets `SyncSession.lastError` also logs `sync.error code=<short code>`. Use a short code (`unauthorized`, `gone`, `network`, `server`, `other`) — **not** the raw exception message, which can embed a URL. - The launch catch at `CouchTourApp.kt:39` is already a `Log.w`; add the matching `sync.error` line. `CouchTourApp.kt` is already in #373's and #374's file lists, so if you need to touch it, say so in the PR. API: - `TimingEventListener` (`ApiTiming.kt`) mirrors each of `callStart` / `connectionAcquired` / `callEnd` / `callFailed` into `DiagnosticsLog`: `api.call path=<encodedPath> phase=start|connected|end|failed ms=<n> reused=<bool>` and on failure `error=<exception simple name>`. Keep the existing `android.util.Log` calls — logcat is still useful with `adb`. Navigation: - In the `NavHost` in `MainActivity.kt:216-314`, log `nav.route route=<route pattern>` on each destination change. Route patterns only, no arguments, no query values. Tests: - `DiagnosticsInstrumentationTest`: a MockWebServer-backed OkHttp test (same setup as `ApiRequestTest.kt` / `SyncTest.kt`) proving `TimingEventListener` writes `api.call … phase=end ms=…` and `phase=failed` for a 500 and a dropped connection into the diagnostics log. - A test that the redaction denylist holds for a sync error line, and one that `library.counts` is emitted with zeros when the lists are empty. - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` recording the event-name vocabulary and the "counts, ids, routes, timings only" privacy rule. Bump the test count in README.md. ## Done when - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green with the new tests. - [ ] Every event in the original request is emitted: library/favorites changes, library counts, play start/resume/progress save, sync start/end/errors, API path/status/duration/failures, navigation routes. - [ ] `library.counts` fires on every completed Library load, including when the counts are zero. - [ ] No line in the log contains a full URL with a query string, a header, an auth token or a pairing code — grep the recorded log in a test to prove it for the API and sync paths. - [ ] Sync errors log a short code, not a raw exception message. - [ ] No new screen, dialog, banner or settings row is added by this issue. - [ ] DECISIONS.md records the event-name vocabulary; README.md's test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - With #376 landed, favorite a track, reopen Library, open Diagnostics: the log should show the `library.favorite` line and then a `library.counts` line with non-zero tracks. - Watch the log for a few days of normal use and confirm it reads sensibly and is not dominated by one chatty event (this is the check that decides whether `playback.progress` needs rate-limiting). ## Context - Part of #344. The event list in the quote above is the owner's, verbatim — do not add event sources beyond it (no per-item list logging, no battery/network state). - Toggle sites: `LikedTracks.toggle(id)`, `SavedShows.toggle(key)`, `Favorites.toggle(key)`, `LocalPlaylistDao.addTrack/removeTrack` — all synchronous, all easy hook points. - Library counts are computed at `LibraryScreen.kt:127-130`; the "Tracks 0" symptom in #343 is exactly what this line has to expose. - `SyncSession` is an `object` with `lastError: StateFlow<String?>` and a `debounceScope`; `SyncTokenStore` holds `lastSeq`, `lastPushWatermark`, `lastSyncedAt`, which is where the sync counts come from. - `ApiTiming.kt:30`'s `runCatching` wrapper exists because plain-JUnit tests run against an unmocked `android.util.Log` that throws. Mirror it around any new `Log` call. - `MainActivity.kt`'s `NavHost` has 19 routes declared inline; there is no route-registry class. ## Out of scope - The crash handler — #374. The diagnostics viewer — #376. The Feedback flow — #377. - Per-track or per-list-item logging, or any event that would blow the 1 MiB cap in a day of use. - Logging request/response bodies, HTTP headers, or user-typed text. - Any macOS-side equivalent. - Any upload. Everything stays in `filesDir` until the owner shares it.

column2: B: crash capture (uncaught-exception handler, last_crash, next-launch notice)
column3: > **Original request:** > > An uncaught-exception handler writes the stack trace to the diagnostics log (and a `last_crash` file) before the app dies. The next launch notes that the previous run crashed. Part of #344 Depends on: #373 Needs from #373: `DiagnosticsLog.recordCrash` and `DiagnosticsLog.mark`. ## Problem / goal There is no uncaught-exception handler. A crash on the owner's phone leaves nothing behind except whatever logcat happened to hold, which is gone by the time anyone looks. Goal: capture the stack trace synchronously before the process dies, write a `last_crash.txt` next to the log, and tell the app on the next launch that the previous run crashed. Key decision, already made in #373 and to be recorded here: **the crash write is synchronous**. Everything else in `DiagnosticsLog` queues onto a background writer; a crash path cannot, because the process dies before the queue drains. `recordCrash` appends directly on the crashing thread, wrapped in `runCatching`, and must never itself throw — a crash handler that throws replaces the original crash with a worse one. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CrashCapture.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CouchTourApp.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CrashCaptureTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: - Add `object CrashCapture` in the flat `dev.mike.couchtour` package:   - `install(context: Context)`: chain a `Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler` in front of whatever is already installed (on Android that is the runtime's `RuntimeInit$KillApplicationHandler`, and it **must still run** — swallowing the exception would leave the app in a zombie state and break ANR/crash reporting). Store the previous handler.   - Handler body, in order: `DiagnosticsLog.init(this)` (idempotent, cheap — covers a crash during `Application.onCreate` itself), `DiagnosticsLog.recordCrash("crash", "<thread> · <throwable chain + full stack trace>")`, write the same text to `filesDir/diagnostics/last_crash.txt`, then delegate to the previous handler. Every step individually wrapped so one failure does not skip the next.   - `previousCrash(): String?` — reads `last_crash.txt` if present, else null.   - `consumePreviousCrash()` — clears the file and returns the text; #376's viewer and any dismiss affordance call it so the banner does not come back forever.   - `lastCrashNotice: StateFlow<String?>` — set once during `Application.onCreate` when a previous crash exists, so a screen can show it without doing file I/O on the main thread. - In `CouchTourApp.onCreate()`: call `CrashCapture.install(this)` **first**, before `DiagnosticsLog.init` and before the existing `*.init(this)` calls, then detect and record the previous crash:   `if (CrashCapture.previousCrash() != null) DiagnosticsLog.mark("Last crash", ...)` plus a `crash.previous` log line with the timestamp and the first line of the trace. - Do not delete `last_crash.txt` on detection — a user who never opens Settings should still be able to export it. - Do not disturb the existing fire-and-forget launch sync at `CouchTourApp.kt:35-41`, whose comment explains that an exception escaping a bare `launch` reaches the default handler. That reasoning stays true, and this handler is what will now record it. - Allocate a decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`; record the synchronous-write decision and the handler-chaining requirement. - Bump the test count in README.md. Test: `CrashCaptureTest` (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [34])`). - Install, then throw an uncaught exception on a background thread: the previous handler is invoked (assert with a recording fake installed beforehand), the trace appears in `diagnostics.log`, and `last_crash.txt` contains the exception class and message. - The handler survives a broken sink: point the diagnostics directory at a path that cannot be created and confirm the previous handler is still called and nothing propagates out of the handler. - Next-launch detection: write a `last_crash.txt`, run the `CouchTourApp.onCreate` detection path, assert `previousCrash()` is non-null, a `crash.previous` line is logged, and the file still exists; then `consumePreviousCrash()` clears it and a second detection is a no-op. - A chained (cause-of-cause) exception is written with its full `caused by` chain, not just the top frame. ## Done when - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green with the new tests. - [ ] The previously-installed handler is always invoked, proven by a test — the app still dies normally. - [ ] The stack trace is in the log synchronously, proven by reading the file immediately after the throw in the test, with no waiting and no coroutine drain. - [ ] A crash that happens *before* `CouchTourApp` finishes initialising is still captured. - [ ] `last_crash.txt` survives relaunch until something explicitly consumes it. - [ ] The handler never throws out of itself under any sink failure. - [ ] DECISIONS.md records the synchronous-on-crash exception and the chaining requirement; README.md's test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - Install a build on the phone, force a crash from a debug build, relaunch: the app should say the previous run crashed, and the trace should be visible in the Diagnostics viewer once #376 lands. ## Context - Part of #344. Privacy rules apply: the trace is written with the same redaction as everything else, and must not carry the auth token or pairing code out of a stack frame — if a frame's text contains one, `DiagnosticsLog`'s denylist catches it by key only, so do not paste raw exception messages that embed a URL with a query string. Log the exception class and message; they are the useful part. - `CouchTourApp.kt:29-41` — the existing comment on why a bare `launch` must not throw, and why that still holds. - `CouchTourApp` is the only `Application` subclass and both `MainActivity` and `TvMainActivity` share the `:app` module, so a handler installed here covers phone and TV. - The Google TV surface is a second Activity in the same module (D233), so no manifest change is needed for this issue. ## Out of scope - Showing a crash banner or dialog — #376 owns diagnostics UI. This issue only exposes `lastCrashNotice` and the read/clear API. - ANR detection, native (NDK) crash capture, or `ApplicationExitInfo` history. - Uploading crash reports. Nothing leaves the device without an explicit owner action. - Symbolicated/pretty stack traces, or mapping frames to source line numbers.

column2: A: core on-device diagnostics log (rotation, redaction, tail, summary)
column3: > **Original request:** > > A small append-only file in app storage, rotated at about 1 MB, keeping the last few days. Each entry has a timestamp, an event name and short details. > > Logging must never throw or block the main thread. Write on a background dispatcher, and swallow I/O errors (same approach as `TimingEventListener.log`). Part of #344 ## Problem / goal There is no on-device record of anything the app did. This is the foundation: a small, safe, rotating log file plus the read APIs the crash handler, the viewer and the Feedback flow need. No event sources are wired up here — that is #375. Design decisions (made here, recorded in DECISIONS.md): - **Location**: `context.filesDir/diagnostics/` — internal storage, not `cacheDir`, because Android may evict cache under pressure and a diagnostics log that vanishes is worthless. Not world-readable; the viewer and Feedback flow are the only exports. - **Files**: `diagnostics.log` (current) and `diagnostics.log.1` (one previous generation). Disk ceiling is therefore 2 MiB, not 1. - **Rotation**: on append, if `diagnostics.log` is already at or over the 1 MiB cap, delete `diagnostics.log.1`, rename `diagnostics.log` → `diagnostics.log.1`, start a fresh `diagnostics.log`, and write a `log.rotated` line into it. - **Retention**: on `init`, if `diagnostics.log` is over the cap, keep only lines newer than 7 days; if it is *still* over the cap, keep the last 2000 lines. Rotation handles the common case; this is the safety valve for a long-idle device. - **Line format**: `<ISO-8601 UTC timestamp>\t<LEVEL>\t<event>\t<key>=<value> ...`, e.g.   `2026-09-29T22:14:58.123Z INFO library.counts playlists=3 shows=12 tracks=410`   One line per entry, tab-separated, so it parses back with a `split('\t')` and survives a paste into a GitHub issue. - **Redaction**: a key-name denylist. If a key's lowercase name contains any of `token`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `auth`, `credential`, `cookie`, `pairing`, `code`, `key` (as a whole word or `access_key`/`sync_key` style compound), its value is replaced with `***` before the line is written. Callers that log something token-shaped must go through `redactValue`. - **Writes are asynchronous**: `DiagnosticsLog.log(...)` is a non-suspend function that does `trySend` on a `Channel` drained by a single-writer coroutine on `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)`. It never blocks, never touches disk on the caller's thread, and never throws — any failure inside the writer is caught and latches writing off for the rest of the process (a broken log must not take the app down). - **The one synchronous path is `recordCrash`** — deliberately not asynchronous, because the process is about to die and a queued write would be lost. It appends directly, wrapped in `runCatching`. Log this exception to the rule in DECISIONS.md; #374 depends on it. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/DiagnosticsLog.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CouchTourApp.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/DiagnosticsLogTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: - Add `object DiagnosticsLog` in the existing flat package `dev.mike.couchtour` (this codebase has no subpackages).   - `init(context: Context)`: create `filesDir/diagnostics/`, run retention, write a `log.start` line carrying the app version. Idempotent, and safe to call more than once.   - `log(event: String, level: Level = INFO, vararg fields: Pair<String, Any?>)`: apply redaction, build the line, `trySend` to the writer channel. No-op before `init`.   - `recordCrash(event: String, detail: String)`: synchronous, direct append (see above). Also used by #374.   - `mark(event: String)`: a named last-value marker that `summaryLines()` reports. `Library counts`, `last sync result` and `last crash` are the three the Feedback summary needs, so #375/#374 call this for their high-value events instead of leaving #376/#377 to re-parse the log.   - `tailLines(n: Int): List<String>`: last `n` lines, oldest first, read from at most the last 256 KiB of the file.   - `summaryLines(): String`: the last value of each `mark`, plus total entry count and on-disk size, as short human-readable lines.   - `exportText(context: Context): String`: `diagnostics.log.1` then `diagnostics.log`, oldest first — what #376 shares and #377 pastes.   - `clear()`: delete both generations and `last_crash.txt` if present.   - `onDiskBytes(): Long`. - Call `DiagnosticsLog.init(this)` from `CouchTourApp.onCreate()` before the other `*.init(this)` calls, so a crash in any of them is still recorded. - Follow the `runCatching`-around-`android.util.Log` precedent at `ApiTiming.kt:30` for anything that might hit an unmocked SDK stub in plain-JUnit tests. - Allocate the decision ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and record the six choices above in DECISIONS.md. - Bump the test count in README.md. Test: `DiagnosticsLogTest` (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [34])`, same config as `SyncTest.kt`; give the log a tmp `filesDir` per test). - A log at the cap rotates on the next append: the current file starts fresh, carries a `log.rotated` line, and the previous content is readable in `.1`. On-disk total never exceeds 2 MiB. - Retention drops lines older than 7 days; when the file is still over the cap after that, the oldest lines are dropped down to 2000. - A key named `access_token`, `pairing_code`, `sync_key` or `auth` writes `***`; `track_id=411` writes `411`. - `log()` returns without touching disk and without throwing when `filesDir` is not writable; `recordCrash` likewise swallows the I/O error. - `tailLines(5)` returns the last 5 lines in order, and does not read a 1 MiB file into a `String` (assert on the read window, not on the whole file). - `summaryLines()` reports the most recent value of each `mark`, not the first. ## Done when - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green with the new tests. - [ ] On-disk diagnostics footprint is bounded at 2 MiB, proven by a test rather than by inspection. - [ ] `log()` is non-blocking and non-throwing on the main thread; the only synchronous write is `recordCrash`. - [ ] No value whose key looks like a credential is ever written, and there is a test naming at least `access_token`, `pairing_code` and `sync_key`. - [ ] Nothing logs an event source yet — no changes to `Sync.kt`, `LikedTracks.kt`, `ApiTiming.kt` or any screen. Those are #375. - [ ] DECISIONS.md has a new `Dnnn` entry covering storage location, the 1 MiB/2-generation/7-day/2000-line numbers, the redaction denylist, and the synchronous-on-crash exception. - [ ] README.md's test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check Nothing yet — there is no UI in this issue. The first thing a human will see is #376's viewer. ## Context - Part of #344, which carries the full rationale, the privacy rules and the acceptance list. - `ApiTiming.kt:30` — the "logging must never throw" precedent to copy. - `SyncSession.debounceScope` (`CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO)`, Sync.kt:484) — the existing background-scope style to match. - `CouchTourApp.onCreate` already orders several `*.init(this)` calls; insert before them. - This codebase is a single flat package `dev.mike.couchtour` with no subpackages — do not introduce one for this. - Test layout: `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/`, JUnit 4 + Robolectric, `testOptions.unitTests.isIncludeAndroidResources = true` already set. There is no `androidTest/`. ## Out of scope - Any event source (library, playback, sync, API timing, navigation) — that is #375. - The uncaught-exception handler and `last_crash` — that is #374. - The Settings viewer — #376. The Feedback flow — #377. - Uploading the log anywhere. The log leaves the device only via an explicit owner share or copy. - Structured JSON, log levels beyond INFO/WARN/ERROR, or a compression format.

column2: Liked Relisten tracks store display metadata, not bare uuids
column3: > **Original request:** > > I have mostly favorited tracks but my library only displays shows, says 0 tracks. And looks more like history of shows I've played than things I've added to my library. History should be separated from library with different tracking and views. Part of #343 ## Problem / goal `LikedTracks` is a `Set<String>` of Relisten track uuids. That is enough to fill a heart and nothing else: a Library row needs a title, a show date and a venue, and none of that survives the toggle. It is also not enough to *play* the track again — resolving a Relisten track needs its artist slug, its show date and its tape (recording) id, because a show can have nine tapes with different track splits (D161, `LocalPlaylistTrackEntity`). So the owner's liked tracks can't be listed in the Library and can't be queued from a list. The same gap blocks #B and #C, which both need a listable liked track. This piece changes the **store**, not the Library. It gives `LikedTracks` a record per like — enough to render a row and to hand the ref to the existing `resolveLocalPlaylistTracks` path — and nothing else. Still `SharedPreferences`, not Room: this is a flat set of single-track records, exactly the shape D161 gave `Favorites`/`LikedTracks`, so there is no migration. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LikedTracks.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LikedTracksTest.kt` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: - Add `data class LikedTrackRef` in `LikedTracks.kt`: `id` (Relisten track uuid), `title`,   `showDate`, `venueName`, `durationMs`, `artistName`, `artistSlug`, `recordingId` (nullable),   `artUrl` (nullable), `likedAt: Long`. Every display field nullable or defaulted to `""` —   a like recorded by an older build has no metadata and must still load. - Replace the `Set<String>` internals with a `Map<String, LikedTrackRef>` serialized with   `kotlinx.serialization` (already a dependency — see `Api.kt`'s `json` and   `implementation(libs.kotlinx.serialization.json)`) into a **new** prefs key, e.g.   `track_records`. Keep `KEY_TRACKS = "track_ids"` readable for the migration.   - `toggle(ref: LikedTrackRef)` writes the record when liking, removes the key when unliking.   - `ids: StateFlow<Set<String>>` is now *derived* from the record map so the existing     `id in likedIds` check in `LikeTrackButton` and the two call sites keep working unchanged     in shape.   - `entries: StateFlow<List<LikedTrackRef>>`, newest `likedAt` first. This is what "Recently     added" sorts on; the record has to carry the timestamp or the Library cannot.   - `contains(id: String): Boolean` alongside `ids`, mirroring `SavedShows.contains`. - **Migration on `init`.** Any id present in the legacy `track_ids` set with no record becomes   a record with blank display fields and `likedAt = 0`. The heart must stay filled and the id   must not be silently dropped — the owner already has likes on disk. Corrupt/unparseable JSON   must degrade to an empty store rather than throwing out of `init` (which would crash app   start-up); log it and carry on. - Change `LikeTrackButton` to take the ref rather than a bare id, and update both call sites:   - `RecordingTrackRow` (`MainActivity.kt:2247`) already holds `track`, `artist`, `date` and     `recordingId` — the complete ref, no plumbing needed beyond the signature.   - `NowPlaying.kt:596` has only `PlayerState`. Build the ref from `state.trackTitle`,     `artistName`, `artistId`, `showDate`, `venueName`, `durationMs`, `artUrl`, `backend`.     `recordingId` is **not** in `PlayerState` or `Keys` (see `PlaybackService.kt:39`): when the     backend is Relisten, derive it from `state.queueKey` with `parseQueueKey`; if the result is     `QueueKind.RECORDING`, call `parseRecordingId(ref.id)` and store **`.sourceId`** (the bare     tape id). Do not store `QueueRef.id` or `RecordingId.id`: those are the full     `artist/date/source` string, whereas `LocalPlaylistTrackEntity.recordingId` and     `RecordingTrackRow`'s `recordingId` are just the source id (`RelistenCatalogSource.show(artist,     date, recordingId)` takes that form). Any other queue kind (show, shuffle, local playlist) →     `null`. A shuffle or a local-playlist queue carries no tape identity — that is the same     `recordingId = null` fallback `LocalPlaylistTrackEntity` already documents, so it is correct     behaviour, not a gap. Use `state.artistId` as `artistSlug` (as the existing playlist ref at     `NowPlaying.kt:~505` does). Do not add a `Keys` constant or a `PlayerState` field for this. - Add `internal fun LikedTrackRef.toLocalPlaylistTrackRef(): LocalPlaylistTrackEntity` in   `LikedTracks.kt` (playlistId `""`, position `0` — the same placeholder the   `AddToPlaylistButton` call sites pass). That is the adapter #B/#C will hand to   `resolveLocalPlaylistTracks`; write it now so the shape is settled and testable. - Update the KDoc on the object: it currently says the store is "a set of ids" and points at   `PlayerState` as the reason Now Playing can't be keyed. Both are now false; say what it is. Test: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests '*LikedTracksTest*'` with `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home"`. Extend `LikedTracksTest` (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [34])`, same shape as the existing file) to cover: a toggle round-trips every field; `entries` is newest-first; unliking removes both the record and the id; a like pre-seeded in the legacy `track_ids` set still reads as liked with blank metadata; malformed JSON in `track_records` does not throw and yields an empty store; `toLocalPlaylistTrackRef` maps backend/slug/recording id through unchanged. ## Done when - [ ] `LikedTracks.entries` returns records carrying title, show date and venue for a like made       from a show's track row, and `likedAt` orders them newest first. - [ ] A like made from Now Playing and a like made from a show's setlist both produce a complete       record, and either heart un-likes the same entry. - [ ] A like stored by the pre-change build (bare id in `track_ids`) still reads as liked after       upgrade, appears in `entries` with blank display fields, and can be un-liked. - [ ] Malformed JSON in prefs does not crash `init`. - [ ] `toLocalPlaylistTrackRef` produces a `LocalPlaylistTrackEntity` that       `resolveLocalPlaylistTracks` can resolve (covered by the existing resolver test's shape). - [ ] No Room migration: `PhishInDb` version and `Progress.kt` are untouched, and no schema       JSON changes. - [ ] A Now Playing like from a tape queue (`relisten:artist/date/source`) stores the bare `source` id as `recordingId`; from a shuffle/local-playlist queue it stores `null` (unit-test the derivation as a small pure helper). - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new `Dnnn` entry (id from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`) noting it revises D161's flat-`Set<String>` shape for liked tracks. - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes and `README.md`'s test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - On device: like a track from a show's setlist, like a different one from Now Playing, force   stop and relaunch, and confirm both hearts are still filled and un-liking either one leaves   the other alone. - If you have a Relisten like from before this change, open that show's track row and confirm   the old heart is still filled (the metadata-less upgrade path). ## Context - The existing two call sites are `MainActivity.kt:2247` (`RecordingTrackRow`) and   `NowPlaying.kt:596`. `LikeButton` (phish.in, `MainActivity.kt:4112`) is a *different*,   server-side like and is not touched here — those likes are fetched from the API in #C. - `PlayerState` (`PlayerViewModel.kt:22`) has `trackTitle`, `artistName`, `artistId`,   `showDate`, `venueName`, `durationMs`, `artUrl`, `backend` and `queueKey` — enough for a   record; it has no recording id, hence the `queueKey` parse. - `resolveLocalPlaylistTracks` (`LocalPlaylist.kt:168`) is the one place a stored track ref is   refetched into something playable, batched per show/tape. Reuse it, don't fork it. - #B (Library lists saved things) and #C (phish.in account content in Library) both depend on   this. Neither is started until this lands. - Log the storage decision in `DECISIONS.md` with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` — it revises the   flat-`Set<String>` shape D161 chose, and the reason (a listable row needs a title) matters to   whoever touches it next. ## Out of scope - Any Library UI. #B and #C own the screen. - phish.in server-side likes (`LikeButton`) — untouched, fetched from the API in #C. - `SavedShows` — #B gives it the same record treatment. - Room, sync, and the macOS client. - Adding recording identity to `PlayerState`/`Keys`; `recordingId = null` outside a tape queue   is the accepted answer.

column2: Smoke spec: scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md + shared runner contract (lib.sh)
column3: > **Original request:** > > 1. `scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md` — ~15 user journeys, each with an explicit pass condition, per platform (Mac + Android). Seed from this round's failures: >    - Browse artists → open moe. >    - Search "moe" → artist hit appears >    - Favorite an artist → relaunch → still favorited; no unfavorited artists shown >    - Relaunch → Home shows In Progress, On This Date, Next Tour Stop >    - Tap Next Stop artist chip → focus changes (not tour picker) >    - Jam chart note shows details + source link >    - Library shows phish.in account playlists >    - Favorite on Mac → appears on Android (and vice versa) >    - In Progress on Android → appears on Mac Part of #357 Depends on: #366 ## Problem / goal Prod 0.83 shipped five seam bugs with a fully green test suite. Nothing in the repo says what a user flow is supposed to *do*, so nothing can fail when it doesn't. The fix is to write the flows down — but a spec that only exists as prose cannot be executed, and a spec that exists only as code cannot be reviewed by a human deciding whether the app is behaving. This sub-issue establishes the contract the whole smoke program runs on, and nothing else: 1. **`scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md`** — the spec. ~15 journeys, each with a stable kebab-case id, the    platforms it applies to, its fixture requirement, its steps in prose, and — the important part    — a pass condition written as a **query over an accessibility identifier**, not as "the screen    looks right". It also carries an appendix defining the report grammar, so D writes a formatter    against a written contract rather than reverse-engineering one. 2. **`scripts/smoke/lib.sh`** — the shared runner contract: the one-line-per-journey result format,    preflight helpers, and the logging both platform runners will `source`. Having it land here    means the Mac and Android runners can be built in the same tick without either of them owning    a file the other wants to edit. The identifiers this spec queries come from #365 (`macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift`) and #364 (`app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt`). Those must be merged first — hence the dependency on #366, which is blocked on #365 and creates `scripts/smoke/README.md`. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md` (new) - `scripts/smoke/lib.sh` (new) - `scripts/smoke/README.md` (append a "Journeys" section — created by #366) - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Write `scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md`. For every journey, exactly these fields, in this order:   - **id** — stable, kebab-case, unique, never renamed once merged. This is the id that appears     in reports, in `Waived:` lines, and in filed bug titles.   - **platforms** — `mac`, `android`, or `mac,android`. Cross-platform sync journeys say     `mac,android` *and* name the direction (`mac→android` or `android→mac`).   - **fixture** — one of `none`, `signed-in`, `seeded-favorite`. State precisely what must     already be true in the installed app before the journey runs. The runner never types     credentials; it reuses whatever session the app already has.   - **steps** — short prose, the literal taps a user makes.   - **pass condition** — a query, written so a runner can execute it. Name the exact identifier     (`AXID.homeSectionInProgress` → `home.section.in-progress` on the wire; `A11yTags.homeSectionInProgress`     on Android) and say what must be true of it: present, absent, count ≥ N, or a specific     sibling/nonexistence. Example: "`home.section.in-progress` is absent, or present with zero     `.row.*` children when nothing is in progress."   Seed it with these fifteen, which cover every 0.83 escape:   | id | platforms | fixture | asserts |   |---|---|---|---|   | `launch-cold-start` | mac, android | none | app reaches Home; nav identifiers present |   | `home-sections-after-relaunch` | mac, android | seeded-favorite | all three Home sections present after a force-quit + relaunch |   | `browse-artists-to-artist` | mac, android | none | Artists section → `moe.` artist screen opens |   | `search-artist-hit` | mac, android | none | query `moe` yields an artist hit under `search.section.artists` |   | `favorite-persists-across-relaunch` | mac, android | signed-in | favorited artist still in `sidebar.favorites.list` / `favorites.list` after relaunch |   | `no-unfavorited-in-favorites` | mac, android | signed-in | every row in the favorites list is a favorited artist |   | `next-stop-chip-focus` | mac, android | none | tapping a Next Stop artist chip changes selection to the artist, not the tour picker |   | `jam-chart-note-details` | mac, android | none | `now-playing.jam-chart-note` present with details and a source link |   | `library-phishin-playlists` | mac, android | signed-in | Library lists the phish.in account's playlists |   | `favorite-syncs-mac-to-android` | mac→android | signed-in | the favorited artist appears on the other platform |   | `favorite-syncs-android-to-mac` | android→mac | signed-in | the favorited artist appears on the other platform |   | `in-progress-syncs-android-to-mac` | android→mac | signed-in | the Android In Progress queue appears on the Mac |   | `nav-reaches-every-destination` | mac, android | none | all five `nav.*` destinations reachable and show their section identifier |   | `search-result-sections` | mac, android | none | artists/shows/tracks sections render for a query that has all three |   | `live-data-not-mockup` | mac, android | signed-in | a known current artist resolves to a real phish.in show — the #345 mockup-favorites regression guard |   Do not add journeys beyond these fifteen in this sub-issue. Adding one is a follow-up edit to   this file; the "every escaped bug adds a journey" rule is a standing practice, not a reason to   over-spec up front. - Add an appendix to `JOURNEYS.md` titled **Report grammar**, quoting #358's contract verbatim so   it is written down in the repo:   - `smoke-reports/<tag>.md` contains, anywhere, a line `Tag: <tag>` and **exactly one** line     matching `^Smoke: (PASS|FAIL)$`.   - A `PASS` report may carry any number of `Waived: <journey-id> - <reason>` lines. A journey the     report lists as failed must be covered by a `Waived:` line for `PASS` to hold.   - Any other line is ignored by the gate. Per-journey rows, screenshots, and bug links are     therefore free-form — keep the grammar this small so a hand-written report and a     runner-written one are both readable. - Also specify, in the same appendix, the **runner result-line contract** that `lib.sh` implements:   - One line per journey, tab-separated: `<platform>\t<journey-id>\t<status>\t<evidence>`.   - `status` is exactly one of `PASS`, `FAIL`, `SKIP`. `SKIP` carries a human-readable reason in     `evidence` and means the fixture wasn't available. `SKIP` is not `PASS`.   - The tag lives in a header comment of the results file (`# tag: <tag>`), not on every line.   - `evidence` is a single line, identifier-level where possible, and must never contain account     data (no artist names, no playlist names, no URLs with user-specific content). It is     committed, in a public repo. - Write `scripts/smoke/lib.sh` (`bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, `chmod +x`, header comment saying it   is sourced, not executed). Provide:   - `smoke::log` — timestamped stderr logging to a `CCTV_SMOKE_LOG` file when set, else stderr.   - `smoke::die <code> <msg>` — one-line error to stderr, exit with `<code>`.   - `smoke::preflight_macos_beta` — is "Couch Tour Beta" running? Is the invoking process allowed     Accessibility access (`osascript` System Events round-trip)? Exits **2** with the exact     remedy when not.   - `smoke::preflight_adb <serial>` — a device is attached (or `$CCTV_SMOKE_SERIAL` / first arg).     Exits **2** listing what was seen when not.   - `smoke::result <platform> <id> <status> <evidence>` — append the tab-separated line to     `$CCTV_SMOKE_RESULTS` (default stdout) and to the console.   - Exit-code convention, documented in the file header: **0** = ran to completion regardless of     verdict (the report decides pass/fail), **1** = usage error, **2** = preflight/setup failure     (app not running, no device, permission denied). A failing journey is *not* exit 2.   - `smoke::require_journeys_file` — verify `scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md` exists and that a given     journey id appears in it, so a runner can never invent a journey.   Keep it small. Both runners `source` it from `$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")` so it works from   any working directory. Do not add journey-execution logic here — that belongs to the runners. - Append a short **Journeys** section to `scripts/smoke/README.md` (created by #366) pointing at   `JOURNEYS.md` and summarizing the result-line format and exit codes in three or four lines. Do   not rewrite what #366 wrote; do not document the runners here — that is D's job, and B and C   deliberately stay out of this file so they can build concurrently. - Add a `DECISIONS.md` entry. Allocate the ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`; do not grep for   the next free number. Title it roughly **Smoke journeys assert on accessibility identifiers,   never on screen regions, and screenshots stay out of the repo.** Record:   - Pass conditions are identifier queries, so they are deterministic and cheap; pixel comparison     is rejected outright.   - The Mac side targets the accessibility tree by window owner and only synthesizes input after     confirming the beta is the frontmost process. The Android side derives tap coordinates per     run from the bounds of a node it located by tag. Hardcoded coordinates and region captures     are banned on both.   - The runner never types credentials; fixture-dependent journeys `SKIP` rather than fail.   - Failure screenshots are written under `smoke-reports/<tag>/` and gitignored. The committed     evidence is the report. This repo is public and the signed-in library, favorites, and     listening history are personal data. Test: `bash -n scripts/smoke/lib.sh` passes. `scripts/smoke/lib.sh` is not executable-as-a-script by design, so also source it in a throwaway shell and assert the helpers behave: `smoke::result mac x PASS y` writes exactly `mac\tx\tPASS\ty`; `smoke::preflight_adb` against a `CCTV_SMOKE_SERIAL` that cannot exist exits 2; `smoke::require_journeys_file bogus-id` exits non-zero. A `scripts/smoke/lib-test.sh` covering exactly these three cases is welcome but is not required. No app code changes, so `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` and `swift test` are unaffected — do not run them. ## Done when - [ ] `scripts/smoke/JOURNEYS.md` exists with exactly the fifteen ids in the table above, each with       all five fields (id, platforms, fixture, steps, pass condition), and no duplicate ids. - [ ] Every pass condition names at least one identifier that exists in `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift`       (#365) or `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt` (#364). Cross-check by name; a       condition that invents an identifier is a fail. - [ ] The nine journeys named in the original request are present by id, including both sync       directions for favorites and the Android→Mac In Progress one. - [ ] The Report grammar appendix quotes the `Tag:` / `Smoke: PASS|FAIL` / `Waived:` contract       exactly as #358 defines it. - [ ] `scripts/smoke/lib.sh` exists, is `chmod +x`, passes `bash -n`, and provides `smoke::log`,       `smoke::die`, `smoke::result`, `smoke::require_journeys_file`,       `smoke::preflight_macos_beta`, and `smoke::preflight_adb`. - [ ] The exit-code convention (0 complete / 1 usage / 2 preflight) is documented in `lib.sh`'s       header comment and in `JOURNEYS.md`. - [ ] `scripts/smoke/README.md` has a "Journeys" section that points at `JOURNEYS.md`; nothing       #366 wrote was removed or reworded. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has the entry, with its ID allocated via `mahler next-id`. - [ ] Nothing under `macos/`, `app/`, or `sync/` is touched. ## Needs a human to check - Read `JOURNEYS.md` and confirm the fifteen journeys are the ones you would actually call   "the app works". The pass conditions are mechanical, but *which* flows count as smoke is a   product call, and a journey that isn't listed is never run. This is the one review worth doing   by hand before the runners are built on top of it. ## Context - #365 defines `AXIdentifiers.swift`; #364 defines the identical Android `testTag` names in   `A11yTags.kt`. One query name, two platforms — that is what keeps the spec single-sourced. - #366 creates `scripts/smoke/README.md` and `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh`, and blocks on #365. Read   its README before appending to it; do not create a second one. - B (`run-mac.sh`) and C (`run-android.sh`) source `lib.sh` but must not edit it. If a runner   genuinely needs a new shared helper, put it in the runner file. This boundary is what lets B and   C build in the same tick without a merge conflict. - #358's promotion gate parses the report. It does not need to wait for D: it defines the   minimal contract itself, and this appendix simply records it where the runners can see it. - `DECISIONS.md` is large and append-only. Append at the end with the next allocated ID. - `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`; this sub-issue deliberately does not touch either — the   build/run documentation lands in D, once there is something to document. ## Out of scope - The runners themselves (B, C), the orchestrator and report writer (D), and the gate (#358). - The accessibility identifiers (#364, #365) and the AX dump helper (#366). - Adding journeys beyond the fifteen listed. "Every escaped bug adds a journey" applies going   forward, one bug at a time. - Any app code change. If a pass condition can't be expressed with today's identifiers, write the   condition anyway and note the gap — the missing identifier is a separate issue.

column2: scripts/smoke: bounded, identifier-scoped accessibility-tree dump for the Mac beta
column3: > **Original request:** Accessibility identifiers on key Mac/Android views for cheap agent-driven UI checks > > Agent-driven UI testing on the Mac currently relies on screenshots (token-expensive); AppleScript `entire contents` hangs because views aren't labeled. Accessibility identifiers let the smoke runner query "is there an Artists row / a Favorites section / N items" cheaply and deterministically — and improve VoiceOver. > > - Small helper in `scripts/smoke/` that dumps the AX tree of "Couch Tour Beta" scoped to those identifiers (bounded depth, no `entire contents`). Part of #360 Depends on: #365 ## Problem / goal Identifiers on their own don't help an agent: it still has to know how to reach them. Right now the only ways to inspect the running Mac app are a screenshot (expensive, non-deterministic) or `tell application "System Events" to get entire contents of ...` (hangs — that is the whole reason #365 exists). This sub-issue adds one small script that walks the accessibility tree of the running "Couch Tour Beta" **by window owner**, scoped to the identifiers from #365, with a bounded depth, and prints a compact text summary an agent can read in a few hundred tokens. ## Plan Files: - `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh` (new) - `scripts/smoke/README.md` (new) - `CLAUDE.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Create `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh` (`bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, `chmod +x`):   - Target the app **by bundle id / window owner** (`dev.mike.couchtour.mac.beta`), never by     screen region or by whatever happens to be frontmost. Fail with a clear message if it isn't     running.   - Fetch only the elements whose `AXIdentifier` is in the set declared by     `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` (parse that file at run time so the script can't drift     from the constants — that is the whole point of #365 making it the single source of truth),     plus a `--all` flag that lists every element carrying any non-empty identifier.   - Bound the walk: maximum depth (default 6, `--max-depth N` to override) and a hard timeout     (default 5s, `timeout` command or a watchdog). Never call `entire contents` on a window.   - Output one line per matched element: `<identifier>\t<role>\t<title or value>`, sorted by     identifier, so a diff between two runs is readable.   - `--identifiers-only` prints just the identifier column, for "does this row exist?" checks.   - Exit codes: 0 ran fine, 2 app not running, 3 no elements matched. - Create `scripts/smoke/README.md`: what the script is, how to install and launch the beta   (`macos/scripts/install-beta.sh`), a worked example invocation and its real output, the exit   codes, and an explicit note that this directory is shared with the smoke journey runner   (#357) — coordinate file names rather than adding a second README. - Add a `### Accessibility checks (macOS)` subsection to `CLAUDE.md` under "Building (macOS)"   with the one-line invocation, so an agent finds it without reading scripts. - Log a `DECISIONS.md` entry: **AX tree walking is bounded and identifier-scoped by   construction** — record the depth/timeout bounds, why `entire contents` is banned (it hangs on   this app), and why window-owner targeting is used instead of screen coordinates. Allocate the   ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`; do not grep for the next free number by hand. Test: `bash -n scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh` passes, `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh --help` prints usage, and the script exits 2 with the "not running" message when Couch Tour Beta is not launched. The full running-app path cannot be exercised headlessly, so that goes in "Needs a human to check" below. ## Done when - [ ] `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh` exists, is `chmod +x`, and passes `bash -n`. - [ ] `--help` prints usage; with Couch Tour Beta not running the script exits 2 with a clear message. - [ ] The identifier set is parsed from `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` at run time, not hardcoded — deleting a constant from that file removes it from the script's output. - [ ] The walk is bounded by both a max depth and a timeout; the string `entire contents` appears nowhere in the script except in a comment explaining why it is banned. - [ ] Targeting is by window owner `dev.mike.couchtour.mac.beta`, never by screen coordinates. - [ ] With Couch Tour Beta running, the script prints the Home section list and the sidebar entries as text in under 2 seconds. - [ ] `scripts/smoke/README.md` has a worked example with real pasted output. - [ ] `CLAUDE.md` and `DECISIONS.md` both record the script, with the decision ID allocated via `mahler next-id`. ## Needs a human to check - Install the beta (`macos/scripts/install-beta.sh`), launch it, and run   `scripts/smoke/ax-tree.sh`. Confirm the Home sections (In Progress, On This Date, Next Tour   Stops) and the sidebar entries all appear, and that the whole run finishes in under 2 seconds.   Paste the output into the PR body. An agent cannot do this: it needs a logged-in Mac session   with the beta app actually running. ## Context - Bounding the walk is the difference between this working and hanging. `entire contents` on   "Couch Tour Beta" is the exact call that motivated #365, so the ban belongs in the code as a   comment, not just in the issue. - `scripts/smoke/` is new — it does not exist yet. #357 (journey spec + agent runner) also   creates files in it. The two are labelled `area:smoke` so the scheduler won't run them   concurrently; keep file names distinct and read `scripts/smoke/README.md` before adding to it. - `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md` — edit only `CLAUDE.md`. - The Android equivalent (`adb shell uiautomator dump` plus `uiautomator` node filtering) belongs   to #357's runner and to the `testTag`s from #362. Don't build it here; this script is Mac-only,   matching the original acceptance criterion. ## Out of scope - The journey spec and the smoke runner itself (#357). - Gating `promote-beta.sh` on a passing smoke report (#358). - Any Android-specific tooling. - Screen capture, click synthesis, or frontmost-gated input — the runner's job, not this script's.

column2: macOS: stable accessibilityIdentifier values on sidebar, Home, search, and jam chart note
column3: > **Original request:** Accessibility identifiers on key Mac/Android views for cheap agent-driven UI checks > > Agent-driven UI testing on the Mac currently relies on screenshots (token-expensive); AppleScript `entire contents` hangs because views aren't labeled. Accessibility identifiers let the smoke runner query "is there an Artists row / a Favorites section / N items" cheaply and deterministically — and improve VoiceOver. > > - Add `.accessibilityIdentifier` (and labels where missing) to key Mac views: sidebar entries, favorites list, Home sections (In Progress, On This Date, Next Tour Stop), search result sections (artists/shows/tracks), Now Playing jam chart note. > - Android: ensure matching `testTag`/contentDescription on the same elements for uiautomator. > - Small helper in `scripts/smoke/` that dumps the AX tree of "Couch Tour Beta" scoped to those identifiers (bounded depth, no `entire contents`). Part of #360 ## Problem / goal Agent-driven UI checks on the Mac currently can only take screenshots and look at them, which burns tokens and is non-deterministic. AppleScript `entire contents` against "Couch Tour Beta" hangs because nothing in the view tree carries a stable identifier, so there is no way to ask "is there an Artists row / a Favorites section / how many items" without pixels. This sub-issue adds stable `.accessibilityIdentifier` values to the key macOS views. That makes the tree queryable by the AX dump helper (#366) and improves VoiceOver as a side effect. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` (new) - `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/HomeView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/SearchView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ThreePaneRootView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/DesignSystem/SectionHeader.swift` - `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh` (new) Steps: - Create `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` as the single source of truth: an `enum AXID`   (or similar) of `String` constants. No identifier string literal is written anywhere else.   `macos/project.yml` globs `macos/CouchTour` as a source path, so the new file is picked up   automatically — do not regenerate the project for this. - Add these constants and apply them:   - `sidebar.nav.home` / `.search` / `.library` / `.history` / `.settings` — each     `SidebarNavItem` in `SidebarView.swift`. `SidebarNavItem` already takes `title`, so derive     the identifier from a new `id` parameter rather than string-matching the title.   - `sidebar.favorites.header`, `sidebar.favorites.list`, `sidebar.favorites.row.<artistKey>`,     `sidebar.sync.footer` — `SidebarView.swift`.   - `home.section.in-progress` (+ `.in-progress.row.<queueKey>`), `home.section.next-tour-stops`     (+ `.row.<showKey>`), `home.section.on-this-date` (+ `.row.<showKey>`) — `HomeView.swift`.
