Tag the section *container* (the `VStack`/`ScrollView` that holds the header + cards), not     the header `Text`, so a query can count the children.   - `search.section.artists` / `.shows` / `.tracks` / `.songs`, `search.tab.<tab>`,     `search.results` — `SearchView.swift`.   - `now-playing.jam-chart-note` and `now-playing.jam-chart-note.dismiss` — on `JamChartNoteCard`     in `DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift`, so both `PlayerRailView` and `ExpandedNowPlayingView`     get it for free.   - `ThreePaneRootView.swift`: keep the existing `.accessibilityLabel`s and add     `app.search-field` / `app.search-clear` identifiers alongside them. - Give `SectionHeader` an optional `identifier: String?` parameter. Apply the modifier **only   when the value is non-nil** (branch in the `body`, don't use   `.accessibilityIdentifier(identifier ?? "")`) so untagged headers don't contribute empty   identifiers that show up as noise in the AX tree. - Write `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh`: extract every string constant declared in   `AXIdentifiers.swift`, then assert each one's value is actually referenced somewhere under   `macos/CouchTour/`. Exit 1 and print the unreferenced constant names if any. This is the   regression guard that stops a rename or a deleted view from silently orphaning a constant. - Add a `## Accessibility identifiers` note to `CLAUDE.md` documenting the naming convention   (`<surface>.<element>[.<variant>]`, lower-case, dot-separated) and pointing at   `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh`. - Do not add a `DECISIONS.md` entry for this; it introduces no architectural decision. (The   dump helper in #366 records the one that does.) Test: `bash macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh` exits 0, and `xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` succeeds after `cd macos && xcodegen generate`. Neither runs in CI (the Mac app target needs local signing and `macos-tests.yml` only covers `CouchTourKit`), so paste both command outputs in the PR body. ## Done when - [ ] `macos/CouchTour/AXIdentifiers.swift` exists and is the only place identifier strings are declared. - [ ] Every constant in it is applied at least once, and `macos/scripts/check-ax-ids.sh` exits 0. - [ ] The script exits 1 with the offending constant names when one is deliberately made unreferenced (verify by hand, then revert). - [ ] Sidebar nav items, favorites header/list/rows, all three Home sections, all four search sections/tabs, and the jam chart note all carry identifiers. - [ ] No existing `.accessibilityLabel` was removed or reworded; VoiceOver output is unchanged except for the added identifiers. - [ ] `xcodebuild ... build` for the `CouchTour` scheme succeeds, output pasted in the PR body. - [ ] `CLAUDE.md` documents the naming convention and the check script. ## Needs a human to check - Launch the Mac beta, turn on VoiceOver, and walk Home → sidebar → Search. Confirm the new   identifiers did not make VoiceOver read anything twice or swallow an existing label   (e.g. "In progress — open History", "Dismiss jam chart note"). This is the one thing an   agent cannot verify from the source tree. ## Context - The Mac app target has **no** UI test target: `macos/project.yml` defines only the `CouchTour`   and `CouchTourBeta` application targets, and `macos-tests.yml` runs `swift test` over   `CouchTourKit` alone (which never sees these views). Hence the source-level check script   rather than a unit test — same reason D208's "swift test doesn't cover the app UI" note exists. - `.accessibilityIdentifier` is a no-op visually, so there is no screenshot-diff risk here. - Sibling sub-issues: #364 (same identifiers on Android, as Compose `testTag`) and #366 (the   `scripts/smoke/` AX-dump helper that queries these). This sub-issue blocks #366. - `UAT.md` is deliberately **not** in the file list: it is appended to by nearly every issue in   the backlog and listing it would make the scheduler block unrelated builds. Put the   human-check item in the PR description instead. ## Out of scope - Any change to layout, styling, copy, or navigation behaviour. - The Google TV surface (`TvMainActivity`) and `TvBrowse.kt` / `TvNowPlaying.kt`. - The `CouchTourKit` package (it has no SwiftUI views). - The `scripts/smoke/` AX-dump helper (#366) and the journey spec/runner (#357). - Wiring a check script into `macos-tests.yml` — that workflow only triggers on   `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/**` paths and would need its own CI decision.

column2: Android: stable testTag values on nav, Home sections, favorites, and search results
column3: > **Original request:** Accessibility identifiers on key Mac/Android views for cheap agent-driven UI checks > > Agent-driven UI testing on the Mac currently relies on screenshots (token-expensive); AppleScript `entire contents` hangs because views aren't labeled. Accessibility identifiers let the smoke runner query "is there an Artists row / a Favorites section / N items" cheaply and deterministically — and improve VoiceOver. > > - Add `.accessibilityIdentifier` (and labels where missing) to key Mac views: sidebar entries, favorites list, Home sections (In Progress, On This Date, Next Tour Stop), search result sections (artists/shows/tracks), Now Playing jam chart note. > - Android: ensure matching `testTag`/contentDescription on the same elements for uiautomator. Part of #360 ## Problem / goal `adb shell uiautomator dump` returns nodes with no stable handles, so an agent can only assert on user-visible text — which changes with copy, locale, and truncation, and can't distinguish "the section is missing" from "the section is present but empty". Compose's `Modifier.testTag` is the Android equivalent of the macOS `.accessibilityIdentifier` and is what `onNodeWithTag` / uiautomator's `resource-id` actually keys on. This sub-issue adds matching tags to the key Android screens, and locks them in with a Robolectric Compose test so a refactor can't silently drop one. The tag names deliberately mirror the macOS identifier names (see #365) so one query script can be written against both. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt` (new) - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt` (new) Steps: - Create `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTags.kt` as the single source of truth: an   `object A11yTags` of `String` constants plus small `fun` helpers for the parameterized ones   (e.g. `fun homeRow(queueKey: String) = "home.section.in-progress.row.$queueKey"`). No tag   string literal is written anywhere else. - Use exactly the same names as the macOS `AXIdentifiers.swift` from #365:   - `nav.home` / `nav.search` / `nav.library` / `nav.history` / `nav.settings` — the     `BottomNavItem`s in `LedgerBottomBar` (`MainActivity.kt:4284`). Android has a bottom bar,     not a sidebar, so these are the closest counterpart to the Mac's `sidebar.nav.*`.   - `home.section.in-progress` (+ `.row.<queueKey>`), `home.section.next-tour-stops`     (+ `.row.<showKey>`), `home.section.on-this-date` (+ `.row.<showKey>`) — `HomeScreen`     (`MainActivity.kt:322`). Tag the section `item { }` block's container, not the header     `Text`, so a query can count the children.   - `favorites.list` and `favorites.row.<artistKey>` for the favorited-artists list/rows where     `HomeScreen` renders them.   - `search.section.artists` / `.shows` / `.tracks` and `search.results` — `SearchScreen`. - Apply with `Modifier.testTag(...)` (`androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag`), which   `ui-test-junit4` reads via `onNodeWithTag` and uiautomator reads as `resource-id`. - Where a node has an icon-only meaning, keep or add a `contentDescription` alongside the tag;   a tag is not a substitute for a label, and TalkBack still needs the label. - Write `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/A11yTagsTest.kt` as a Robolectric Compose test   using `createComposeRule`, following the existing pattern in   `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/ArtistScreenTest.kt` (the test deps   `androidx.ui.test.junit4` + `debugImplementation androidx.ui.test.manifest` are already   declared in `app/build.gradle.kts` — don't add new ones). Test that:   - every constant in `A11yTags` is non-blank and has no trailing/leading whitespace;   - the `home.section.*` constants each appear in a small `Column` fixture under     `createComposeRule().setContent { }`, proving `onNodeWithTag(..., useUnmergedTree = true)`     resolves against a tagged node;   - the parameterized helpers produce the expected `prefix.value` strings. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests 'dev.mike.couchtour.A11yTagsTest'` passes, and the full `testDebugUnitTest` suite is still green. ## Done when - [ ] `A11yTags.kt` exists and is the only place tag strings are declared. - [ ] `A11yTagsTest` passes under `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. - [ ] The full `testDebugUnitTest` suite passes with no new failures. - [ ] `LedgerBottomBar`'s five items, the three Home sections, the favorites list/rows, and the search result sections all carry tags. - [ ] Tag names are character-for-character identical to the macOS constants in #365 for every shared surface (`nav.*`, `home.section.*`, `search.section.*`). - [ ] No existing `contentDescription` was removed or reworded. ## Needs a human to check - Install the beta APK, open TalkBack, and swipe through Home and the bottom bar. Confirm no   element now reads its tag out loud or announces a label twice. This is the one thing an agent   cannot verify from the source tree. ## Context - The Android app is a single-module Compose UI: the bottom bar, `HomeScreen` and `SearchScreen`   all live in `MainActivity.kt` (4668 lines). Keep the tag constants in their own file so the   string vocabulary is greppable without wading through that file. - Robolectric Compose tests are already proven here — `ArtistScreenTest.kt` uses   `createComposeRule`; don't invent a new harness. - Google TV (`TvBrowse.kt`, `TvNowPlaying.kt`) is a separate surface with no uiautomator story;   out of scope. - The jam chart note is Mac-only today; #355 (placeholder text, still `mahler:inbox`) owns the   Android side. Don't add a `now-playing.jam-chart-note` tag for a UI that doesn't exist. - `UAT.md` is deliberately not in the file list — it's appended to by nearly every issue and   listing it would make the scheduler block unrelated builds. Put the human-check item in the PR   description instead. ## Out of scope - Any change to layout, styling, copy, or navigation behaviour. - The Google TV surface and `TvMainActivity`. - `uiautomator dump` plumbing and the smoke runner (#357) — this sub-issue only makes the nodes   addressable. - Fixing #355's placeholder jam chart text.

column2: macOS: tour picker is unreachable — nothing ever assigns HomeView.tourPickerArtist
column3: > **Original request:** "Check macOS parity: the Mac card is a list with no chips, but check its tour-picker entry point." (from #354, Android: Next Tour Stop artist chips open the tour picker instead of switching focus) ## Problem / goal Split out of #354's "check macOS parity" step. The check found a real bug: the macOS tour picker is unreachable dead UI. `HomeView.swift:25` declares `@State var tourPickerArtist: ArtistRef?`. It is read by the `.sheet(item:)` at `HomeView.swift:69-76` and passed to `TourPickerSheet` at `:75` — and it is never assigned. A repo-wide search for `tourPickerArtist =` matches only the four Android sites (`MainActivity.kt:495, 750, 753, 757`); nothing in `macos/` ever sets it. `TourPickerSheet` (`macos/CouchTour/Browse/TourPickerSheet.swift`, 252 lines) therefore can never be presented, and the "Save → `NextStop.resetCache()` → `reloadDiscovery()`" refresh path it exists to provide (D200/#100) is dead too. So on macOS a user currently **cannot set a tour/year preference for any artist**. That preference is what `NextStop.tourFor` (`CouchTourKit/NextStop.swift:71-116`) consults to track a defunct or non-touring artist — the feature #68 shipped. Android reaches it through the Home card's artist chips (which #354 is fixing to mean "focus", moving tour-picking to a `Change tour…` action). macOS has no equivalent entry point at all: the card at `HomeView.swift:291-354` is a `prefix(3)` list of rows with only a "Favorite artists" `NavigationLink` in its header (`:317-326`). **Decision recorded here (technical, no owner input needed):** the entry point goes on the macOS card's existing artist row, not in a chip row (macOS has no chips and the card is intentionally a list of up to three shows rather than Android's single focused show). `tourStopRow(_:)` (`HomeView.swift:356-412`) gains a secondary "Track tour…" affordance, and a context-menu item on the same row so the action is reachable without widening the row. The builder picks the concrete control after reading the row's layout; the requirement is that every artist row in the card can present `TourPickerSheet`, and that the existing `TourPickerSheet` and `ProgressStore` paths are reused unchanged. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/HomeView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/Browse/TourPickerSheet.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/ProgressStoreTests.swift` - `UAT.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: 1. Read `HomeView.swift:291-412` and confirm the finding: `tourPickerArtist` is read at `:69-76` and `:75`, declared at `:25`, and assigned nowhere in `macos/`. Verify with a search over `macos/` for `tourPickerArtist` — every hit is a read or a declaration. Record the result in a comment on this issue before changing code, so the dead-UI claim is on the record even if a later fix removes it. 2. Add the entry point in `tourStopRow(_:)`. A secondary text control ("Track tour…") and/or a `.contextMenu` item, both setting `tourPickerArtist = show.artist`. Follow whatever secondary-control pattern `LedgerDesign.swift` already provides rather than introducing new styling tokens. 3. Add a `Dnnn` entry to `DECISIONS.md` (allocate with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`) recording that the macOS tour-picker entry point is per-artist-row, and that the sheet itself is unchanged from #68. 4. Add a `UAT.md` item with the next free `uat-NNN` id for the owner-only check. Test: what proves it - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` still passes at 448. - `ProgressStoreTests.swift:303-385` (tour-preference CRUD) still passes unchanged — the persistence path is reused, not rewritten. - A test that the row's action assigns `tourPickerArtist` for that row's artist. column2: Isolated test sync group for smoke runs (playback without polluting real history)
column3: > **Original request:** Isolated test sync group for smoke runs (playback without polluting real history) — Beta clients are in the owner's real sync group, so smoke tests can't play audio or test handoff/In Progress without polluting real listening history. This was the biggest limit on the 2026-09-29 test round. > - A dedicated smoke/test sync group (or test account) the beta can be pointed at for test runs, with a documented way to switch it in and out (e.g. a debug setting or launch arg on Mac and an intent extra / debug menu on Android). > - A cleanup step that wipes the test group's data after a run. > - Must never touch prod sync data; never deploy sync by hand (CI only). ## Problem / goal The Mac and Android betas are paired into the owner's real sync group, so every smoke run (`scripts/smoke/`, see #357/#358) that plays audio or checks the In Progress handoff writes throwaway history into the real group. That was the single biggest limit on the 2026-09-29 test round. Goal: give the beta builds a sync backend they can be pointed at that is isolated from prod data, with a documented switch, plus a one-command cleanup of whatever the run left behind. ## Plan **Decision (made here, do not re-litigate): the isolated environment is the existing staging Cloudflare Worker, not a hand-made group inside prod.** `sync/wrangler.toml:38` already defines `[env.staging]` with its own D1 (`couch-tour-sync-staging`, separate `database_id`), it already runs the same migrations, and `sync-deploy.yml:66` already smoke-tests it over raw HTTP. A group created there is disposable, so "wipe the test group" becomes "wipe a throwaway database" instead of "carefully delete one group out of prod". Consequence: **no change to `sync/` at all** — same protocol, same pairing flow, different base URL. Second decision: **beta points at staging by default**, with a documented override back to prod for when the owner wants the betas on the real group. A beta that can silently write to real listening history is the exact problem being fixed; prod clients (`release` Android build, non-`BETA` Mac target) are untouched. Third decision: **switching hosts clears the local sync token store.** A bearer token issued by prod is meaningless to staging, so sending it would just 401 — and a staging token must never be presented to prod. Cleared on change, the app comes up unpaired and pairs fresh against the new host, which is also what gives each smoke run a clean group. Files: - `app/build.gradle.kts` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Sync.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CouchTourApp.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SyncTest.kt` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Sync.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/AppModel.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/SyncTests.swift` - `scripts/smoke-sync-reset.sh` - `scripts/test_smoke_sync_reset.sh` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - [ ] Android `app/build.gradle.kts`: add a `buildConfigField` for the sync base URL — staging host       on `buildTypes.debug` (this is also the `-PsideInstall=true` beta build), prod host on       `buildTypes.release`. Name it `SYNC_BASE_URL`. Confirm `buildConfig = true` is already on       (`app/build.gradle.kts:114`). - [ ] `Sync.kt`: give `SyncApi` (line 117) a public entry point that applies an override, e.g.       `applyConfiguredBaseUrl(BuildConfig.SYNC_BASE_URL, override: String?)`, which parses the URL,       sets `baseUrl`, and — when the host differs from the host the current token was issued for —       clears `SyncTokenStore` (persist the issuing host next to the token; no schema change, this       is `EncryptedSharedPreferences`, not Room). Keep `internal var baseUrl` so existing tests       keep working unchanged. - [ ] `CouchTourApp.kt`: apply the configured base URL once at process start, before `SyncSession.init`. - [ ] `MainActivity.kt`: honour an intent extra (alongside the existing       `EXTRA_OPEN_NOW_PLAYING` precedent at line 151) that overrides the base URL for that launch,       so the owner can `adb shell am start … --es syncBaseUrl https://couch-tour-sync…` to flip a       beta back to prod without a rebuild. - [ ] macOS `Sync.swift`: add the resolution logic **in CouchTourKit, not the app target** — the       app target has no test coverage, so the logic must be unit-testable. e.g.       `SyncConfig.resolveBaseURL(defaultBase:arguments:environment:)` reading `--sync-base-url=<url>`       from `CommandLine.arguments` and `COUCHTOUR_SYNC_BASE_URL` from the environment, with args       > env > default. `SyncAPI.baseURL` is already `public static var` (line 190). - [ ] `macos/CouchTour/AppModel.swift`: under the existing `#if BETA` block (line 25, which already       isolates the beta's Keychain service and GRDB directory), set       `SyncAPI.baseURL = SyncConfig.resolveBaseURL(defaultBase: stagingHost, …)` before the       `SyncSession` is constructed. The non-beta `CouchTour` target must not change. - [ ] `scripts/smoke-sync-reset.sh`: empty the staging D1 — `progress`, `devices`, `pairings`,       `seqs`, `groups` — via `wrangler d1 execute couch-tour-sync-staging --remote`. Hard guard:       refuse to run unless the resolved database name is exactly `couch-tour-sync-staging`, and       require an explicit `--yes` for the remote write. Default to printing the commands       (dry run), matching the safety posture of the other `scripts/*.sh` in this repo. - [ ] `scripts/test_smoke_sync_reset.sh`: assert the guard rejects the prod database name and the       prod database id from `sync/wrangler.toml`, and that dry-run emits the expected statements. - [ ] `README.md`: document the switch — which build/config points where, the Mac launch arg, the       Android intent extra, and the reset command. Update test counts for any new tests. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md`: new entry (allocate the ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`, do not grep)       recording the staging-as-test-group decision, the beta-defaults-to-staging decision, and the       clear-token-on-host-change rule. Test: what proves it - Android: `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SyncTest.kt` — `BuildConfig.SYNC_BASE_URL` for   the debug variant is the staging host; `applyConfiguredBaseUrl` honours an override; switching   to a host that differs from the token's issuing host clears the token store; re-applying the   same host does not clear it; a malformed override URL is ignored (falls back to the configured   default) rather than crashing at startup.   Run: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` - macOS: `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/SyncTests.swift` — launch arg beats   env var beats default; empty/garbage values fall back to the default.   Run: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` - Script: `scripts/test_smoke_sync_reset.sh` (guard + dry run). - `sync/` is untouched: `cd sync && npm run typecheck && npm test` still green. ## Done when - [ ] The debug/beta Android build sends sync traffic to `https://couch-tour-sync-staging.mkastellec.workers.dev`; the release build's configured URL is still the prod host. - [ ] `CouchTourBeta` (macOS) resolves the staging host under `BETA`; the non-beta `CouchTour` target is byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour. - [ ] `--sync-base-url=<url>` (Mac) and the `syncBaseUrl` intent extra (Android) override the host in either direction, and this is written up in `README.md` with copy-pasteable examples for both. - [ ] Changing the host clears the local sync token store; the app comes up unpaired against the new host rather than replaying a token from the old one. - [ ] `scripts/smoke-sync-reset.sh` refuses to run against the prod D1 name or id, and empties staging when run with `--yes`. - [ ] `scripts/test_smoke_sync_reset.sh` passes and covers that refusal. - [ ] All three test commands above pass, and `sync/` is unchanged (`git diff --stat sync/` is empty). - [ ] A `DECISIONS.md` entry exists with an ID allocated via `mahler next-id`. ## Needs a human to check - The actual round trip: install both betas, pair Mac beta with Android beta **against staging**,   play a track on Mac, confirm it shows up In Progress on Android — and confirm the real prod group   gained no rows. Automated tests can prove the host resolves; only the owner can confirm the run   behaves and that real history stayed clean. - Whether beta should stay pointed at staging by default, or be reverted to prod-with-a-flag once   the smoke harness is comfortable. The default here favours smoke safety. ## Context - The group is never client-supplied: the Worker resolves `Authorization: Bearer <token>` →   `devices.tokenHash` → `device.groupId` (`sync/src/auth.ts:19`). There is no group id on the   client, and no admin/reset endpoint. So "point the app at a test group" can only be done by   changing the base URL, not by setting a group. - Beta already has isolated *local* storage: Android by `applicationIdSuffix = ".beta"`   (`app/build.gradle.kts:86`), macOS by the `BETA` Keychain service and GRDB directory   (`AppModel.swift:25`, `:73`). What beta does not have is isolation on the *server*. - `scripts/cut-beta.sh` builds both betas; it injects no config and needs no change. - The staging D1 is also used by the CI smoke test in `sync-deploy.yml:66`, which already leaves a   throwaway group per run and documents that as acceptable growth. Resetting staging wholesale is   strictly cleaner than that. - Related: #357 (smoke journeys + runners), #358 (promote gate), #360 (accessibility identifiers).   Those runners should need no changes — a beta that points at staging by default is already in   the right state for a smoke run. ## Out of scope - Any change under `sync/` — no new wipe/admin endpoint, no protocol change, no migration. Use the   existing staging environment. - A separate phish.in / Relisten account, or any new credentials. Auth is unchanged. - Automating pairing or the reset inside CI. This is a human-driven smoke tool. - Changing prod clients (Android `release`, macOS non-`BETA` `CouchTour`). - A settings-screen toggle. The launch-arg / intent-extra switch is the documented interface; a   UI toggle is a follow-up if the owner asks for one.

column2: Audit Ledger redesign (#133/D214) for leftover mockup data and dropped/miswired features
column3: > **Original request:** Follow-up to beta UAT 2026-09-29. Most regressions found that day trace to the Ledger design-system change, `2a6b2cc` "Implement Ledger design system across Android and macOS" (#128, D214, #133, 2026-09-04). It left design-mockup placeholders in shipping code and dropped or miswired pre-existing features: > > - #347: hardcoded mockup favorites (Goose, WSP…) in `SidebarView.swift` > - #355: hardcoded jam-chart note text; Android badge on every track > - #348: macOS sidebar lost the Artists destination > - #349: macOS search stopped rendering artist results > - #354: Android Next Tour Stop chips wired to the tour picker instead of focus > - Seen in passing: macOS fake `TrafficLights()` view drawn under the real window controls (two sets of traffic lights), unlabeled icon buttons (no accessibility names), and Phish showing "0" shows in the sidebar. > > **Task:** a systematic audit of everything `2a6b2cc` (and its follow-ups #153/D221 and #157) touched, on both platforms. Deliverable: one checklist comment on this issue, then a separate issue per finding (don't fix inline). Look for: > 1. **Mockup data in shipping code:** string or numeric literals standing in for real data (names, counts, dates, "just now", sample notes, fallback lists). Grep for hardcoded artist names, `fallback`, `sample`, `mock`, `placeholder`, and literal counts inside view code. > 2. **Lost features:** diff the pre-redesign navigation, search and Home against the current versions (`git show 2a6b2cc^:<file>`). List every entry point, action or result type that existed before and is now missing or only reachable by shortcut. > 3. **Miswired actions:** controls whose tap/click does something other than what their label or styling implies. > 4. **Accessibility:** icon-only buttons without labels (macOS AX description, Android contentDescription). > 5. **Cosmetic duplication:** the fake window chrome and similar. > > Record the result as a UAT/DECISIONS note so future design passes keep a "no mockup data in shipping code" rule. ## Problem / goal The Ledger redesign (`2a6b2cc`, #133/D214) and its follow-ups (#153/D221 `28fa02c`, #157 `c0c0912`) rewrote navigation, Home, Now Playing and the design system on both platforms. Five concrete regressions from it are already filed (#347, #348, #349, #354, #355), but they were found by eye during one beta UAT pass. Nobody has systematically compared pre- and post-redesign surfaces, so there is no way to know whether the list of five is complete. This issue produces that comparison once, as a written artifact, plus one filed issue per new finding. It fixes nothing inline. The artifact is the input to a durable rule ("no mockup data in shipping code") so the next design pass cannot reintroduce the same class of defect. **Decision (recorded here, technical, no owner input needed):** the audit lands as a new markdown report under `docs/` (matching `docs/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT.md` and `docs/MODEL_PARITY_AUDIT.md`), a `Dnnn` entry in `DECISIONS.md` carrying the rule, and `uat-NNN` check items in `UAT.md` for anything only the owner can confirm by using the app. No source file is modified by this issue. ## Plan Files: - `docs/LEDGER_REDESIGN_AUDIT.md` (new) - `DECISIONS.md` - `UAT.md` Steps: 1. Establish the audit surface. Get the file lists of `2a6b2cc` (`git show --stat 2a6b2cc`), `28fa02c` (#153/D221) and `c0c0912` (#157), and union them. For each file, read both the pre-redesign version (`git show 2a6b2cc^:<file>`) and the version at HEAD. The surface is roughly: Android `MainActivity.kt`, `NowPlaying.kt`, `DesignComponents.kt`, `LibraryScreen.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`, `Theme.kt`, `ArtistAbbreviations.kt`; macOS `SidebarView.swift`, `ThreePaneRootView.swift`, `SearchView.swift`, `HomeView.swift`, `PlayerRailView.swift`, `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift`, `WaveformScrubber.swift`, `DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift`, `Browse/ShowDetailView.swift`, `LocalPlaylistsView.swift`. 2. Mockup-data sweep. Grep the surface for hardcoded artist/band names, `showCount:` literals, sample/fallback/mock/placeholder identifiers, literal counts in view code, and static date strings ("just now", "Today", hardcoded `YYYY-MM-DD`). Known instances to confirm and cite (do not re-file): `SidebarView.swift:17-22` (`goose`, `grateful-dead`, `widespread-panic` fallback list), `DesignComponents.kt:308-340` (`JamChartNoteCard` sample note text), `NowPlaying.kt:390-450` (JAM CHART badge shown unconditionally, and again at `MainActivity.kt:4079`), and the owner's observed Phish row rendering "0" shows (locate where `SidebarView` renders `ArtistRef.showCount` and whether a zero can reach it). Every hit goes in the report with `file:line`. 3. Lost-feature diff. Per surface file, list the entry points, actions and result types present at `2a6b2cc^` and missing or shortcut-only now. Cover at minimum: macOS sidebar destinations (the Artists row — see #348), macOS search result types (artists/shows/tracks/venues — see #349), Android Home sections (Next Tour Stops, On This Date, Continue Listening, Surprise Me) and their tap targets, Android navigation entries and the TV surface, and macOS Browse/Show/Local-Playlists entry points. Confirm #348 and #349 by diff, not by re-deriving. 4. Miswired-action sweep. For each control in the surface, compare the action its label/styling implies with what the handler does. Known instance: Android Next Tour Stop artist chips (see #354). Also check the JAM CHART badge/`jamChartOnly` chip on both platforms, favorite star toggles, and every settings row in `SettingsScreen.kt` / `PlaybackSettingsView.swift`. 5. Accessibility sweep. List every icon-only control in the surface that has no `contentDescription` (Android) or `.accessibilityLabel`/AX description (macOS). Group them into one filed issue per platform — a single finding per icon is noise, one per platform surface is a buildable PR. 6. Cosmetic-duplication sweep. Confirm the fake `TrafficLights()` from `DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift:227` rendered inside the real window chrome at `SidebarView.swift:39` and `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:53`, and look for siblings of the same kind (duplicate headers, duplicate controls, doubled empty-state art). 7. Write `docs/LEDGER_REDESIGN_AUDIT.md`: one section per finding class, each finding with `file:line`, what the pre-redesign behaviour was, and severity (data-affecting > visible-wrong > cosmetic). Close with the short list of things checked and found clean, so a later pass knows what was covered. 8. File one issue per **new** finding. Each new issue gets the standard body shape (`## Problem / goal`, `## Plan` with `Files:` and `Steps:`, `Test:`, `## Done when`, `## Needs a human to check`, `## Context`, `## Out of scope`), one `type:bug`/`type:chore` label, one `size:s`/`size:m` label, and `p1` only for data-affecting findings. Never add `mahler:*` labels. The five already-filed findings (#347, #348, #349, #354, #355) are **not** re-filed — instead record, in the checklist comment, whether each is still open and still unfixed at HEAD, and link it in the report. 9. Post one checklist comment on this issue: the finding list with its filed issue numbers (or "already filed as #N"), each tagged confirmed/still-unfixed or fixed-at-HEAD. 10. Log the rule: run `mahler next-id couch-tour D` for the next sequential ID and append a `Dnnn` entry to `DECISIONS.md` stating the rule (no literal sample data, fallback artist lists, placeholder counts or decorative window chrome in shipping code; design mockups live in `design/`) and recording the audit's location and finding count. 11. Add a `UAT.md` section for this batch, with new `uat-NNN` ids (never reused, next free number continues the existing series), covering the checks only the owner can perform: the double traffic lights, unlabeled icon buttons via VoiceOver/TalkBack, and the `0 shows` sidebar count. Test: what proves it - Docs-only diff: `git diff --stat main...HEAD` lists only `docs/LEDGER_REDESIGN_AUDIT.md`, `DECISIONS.md` and `UAT.md`. No `.kt`/`.swift` file is modified — if one is, the scope was violated. - The report cites `file:line` for every finding, and each cited line is greppable at HEAD (`grep -n "<literal>" <file>` reproduces it). - Every "lost feature" claim names a symbol or entry point that exists at `2a6b2cc^` and is absent at HEAD, verifiable with `git show 2a6b2cc^:<file> | grep <symbol>` returning a hit and `grep -rn <symbol> app/ macos/` not returning one. - The checklist comment lists every finding and points at a real issue number, and `gh issue view` on each shows the full body shape and correct labels. - Suites unchanged and still green (Android 668, `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`; macOS 448, `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test`). ## Done when - [ ] `docs/LEDGER_REDESIGN_AUDIT.md` committed, covering all five finding classes across every file in the union of `2a6b2cc`, `28fa02c`, `c0c0912`, with `file:line` citations and an explicit "checked, clean" list - [ ] Each of the five known findings (#347, #348, #349, #354, #355) is confirmed or marked fixed-at-HEAD in the report, and none of them is re-filed as a new issue - [ ] At least one new issue filed per genuine new finding, each with the full body shape, one `type:` label, one `size:s`/`size:m` label, and a p-label - [ ] One checklist comment posted on this issue listing every finding with its issue number (or the existing number) - [ ] `Dnnn` entry appended to `DECISIONS.md` stating the "no mockup data in shipping code" rule, with its ID allocated via `mahler next-id couch-tour D` - [ ] New `UAT.md` section with fresh `uat-NNN` ids for the owner-only checks (double traffic lights, unlabeled icon buttons, `0 shows` count) - [ ] `git diff --stat` shows no source-file changes; Android 668 / macOS 448 tests pass ## Needs a human to check - Whether the two sets of macOS traffic lights are actually both visible in the shipped window (agent cannot see pixels). - Whether icon-only buttons are unlabelled in practice — needs VoiceOver (macOS) and TalkBack (Android) on the real app. - Whether the `0 shows` Phish row in the sidebar is a display bug or correct for an account with no phish.in data. - Whether any other surface the audit missed shows a visual regression the agent could not detect from source. ## Context - Redesign commits: `2a6b2cc` (#128/#133, D214 — Android `MainActivity.kt` +780, `NowPlaying.kt` +599, `DesignComponents.kt` +274, `LibraryScreen.kt` +387, `SettingsScreen.kt` +303, `Theme.kt` +204; macOS `SidebarView.swift`, `ThreePaneRootView.swift`, `PlayerRailView.swift`, `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift`, `WaveformScrubber.swift`, `DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift`), `28fa02c` (#153, D221), `c0c0912` (#157). - Known mockup literals, for confirmation not discovery: `SidebarView.swift:17-22`, `DesignComponents.kt:308-340`, `NowPlaying.kt:390-450`, `MainActivity.kt:4079`, `DesignSystem/LedgerDesign.swift:227` used at `SidebarView.swift:39` and `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:53`. - House style for audit reports: `docs/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT.md`, `docs/MODEL_PARITY_AUDIT.md`; older root-level ones are `android_dead_code_audit.md`, `macos_dead_code_audit.md`. New report goes in `docs/`. - `design/` holds the branding/handoff mockups — the place mockup literals should have come from. - This is an audit of a 2026-09-04 change; current HEAD has drifted well past it, so re-verify each finding against HEAD before filing. - Related sibling issues in flight: #347, #348, #349, #354, #355 (the known findings), #345 (macOS data stores). ## Out of scope - Fixing anything found. Every finding becomes its own issue; none is fixed in this run. - Auditing changes made after the Ledger redesign beyond what those three commits touched, and the `sync/` backend entirely. - Any change to the design system itself, navigation structure, or the five already-filed issues' fixes. - Android Auto / Google TV surface beyond confirming the redesign did not drop a TV entry point.

column2: Android: Next Tour Stop artist chips open the tour picker instead of switching focus
column3: > **Original request:** Reported by the owner (Android v0.78) and reproduced on a beta built from `main` (emulator, UAT 2026-09-29). > > **Repro:** favorite Phish and moe. On Home → NEXT TOUR STOP, tap the "moe." chip. The "Track tour for moe." year/tour picker dialog opens. Expected: the card switches its focus to moe.'s next stop. > > **Cause:** `MainActivity.kt:495`, where every favorite-artist chip is `.clickable { tourPickerArtist = artist }`. There is no focused-artist state. `nextStop` (line 360) is always `oldestUnplayed(...)` across all favorites, and the chip's "selected" styling only reflects whichever artist that happens to be. This came in with the Ledger redesign (#133, D214). > > **Fix:** > - Tapping a chip sets a remembered focused artist, and `nextStop` filters to that artist's candidates. Default to the current behavior when nothing is focused. > - Move "track a tour" to its own affordance (a long-press on the chip, or a "Change tour…" action on the card). > - Check macOS parity: the Mac card is a list with no chips, but check its tour-picker entry point. ## Problem / goal The artist chips in the Android Home "NEXT TOUR STOP" card do the one thing they should not. Tapping a chip is wired to `tourPickerArtist = artist` (`MainActivity.kt:495`), which opens the year/tour dialog. Nothing in the app records which artist the user is looking at, so the card itself can never change: `nextStop` (`:360-362`) is always `oldestUnplayed(allCandidates, played)` across every favorited artist, and a chip's "selected" styling (`:482`) is derived from whichever artist happened to win that cross-artist pick. The chips read as a selector and are wired as an editor, which is the "miswired action" the Ledger audit (#356) is also looking for. Result: a user with two favorites cannot see the second artist's next stop at all. The only way to influence what the card shows is to be the oldest show across all favorites, which is not a user-facing concept. Goal: tapping a chip focuses the card on that artist. Tour tracking moves to its own visible control. Default (nothing focused) looks and behaves exactly as it does today. **Decisions recorded here (technical, no owner input needed):** - **State lives in `HomeScreen`, not a new ViewModel.** The app has exactly one ViewModel (`PlayerViewModel.kt:70`) and it holds no Home/NextStop UI state; every other Home transient (`query` at `:333`, `tourPickerArtist` at `:341`, `nextStop` at `:360`) is local Compose state. A one-string ViewModel is unjustified. Use `var focusedArtistKey by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }` next to `tourPickerArtist` — `rememberSaveable`, not plain `remember`, because focus is state the user set and losing it on rotation would be a second, smaller bug. - **Filtering is client-side; no refetch.** `NextStop.load` already returns every participating artist's candidates in one list, and `oldestUnplayed` is a pure function over that list. So the focus filter is applied to the loaded list before `oldestUnplayed`, and the `loadOnce` key at `:356` (`Triple(todayStr, favKeys, preferencesMap)`) and `NextStop.cacheKey` stay untouched. Switching chips must never hit the network. - **Join on `ArtistRef.key`, not `id`.** The chip row keys off `artist.key` (`:482`, `:495`) and `currentTours` populates `show.artist` from the same `ArtistRef` list, so `show.artist.key == chip.key` holds. (Note the asymmetry that already exists: *preference* lookups accept `key` or `id`, `NextStop.kt:130`. Do not copy that looseness into the focus filter.) - **A second tap on the focused chip clears focus**, restoring the cross-artist default. This is the escape hatch when the focused artist is all played, and it is the only path back that does not need a new control. - **The tour picker gets a visible `Change tour…` text action in the card header, not a chip long-press.** The issue offered either. A long-press has no `contentDescription`, no affordance, and is invisible to anyone who has not been told — the exact class of defect the Ledger audit is filing. A labeled header action beside "NEXT TOUR STOP" is discoverable and costs the same. It targets the focused artist if one is set, else the displayed show's artist, else the first favorited artist. - **Focus clears when the artist stops being a favorite** (`LaunchedEffect(favoriteKeys)`), so un-favoriting moe. while focused on it cannot strand the card on an empty filter. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStop.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStopTest.kt` - `UAT.md` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: 1. **Extract the selection rule as a pure function in `NextStop.kt`**, next to `oldestUnplayed` (`:109-111`), with a KDoc comment saying what it is for and why it is a filter-then-pick rather than a second picker:    ```kotlin    internal fun focusedCandidates(        shows: List<ShowSummary>,        focusedArtistKey: String?,    ): List<ShowSummary> =        if (focusedArtistKey == null) shows else shows.filter { it.artist.key == focusedArtistKey }    ```    A `null` key means "no focus" and must pass the list through untouched, so the unfocused default is bit-for-bit today's behavior. 2. **Add the state to `HomeScreen`**, immediately after `tourPickerArtist` (`:341`): `var focusedArtistKey by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }`. 3. **Apply the filter in the `nextStop` computation** (`:360-362`): feed `focusedCandidates(nextStopShows.value?.getOrNull().orEmpty(), focusedArtistKey)` into `oldestUnplayed(..., playedShowIds(finishedKeys))`. Add `focusedArtistKey` to the `remember` key list so a chip tap recomposes the pick. Do **not** change the `loadOnce` key at `:356` — see the decisions above. 4. **Rewire the chip** (`:495`): `.clickable { focusedArtistKey = if (focusedArtistKey == artist.key) null else artist.key }`. Remove `tourPickerArtist = artist` from the chip entirely — after this step no chip tap can open the dialog. 5. **Make the selected styling reflect focus, not the winner** (`:482`): `val selected = (focusedArtistKey ?: show?.artist?.key) == artist.key`. With nothing focused this is exactly today's expression, so the unfocused card looks unchanged; once focused, the highlighted chip is the one the user chose even when that artist has no unplayed show to display. 6. **Clear a stale focus** with `LaunchedEffect(favoriteKeys) { if (focusedArtistKey != null && focusedArtistKey !in favoriteKeys) focusedArtistKey = null }`. 7. **Add the "Change tour…" action.** Turn the bare `Text("NEXT TOUR STOP")` (`:466-473`) into a `Row` (text + `Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` + the action) inside the same padding. Style the action with the existing `ledger.textSubtle` / `ledger.accentIcon` tokens at the same 12sp scale as the label — no new colors. It sets `tourPickerArtist` to `favoritedArtists.firstOrNull { it.key == focusedArtistKey } ?: show?.artist ?: favoritedArtists.firstOrNull()` — `ShowSummary.artist` is an `ArtistRef` directly, so no lookup is needed for the middle case. If that is still null, do not render the action. Make sure a tap on the action does not also propagate to the card. 8. **Handle focused-and-caught-up.** When `focusedArtistKey != null && show == null`, the card currently renders a header and chips with nothing below. Add one `Text` line in that gap, 12sp `ledger.textSubtle`, reading `"Nothing to catch up on ${artistName}."` where `artistName` resolves from the focused key. Do not add a new button — re-tapping the focused chip already clears focus. 9. **Log the decision.** Run `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and append a `Dnnn` entry to `DECISIONS.md` recording: chips select focus, the tour picker moved to a `Change tour…` header action, the focus filter is client-side and does not re-enter `NextStop.load`'s cache, and why the header action was chosen over a long-press. If this reverses any part of D214 (#133), mark that prior entry superseded rather than editing it. 10. **Add UAT items** to `UAT.md` with the next free `uat-NNN` ids for the owner-only checks listed below. 11. **Update the Android test count in `README.md`** (currently "668 Android unit tests" at `README.md:135`) to the new total. 12. **Run the suite:** `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. Also run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` to confirm the untouched Mac package still passes at 448. Test: what proves it New cases in `NextStopTest.kt` against a `focusedCandidates`-shaped call, using the file's existing fake `MusicSource`/show fixtures: - null focus returns the input list unchanged (element-identical, same order) — this is the regression guard for the unfocused default. - a focus key matching a subset of candidates returns only that artist's shows. - a focus key matching no candidate returns an empty list (not the full list) — the caught-up path. - focus is joined on `artist.key`, so a key that matches no candidate's `artist.key` never falls back to `artist.id`. - end-to-end through `oldestUnplayed(focusedCandidates(shows, "moe."), played)`: with Phish and moe. candidates where Phish holds the older unplayed show, focusing moe. returns moe.'s show, and clearing focus returns Phish's — the actual reported bug, as a test. - the existing `oldestUnplayed` cases at `NextStopTest.kt:126-163` and the `NextStop` cache cases at `:247`, `:260`, `:417` still pass unchanged, which is the proof that the focus filter did not alter the cache or the default pick. Green `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` (668 + new) and `swift test` (448, unchanged). There is no `app/src/androidTest` directory in this repo, so the chip-row interaction itself is not unit-tested — it is covered by the UAT items below, and the selection *rule* behind it is what the tests pin down. ## Done when - [ ] Tapping a favorite-artist chip sets `focusedArtistKey` and the card's show row changes to that artist's oldest unplayed show. No dialog opens. - [ ] Tapping the already-focused chip clears focus and the card returns to the cross-artist default. - [ ] A focused artist with no unplayed (or no current-tour) shows shows `Nothing to catch up on <artist>.` and the chip row stays visible and interactive. - [ ] A `Change tour…` action sits in the card header; tapping it opens `TourPickerDialog` for the focused artist (else the displayed show's artist, else the first favorite) and Save/Reset still persist through `vm.setArtistTourPreference` / `vm.clearArtistTourPreference`. - [ ] With nothing focused, the card's chip styling, show row and pick are identical to the pre-change behavior. - [ ] Un-favoriting the focused artist clears focus rather than stranding the card. - [ ] `focusedCandidates` and its KDoc exist in `NextStop.kt`; `NextStop.load` and `NextStop.cacheKey` are unchanged; the `loadOnce` key at `MainActivity.kt:356` is unchanged. - [ ] At least 5 new tests in `NextStopTest.kt` pass, the whole Android suite is green, and the macOS `swift test` count is unchanged at 448. - [ ] A `Dnnn` entry (ID from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`) is appended to `DECISIONS.md`; the Android test count in `README.md` matches the new total. - [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds — the chip row's `LazyRow` and the new header `Row` compile and lay out. ## Needs a human to check - That tapping "moe." now shows moe.'s next stop instead of the dialog, and that the highlighted chip is the one tapped. - Whether the `Change tour…` label and placement in the card header read as obvious, or whether it should say "Track tour…" / carry a small icon to match the Ledger visual language. The agent cannot judge this without pixels. - That a second tap on the focused chip is discoverable as "go back to all artists", or whether the caught-up message needs an explicit inline "Show all artists" link instead. - Whether the `Nothing to catch up on …` copy is the right tone and wording; it is agent-invented placeholder copy. - That the focused card's show row (artist, date, rating, play button) still fits the card width for long artist names once the header row is a `Row` rather than a lone `Text`. ## Context - Cause confirmed at HEAD: chip click at `MainActivity.kt:495`, dialog host at `:746-760`, `tourPickerDialog` composable at `:2481-2595`, selection at `:360-362`, chip styling at `:482`. - `oldestUnplayed` (`NextStop.kt:109-111`) has no per-artist parameter and no per-artist callers besides `HomeScreen`; the filter is added at the call site, not to the function, so its five existing tests and the macOS twin stay untouched. - `NextStop.load` (`NextStop.kt:212-224`) caches only `currentTours`' network result; the unplayed filter is deliberately outside that cache. The focus filter must stay outside it too — see the KDoc at `NextStop.kt:22-26`. - `HomeView.swift:291-354` (macOS) renders the card as a `prefix(3)` list with no chip row, and `HomeView.swift:18-19` has no per-artist selection state, so there is no macOS counterpart to this fix. The Mac "NEXT TOUR STOPS" card is a different shape on purpose. - **macOS parity finding, reported here and filed separately:** `HomeView.swift:25` declares `@State var tourPickerArtist` which is read by the `.sheet(item:)` at `:69-76` and instantiated at `:75` — and is never assigned anywhere in the repo (`tourPickerArtist =` matches only the four Android sites). `TourPickerSheet` (`macos/CouchTour/Browse/TourPickerSheet.swift`, 252 lines) is therefore unreachable dead UI on macOS, as is `HomeView.reloadDiscovery`'s preference reload path for it. That is a real bug and it is a *different* bug from this one; it needs a macOS-side UI decision this issue does not make. - This is one of the five findings #356 lists from the Ledger redesign `2a6b2cc` (#128/#133, D214) — it is already cited in #356's body as the known miswired-action instance, so do not re-file it there. - Related: #68 (the tour picker for defunct/non-touring artists, closed) is where the chip-tap-opens-picker behavior was introduced deliberately, and #100 (macOS shelf refresh after saving a preference, closed) is the `reloadDiscovery` half of the dead macOS sheet. ## Out of scope - **macOS.** No chip row exists there and the card has a different shape; no focused-artist work lands in `HomeView.swift`. The unreachable `TourPickerSheet` is filed as its own issue. - Making `tourPickerArtist` (`MainActivity.kt:341`) `rememberSaveable` like the new focus state. It is a one-line adjacent nit, deliberately not bundled. - Changing `oldestUnplayed`'s signature, `NextStop.load`, `NextStop.cacheKey`, or the `MAX_TOUR_ARTISTS` / `TOUR_PERIODS` caps. - Persisting the focused artist across app restarts (it is `rememberSaveable`, i.e. config-change-scoped). A stored preference is a bigger product decision. - Any change to the `TourPickerDialog` itself — same dialog, same persistence path, new caller. - Compose UI tests. There is no `app/src/androidTest` in this repo; creating that infrastructure is a separate piece of work. - The other four findings #356 lists (#347, #348, #349, #355) and the Ledger design system itself.

column2: Android: curated/heuristic Spotify–Tidal matches fail to load ('spotify' not a valid ExternalReleasePlatform)
column3: > **Original request:** Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29 (Android beta built from `main`). At startup logcat shows: > > ``` > E CuratedMatches: Failed to load curated releases > E CuratedMatches: kotlinx.serialization.SerializationException: dev.mike.couchtour.ExternalReleasePlatform does not contain element with name 'spotify' at path $['phishin:phish:1995-11-14'].platform > E HeuristicMatches: Failed to load heuristic matches > E HeuristicMatches: kotlinx.serialization.SerializationException: ... 'spotify' at path $['phishin:phish:1994-06-22'].platform > ``` > > The bundled JSON (#281 curated, #321 heuristic) uses lowercase `"spotify"`, but the Kotlin enum `ExternalReleasePlatform` has no matching serial name (probably `SPOTIFY` with no `@SerialName`). Both files fail to load entirely, so no show gets Spotify/Tidal links on Android. The feature shipped in betas after v0.83, so prod is not affected. > > **Fix:** add `@SerialName("spotify")` / `@SerialName("tidal")` (or align the JSON). Add a unit test that decodes the real bundled asset files, so the existing tests can't pass on hand-built fixtures alone. Check that the macOS decoder of the same files agrees. ## Problem / goal `curated_releases.json` and `heuristic_matches.json` are the *only* source of the Show Detail "Spotify" / "Tidal" pill on Android whenever phish.in itself supplies no external release. Both files are 100% `"platform": "spotify"` (lowercase). The Kotlin enum `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt:226` ```kotlin enum class ExternalReleasePlatform {     SPOTIFY, TIDAL } ``` has no `@SerialName`, so kotlinx.serialization matches the JSON string against the *constant name*, case-sensitively. `"spotify" != "SPOTIFY"`, the whole map fails to decode, and because `CuratedMatches.init` / `HeuristicMatches.init` swallow the exception into `runCatching { … }` with only a `Log.e`, `mappings` silently stays `emptyMap()`. Result: the pill never appears, with no user-visible error. macOS is unaffected — `Catalog.swift:347` declares `enum ExternalReleasePlatform: String { case spotify; case tidal }`, whose raw values are exactly the lowercase strings in the JSON. Goal: the bundled files decode on Android, and a test proves it against the *real* files so this cannot regress silently again. **Decided (no owner input needed):** fix the Kotlin side with `@SerialName("spotify")` / `@SerialName("tidal")` on the enum entries. Do **not** uppercase the JSON: lowercase is the canonical wire format (it is what the Swift `String`-raw-value enum expects, and what `scripts/generate_heuristic_matches.py` writes), so aligning Android to the JSON is the one-way fix. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CuratedMatchesTest.kt` (new) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/CatalogTests.swift` - `README.md` Steps: - Add `@SerialName("spotify")` to `SPOTIFY` and `@SerialName("tidal")` to `TIDAL` in   `Catalog.kt:226-228`, with a short comment saying *why* the serial names are lowercase (the   bundled JSON and the Swift `String`-raw-value enum are both lowercase; changing this breaks   `scripts/generate_heuristic_matches.py` output). Add the `kotlinx.serialization.SerialName`   import if not already present in the file. - Do **not** change `app/src/main/assets/*.json` or the macOS `Resources/*.json` copies, and do   not change `CuratedMatches.kt` / `HeuristicMatches.kt`. The other Android call sites   (`Catalog.kt:689`, `MainActivity.kt:1676`, `MainActivity.kt:3893`) build the enum with   `ExternalReleasePlatform.valueOf(string.uppercase())` from the phish.in API and the Room   `external_releases` table, which already store uppercase and keep working unchanged. - New `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CuratedMatchesTest.kt`:   - Robolectric, following `ExternalReleaseHelperTest.kt` (`@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)`,     `@Config(sdk = [34])`, JUnit4, backticked test names).   - It must decode the **actual bundled files**, never a hand-built fixture literal — that is the     whole point of the regression test. Load them via     `RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication().assets.open("curated_releases.json")` /     `open("heuristic_matches.json")`; if Robolectric does not surface `src/main/assets` in the unit     test runtime, read them from disk instead (unit tests run with the module directory     `app/` as the working directory, so `File("src/main/assets/curated_releases.json")`).   - Assert after calling `CuratedMatches.init(context)` / `HeuristicMatches.init(context)`:     - `CuratedMatches.match(Backend.PHISHIN, "phish", "1995-11-14")` is non-null, with       `platform == ExternalReleasePlatform.SPOTIFY`, the expected open.spotify.com URL, and       `isHeuristic == false` (the curated entry omits the field, exercising the default).     - `HeuristicMatches.match(Backend.PHISHIN, "phish", "1994-06-22")` is non-null with       `isHeuristic == true`.     - `HeuristicMatches.match(Backend.RELISTEN, "grateful-dead", "1970-02-13")` is non-null, which       covers the Relisten key prefix of the same map.     - A decode of a `{"k":{"platform":"tidal","url":"…"}}` literal into       `Map<String, ExternalRelease>` yields `TIDAL`, so the `tidal` branch is covered even though       no bundled asset uses it.   - `CuratedMatches` / `HeuristicMatches` are singletons, so one `init` per object per test class is     enough; the previous `runCatching` failure mode is what the non-null assertions rule out. - Add a macOS parity test in `CatalogTests.swift` that decodes the **real** bundled JSON with   `JSONDecoder().decode([String: ExternalRelease].self, …)` and asserts the same entries (curated   `phishin:phish:1995-11-14` is `.spotify`, `isHeuristic` defaults to `false`; heuristic   `phishin:phish:1994-06-22` is `.spotify` with `isHeuristic` true). Locate the files relative to   `#filePath`: from   `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/CatalogTests.swift`, drop three path   components to reach the package root, then `Sources/CouchTourKit/Resources/<name>.json`. This   also guards against the two hand-maintained copies of the JSON drifting apart. - Bump the test counts in `README.md` ("668 Android unit tests" and "448 macOS package tests") to   the real numbers `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` and `swift test` report. Test: what proves it - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`   — the new `CuratedMatchesTest` passes and the suite stays green. - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` — the new parity test passes (needs full Xcode, not   just Command Line Tools, or it fails with `__allocating_init`, D115). - Before the fix, the new Android test fails with the same   `SerializationException: … does not contain element with name 'spotify'` from the logcat report. ## Done when - [ ] `ExternalReleasePlatform` entries carry `@SerialName("spotify")` / `@SerialName("tidal")`, and       the bundled JSON files are unmodified (byte-identical to `main`). - [ ] A JVM unit test decodes both real bundled asset files and asserts non-null matches for       `phishin:phish:1995-11-14` (curated), `phishin:phish:1994-06-22` and       `relisten:grateful-dead:1970-02-13` (heuristic), plus `tidal` from a literal. - [ ] No unit test for this feature builds its own JSON fixture in place of the bundled file. - [ ] A macOS `swift test` decodes the same real bundled resource and asserts the same entries. - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green and `README.md` test counts match the actual totals. - [ ] `git diff --stat main -- app/src/main/assets macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Resources`       is empty. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` unchanged or extended with a sequential `Dnnn` (via `mahler next-id couch-tour D`)       if you decide the JSON wire format deserves logging. ## Needs a human to check - Install the next Android beta and open a curated/auto-matched show (e.g. Phish 1995-11-14) and an   auto-matched one (e.g. 1994-06-22): the Spotify pill with the "· Auto-matched" suffix must appear   on the show screen, and tapping it must open the Spotify app (or the web page if Spotify is not   installed). No `E CuratedMatches` / `E HeuristicMatches` lines in logcat at startup. ## Context - Feature origin: `58b5842` (#281, curated) and `02b4b53` (#321, heuristic); noted in   `ROADMAP.md:100` as "Show Detail external link … Part 1/2/3". - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CuratedMatches.kt` and `HeuristicMatches.kt` load their   assets with `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` — which does nothing for a bad enum value — and   swallow failures with `Log.e`. That is why this shipped unnoticed: silent empty map, not a crash. - The JSON is produced by `scripts/generate_heuristic_matches.py`, which hard-codes lowercase   `"platform": "spotify"`. There is no generator for the curated file; it is hand-edited in both   `app/src/main/assets/` and `macos/.../Resources/`. - `scripts/cut-beta.sh` is the wrapper for cutting the beta needed for the human check. - Known remaining gaps, deliberately **not** in scope here: no unknown-platform resilience (a   future `"bandcamp"` value would again nuke the whole map), and no test that the two hand-maintained   copies of the JSON are byte-identical. ## Out of scope - Changing the lowercase wire format in any direction (including adding `"tidal"` entries to the   bundled assets). - Renaming the enum constants, or changing the phish.in-API / Room call sites that already   `.uppercase()` before `valueOf`. - Curated-match curation work (adding more curated dates, Tidal links, other bands). - Making `CuratedMatches` / `HeuristicMatches` fail loudly instead of logging, or restructuring them. - Google TV and sync-backend surfaces.

column2: Android: On This Date silently drops phish.in years when a large year_range request times out
column3: > **Original request:** > > Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29 (Android beta built from `main`, emulator). > > **Repro (9/29, Phish favorited):** On This Date shows 2 Phish shows (2000, 1999). The Mac finds 5, and phish.in has 9/29 shows in at least 1995, 1999 and 2000. > > **Cause:** `OnThisDate.kt` `showsFor` fetches phish.in in `year_range=` batches of up to 900 shows with `per_page=1000`. Those responses are about 2.7 MB and take 8–20 s live (measured with curl today). With several running in parallel on a phone, one exceeds OkHttp's 30 s `readTimeout` (`Api.kt:195`). Logcat: `W PhishInApi: /api/v2/shows: call failed after 30003ms (SocketTimeoutException: timeout)`. `runCatching { … }.getOrDefault(emptyList())` then silently drops that whole range, so every anniversary in it disappears, and `OnThisDate.load` caches the partial result for the day. > > **Fix direction:** > - Smaller batches, or per-year requests (`/api/v2/shows?year=` is about 0.9 s and 260 KB), or phish.in's date filtering if one exists. > - Don't cache a result that had failed ranges. > - Consider the same change on macOS (`CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift`), which uses the same batching and only gets away with it on faster networking. > > Related: #350 (Relisten year budget) and #346 (macOS caches a failed load as empty). ## Problem / goal A phish.in `year_range=` request that times out is indistinguishable from a year with no shows. `showsFor` swallows the failure (`runCatching { … }.getOrDefault(emptyList())`, `OnThisDate.kt:200`), and `OnThisDate.load` writes whatever came back into its one-entry daily cache (`OnThisDate.kt:241`). One slow response therefore removes whole spans of Phish history from On This Date for the rest of the day, with no error and no way to retry. Goal: a year range never disappears silently, and a partly-fetched answer is never cached. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDate.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDateTest.kt` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: - [ ] **Shrink the batches.** Lower `PHISHIN_RANGE_CAP` (`OnThisDate.kt:41`) from `900` to `300`. phish.in serializes roughly 3 KB per show, so a 900-show range is the ~2.7 MB / 8–20 s response in the report; a 300-show range is ~0.9 MB / ~3 s, which clears the 30 s read timeout with several requests in flight. Phish's whole archive is under 2,000 shows with audio, so this is ~7 requests instead of ~4 — still far under `per_page=1000`, so no page can truncate. Update the KDoc on `phishInRanges` and the D-entry, not just the constant. - [ ] **Bound the fan-out.** The per-period `async` at `OnThisDate.kt:200` is unbounded, which is the "several running in parallel on a phone" half of the bug. Add an `internal const val PHISHIN_CONCURRENCY = 4` and gate the phish.in period fetches on a `kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Semaphore` (that package is already a dependency — `Mutex` is used at `OnThisDate.kt:220`). Relisten's sequential-by-budget path is unaffected. - [ ] **Stop swallowing cancellation.** `runCatching` catches `Throwable`, so it also eats `CancellationException` — a cancelled load currently returns an empty list instead of propagating. Replace it with an explicit `catch (e: IOException)` for the fetch, letting cancellation and programming errors through. The per-artist `runCatching` at `OnThisDate.kt:172` gets the same treatment. - [ ] **Retry a failed range once.** A range that fails with an `IOException` (timeouts included) gets one more attempt after a short `delay` — the same range, no backoff loop, no retry on `HttpException`/4xx, which will not fix themselves. This is what actually recovers a year on a marginal connection rather than just not caching the loss. - [ ] **Report incompleteness, and stop caching it.** Add `internal data class Fetched<T>(val value: T, val complete: Boolean)`. `showsFor` returns `Fetched<List<ShowSummary>>` (complete = every period fetch succeeded), `showsOnDate` returns `Fetched<List<ShowSummary>>` aggregated across artists, and `OnThisDate.load` writes to `cached` **only** when `complete` is true. `OnThisDate.load`'s own signature is unchanged, so `MainActivity.kt` does not need editing, and per D162 the UI keeps showing the partial row — a partly-populated discovery shelf is worth more than an error message where a row would be. The next `load` for the same day simply re-fetches. - [ ] **Reset hook for tests.** Add `internal fun resetCache()` on `OnThisDate` mirroring `PhishInSource.resetCache()` / `RelistenCatalogSource.resetCache()` (macOS already has one), so the new tests reset consistently instead of assigning the `cached` field directly. - [ ] **Log a new D-entry** with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`. Append; do not rewrite D176. Record: cap 900 → 300 with the size/latency reasoning, the concurrency bound, the `catch (IOException)` narrowing, the single retry, the `Fetched` completeness flag and the no-cache rule. Note explicitly that `Api.kt`'s shared 15 s/30 s timeouts are **unchanged** — this fix does not supersede D176's instrumentation-only position, it removes the request size that made the timeout reachable. - [ ] **Update the test count in `README.md`** (AGENTS.md rule). Test: what proves it Add to `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDateTest.kt`, using the file's existing style — plain JUnit4, `org.junit.Assert.*`, a fake `MusicSource` passed through the `source` parameter, an explicit `today` string, `Random(1)`, and the `// ---- section` banner comments. Cases: - `phishInRanges` with `cap = 300` over a 1983–2000 Phish-shaped period list returns batches that each sum to ≤ 300, cover every year, and contain more batches than the `cap = 900` call does. - A fake whose phish.in period fetch throws `SocketTimeoutException` on the first call and succeeds on the second still returns that period's anniversary shows. - A fake where one period always throws: `showsOnDate` returns the other periods' matches (nothing else is lost) and reports `complete = false`; `OnThisDate.load` over the same source leaves `OnThisDate.cached` null, and a second `load` calls the source again. - The complement: a source where every period succeeds — the first `load` populates the cache and a second `load` does not re-fetch. - A source that suspends in `periods()` and records peak in-flight period fetches never exceeds `PHISHIN_CONCURRENCY`. - A source whose `periods()` throws `CancellationException` propagates it out of `showsOnDate` rather than returning an empty list. Run: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` (Android suite was 641 after D272; macOS is untouched by this issue and must stay at 443). ## Done when - [ ] `PHISHIN_RANGE_CAP` is 300 and no phish.in `year_range=` request built by this code can exceed ~1 MB. - [ ] Peak concurrent phish.in period fetches are bounded by a named constant, asserted by a test. - [ ] A period fetch that throws `CancellationException` propagates; only `IOException` is absorbed. - [ ] A failed range is retried exactly once and succeeds when the second attempt works. - [ ] `OnThisDate.load` does not populate `cached` when any range failed, and does populate it when none did — both asserted. - [ ] `showsOnDate`'s partial results are still returned and still render; the fix changes caching, not the UI contract. - [ ] `Api.kt` is unmodified — the shared client timeouts are untouched. - [ ] New tests added to `OnThisDateTest.kt`; `testDebugUnitTest` green; the Android test count in `README.md` matches the run. - [ ] A new `Dnnn` entry is appended to `DECISIONS.md` and D176 is not edited. - [ ] Work ends at a pushed branch with a mergeable commit. ## Needs a human to check - On a real phone (not the emulator, and ideally on cellular or a weak wifi signal) with Phish favorited, open Home on a date Phish played — 9/29 is the known case — and confirm the shelf now lists shows from the early years (1995, 1999, 2000) and not just 1999/2000. - Confirm Home does not feel slower to paint the On This Date row. The fix trades ~4 requests of 2.7 MB for ~7 of 0.9 MB, all concurrent and bounded at 4; it should be strictly faster, but that is a judgement only the owner can make on a device. - Confirm nothing new appears on a day with no anniversaries: no error text, no spinner stuck (D162 requires the row to render nothing at all when empty). ## Context - `OnThisDate.kt:200` is the swallow; `OnThisDate.kt:241` is the cache write; `Api.kt:193-197` is the 15 s/30 s client this is deliberately not touching. - D176 considered the 30 s read timeout and deliberately deferred tuning it in favour of instrumentation (`ApiTiming.kt`). This issue is that instrumentation paying off: the log line in the report is `TimingEventListener`'s `callFailed`. The fix goes after the request size, not the timeout, so D176 stays in force. - D162 set the request budget (~19 requests worst case, cached once a day) and the "partial row beats an error message" rule this issue extends to the cache. - D272 already tightened `phishInRanges` and added the `OnThisDate` mutex; the constant it batches against is the one being lowered here. - `totalEntries` is parsed and discarded everywhere in `Api.kt`, so there is no pagination to lean on. A 300-show cap is the fix, not a page loop; pagination is a separate, larger change. - Per-year requests (`year=1997`, ~260 KB) were the other option on the table. Rejected: Phish has ~35 years, so per-year would be ~35 requests against a ~7-request budget, for the same completeness. ## Out of scope - **macOS.** `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` carries the same `phishInRangeCap = 900`, but it fetches periods sequentially in a `withTaskGroup` and runs on `URLSession.shared` (60 s default) rather than a 30 s read timeout, so it is not known to drop years the same way. Split out to a separate issue rather than doubling this build's blast radius. - #350 (Relisten's 12-year budget) — a different cause, different endpoint, already tracked. - #346 (macOS caching a failed load as empty) — the same *symptom* on the other platform, and it also covers `NextStop`, which this issue does not touch. - Any change to `Api.kt`'s timeouts, connection pool, or `pingInterval`, and any global retry/backoff policy. - Paginating phish.in past `per_page=1000`. - Adding a persistent catalog cache for On This Date; D162 chose in-memory for a reason.

column2: On This Date misses older anniversaries for Relisten artists (12-recent-year budget)
column3: > **Original request:** Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29. > > **Repro (9/29):** with moe. favorited, On This Date shows only Phish. Relisten's `/api/v2/artists/moe/shows/on-date?month=9&day=29` returns 5 shows (1995, 1998, 2001, 2007, 2013). > > **Cause:** `CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` `showsOnDate` fetches at most `relistenYearBudget` = 12 years, split across up to 3 Relisten favorites, and always takes the **most recent** years. An artist with a long history gets anniversaries only from recent years, and with 3 favorites that drops to 4 years each. > > **Fix:** use Relisten's `shows/on-date?month=&day=` endpoint. It is one request per artist, complete, and cheaper than walking years. Remove the year budget for Relisten. Android (`OnThisDate.load` in `MainActivity.kt`) likely has the same design; fix both. ## Problem / goal On This Date (Home) only looks at each Relisten favorite's most recent 12 years (split across up to 3 artists), so older anniversaries never appear. Replace the year-walking with Relisten's on-date endpoint: one request per artist, returns every year. Do it on both macOS (CouchTourKit) and Android. Phish.in behaviour (range-batched `year_range=` fetches) is unchanged. Verified live: `GET https://api.relisten.net/api/v2/artists/moe/shows/on-date?month=9&day=29` returns a JSON array of 5 show objects (`display_date` 1995/1998/2001/2007/2013-09-29, plus `venue`, `tour`, `source_count`, `avg_rating`, `has_soundboard_source`, `has_streamable_flac_source`, `popularity`). These fields match the existing `RelistenShowSummary` model on both platforms, so it decodes as `[RelistenShowSummary]` and maps with the existing `toShowSummary(artist:)`. The slug in `ArtistRef.id` works as the path segment (`moe`). `month=2&day=29` returns 200. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/RelistenAPI.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/OnThisDateTests.swift` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Relisten.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDate.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDateTest.kt` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: 1. Relisten API client (both platforms): add `RelistenApi.showsOnDate(artistIdOrSlug, month, day)` / `RelistenAPI.showsOnDate(...)` doing `GET v2/artists/{slug}/shows/on-date?month=M&day=D` (query params, not path segments; month/day as plain integers, no zero padding needed) and decoding `[RelistenShowSummary]`. Swift path builder returns a bare `URL`, so use `URLComponents` like `search` does. 2. `MusicSource` seam: add a `showsOnDate(artist, month, day)` capability. Kotlin: interface method with a default body. Swift: protocol requirement plus a default in a protocol extension, so the several existing mock `MusicSource` types in tests keep compiling. Default = "not supported" (empty result is fine; only the Relisten branch calls it). `RelistenCatalogSource` (both platforms) overrides it to call the new API and map with `toShowSummary(artist)`. Parse month/day from the `MM-DD` string already produced by `monthDay(today)`. 3. `OnThisDate` (both platforms): in `showsOnDate`/`showsFor`, for the Relisten backend call the new source method (one request) instead of `periods` + per-year `shows`, then pass the result through `showsOnAnniversary` (still needed: the endpoint includes today's own year, which must be excluded). Keep the phish.in branch (`phishInRanges`) as is. 4. Remove `relistenYearBudget` / `RELISTEN_YEAR_BUDGET` and the year-splitting helper on both platforms, and their tests. Decision: keep an artist cap for Relisten, since each favorite still costs one request every launch/day, but raise it from 3 to 10 (`maxRelistenArtists` / `MAX_RELISTEN_ARTISTS`), because it no longer has to share a 12-year budget. Worst case is then about 14 requests, once a day (result is already cached per date+favorites in `OnThisDate`). 5. Update the file-header doc comment in `OnThisDate.kt`, which says Relisten has "no on this day endpoint" and describes the year budget; it is now wrong. Update doc comments in `OnThisDate.swift` likewise. 6. `DECISIONS.md`: get the next id with `mahler next-id couch-tour D`, add an entry that supersedes the Relisten half of D162 (do not rewrite D162): Relisten uses `shows/on-date`, year budget removed, artist cap 10. `README.md`: update test counts if tests are added or removed. 7. Do not touch the phish.in path, the cache, or `MainActivity.kt` / `HomeView.swift` (their `OnThisDate.load` call sites are unchanged). Test: unit tests, no network. - Swift (`OnThisDateTests.swift`): with a mock Relisten `MusicSource` whose `showsOnDate` returns shows from 1995/1998/2001/2007/2013 (plus one dated the current year) and whose `periods` throws or records a call, assert the on-date shows come back, today's year is excluded, and `periods`/`shows` were never called for Relisten. Assert the request path/query at the API level with the existing mock-URLSession style in `RequestTests.swift` if practical (`/v2/artists/moe/shows/on-date?month=9&day=29`). Replace the budget-split tests. Run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test`. - Kotlin (`OnThisDateTest.kt`): replace the "caps at three relisten artists and splits the year budget" test with: a fake Relisten source returning old-year anniversaries through `showsOnDate` shows up in the result; artists beyond the cap of 10 are skipped; a failing artist doesn't drop the others. Delete the `relistenYearBudget` tests. Add a MockWebServer request test (see `RelistenRequestTest.kt` for the pattern; add cases to that file only if needed, and add it to this Files list) asserting the on-date URL.
