Run `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. ## Done when - [ ] Both platforms call `v2/artists/{slug}/shows/on-date?month=M&day=D` once per favorited Relisten artist and no longer call `years`/`year` for On This Date. - [ ] `relistenYearBudget` / `RELISTEN_YEAR_BUDGET` and their tests are gone; Relisten artist cap is 10. - [ ] Today's own year is still excluded, and results are still capped at 8, random, newest-first. - [ ] phish.in behaviour is unchanged and its existing tests still pass. - [ ] A test proves an old-year (pre-recent-12) Relisten anniversary is returned on each platform. - [ ] `swift test` in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` and `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` both pass. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new entry (id from `mahler next-id`) superseding the Relisten part of D162; README test counts updated if they changed. ## Needs a human to check - On a device or Mac with moe. (or another long-history Relisten artist) favorited, open Home on a date the artist played in old years (e.g. Sept 29 for moe.: 1995, 1998, 2001, 2007, 2013) and confirm those older shows appear in On This Date alongside Phish. ## Context - Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29. Prior design: D162 (`DECISIONS.md`). - Related, touching the same files: #352 (Android: phish.in `year_range` timeout drops years) and #346 (macOS: failed On This Date load cached as empty). Do not fix those here; rebase carefully if they land first. - `MusicSource` implementers in tests: several existing mocks exist (Swift: `CatalogTests`, `NextStopTests`, `OnThisDateTests`, `DiscoveryCatalogE2ETests`; Kotlin: `CatalogTest`, `NextStopTest`, `OnThisDateTest`), which is why the new method needs a default implementation. ## Out of scope - phish.in fetching/batching, the cache, and the 8-show random pick. - Fixing #352 and #346. - Any UI change.

column2: macOS: no Artists entry in sidebar — artist browse only reachable via hidden ⌘2
column3: > **Original request:** Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29. The owner reported "I can't browse artists." > > The Ledger sidebar (`SidebarView.swift`) lists Home, Search, Library, History and Settings, with no Artists. `ArtistsView` still works, but it can only be reached through the invisible ⌘2 menu command (`CouchTourApp.swift:69`) or the small "Favorite artists ›" link on the Next Tour Stops card. Neither is discoverable. > > **Fix:** add an Artists entry to the sidebar nav, routing to `.artists`. Check Android parity at the same time. ## Problem / goal The Ledger redesign (`2a6b2cc`, #133/D214) created `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift` as a *new* file (it is an add in that commit, 183 lines) and made it the window's primary nav surface. The five rows it shipped — Home, Search, Library, History, Settings — are one destination short of what the app can actually show. `Route.artists` (`Navigation.swift:18`), `ArtistsView` (`Browse/ArtistsView.swift`) and its `navigationDestination` (`ThreePaneRootView.swift:104-105`) all exist and work; nothing in the nav chrome points at them. What survives is not discoverable: - **⌘2** — a menu-bar command with no on-screen affordance. A user who does not already know the shortcut cannot find it. - **"Favorite artists ›"** — a 12pt link inside the NEXT TOUR STOPS card header (`HomeView.swift:317-326`). It reads as a link to the favorite list, and in fact navigates to the full `.artists` screen. It is the only visible entry, and it is not labelled for what it does. So on macOS there is no way to reach the artist list by looking at the app. The fix is one row. **Android parity check (done, in this planning pass):** Android already has a discoverable Artists entry — Home's "Browse artists" row (`MainActivity.kt:627-636`) navigates to the `"artists"` route (`MainActivity.kt:218`, `ArtistsScreen` at `:1165`), which carries the same filter field and sort chips as the Mac screen. Android's bottom bar (`LedgerBottomBar`, `MainActivity.kt:4284-4344`) has four tabs (Home, Search, Library, Settings) and UAT `uat-027` pins that number, but phone bottom bars are the wrong home for a fifth browse tab when Home already links to it directly. **Decision: this issue is macOS-only. No Android change.** That is recorded here rather than asked, because the defect is a macOS regression and Android already passes the discoverability bar. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift` - `DECISIONS.md` - `UAT.md` Steps: 1. **Add an `Artists` row to the sidebar's primary nav `VStack`** (`SidebarView.swift:45-91`), immediately after the `Home` row (`:46-52`) and before `Search` (`:54-62`). Home and Artists are the two "places" in this app; Search, Library and History are tools over them; Settings is last. Every other row is already in that shape, so nothing else in the stack moves. 2. **Use the same call shape as its siblings**, not a new view. A `SidebarNavItem` (the private struct at `:183-214`) with:    - `title: "Artists"`    - `icon: "music.mic"` — no artist symbol is used anywhere in the sidebar today (`house`, `magnifyingglass`, `books.vertical`, `clock`, `gearshape`), and `music.mic` reads as "artists/bands" rather than the `music.note` used for a single track in `PlayerRailView.swift:425`. Avoid reusing the favorites-list abbreviation styling further down the same pane; this row must not look like one of those entries.    - `isSelected: appModel.path.last == .artists` — the identical predicate its siblings use (`:57`, `:67`, `:77`). Note the consequence: the row lights only on the Artists screen itself, not while an artist is drilled into (path `[.artists, .artist(x)]`). That is what the Library row does when you are inside a playlist, so this is consistent, not a new wart. 3. **Action: `appModel.jump(to: .artists)`.** Not `appModel.path.append(.artists)`, which is what Search/Library/History do. `jump` replaces the path (`AppModel.swift:142-144`), so clicking Artists from deep inside a show lands on Artists with a single Back step to Home, and it is the same call ⌘2 already makes (`CouchTourApp.swift:69`) — one destination, one code path. The siblings' `append` behavior is a pre-existing inconsistency; **do not change it here** (see Out of scope). 4. **Comment the row's `isSelected` and action choice** in the `SidebarView` doc comment (`:4-6`), which currently describes the nav list as "Home, Search, Library, History, Settings". Update that sentence to include Artists. One line, so the next reader does not "fix" the list back. 5. **Log the decision.** Run `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and append a `Dnnn` entry to `DECISIONS.md` recording: (a) the Ledger sidebar is the shipping macOS nav surface even though D203 declared it removed — D203's hub model is superseded by the shipped 3-pane layout, and this entry is the pointer; (b) every `Route` case with a browse screen gets a sidebar row, Artists included; (c) the row uses `jump`, not `append`, and why. Mark D203 superseded rather than editing it (repo convention). 6. **Add a UAT item** to `UAT.md` with the next free `uat-NNN` id (next free is `uat-070`; never reuse an existing one) under a new section for this issue, covering the owner-only check below. 7. **Verify the build.** `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` must stay green at 448, and the app target must build:    ```bash    cd macos && xcodegen generate    xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build    ```    `macos/CouchTour.xcodeproj` is generated and gitignored (D103); in a fresh worktree it may be a symlink to the main checkout — remove the symlink before running `xcodegen generate`, and confirm the build resolves `CouchTourKit` from *this* worktree, not the main checkout. Test: what proves it - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` — unchanged at **448 passing**. No new test is added and that is deliberate, not an omission: `macos/CouchTour` has no unit test target (D166), so `swift test` cannot see a SwiftUI sidebar row, and the only symbols this change touches (`Route.artists`, `breadcrumbTrail`, `jump`) are already covered by `NavigationTests.swift:23-24` and exercised through `AppModel`. A green 448 is the regression guard: the row compiles, and nothing in the route model moved. - The build in step 7 is the real compile check — `SidebarNavItem` is a private struct in the app target, so a typo in the icon name or a wrong argument label is only caught there. - `git diff --stat` shows exactly `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift` plus the `DECISIONS.md` and `UAT.md` additions. No other Swift file changes, no Android file changes, no fixture changes. - The row's *behavior* — click lands on Artists, selection highlight, no stacked path — is only checkable by a person with pixels. That is the UAT item. ## Done when - [ ] The macOS sidebar's primary nav reads **Home, Artists, Search, Library, History, Settings**, in that order, with Artists second. - [ ] The Artists row uses the SF Symbol `music.mic` and the existing `SidebarNavItem` styling (14pt label, 34pt row height, same accent wash when selected) — no bespoke view, no new colors, no change to the 236pt sidebar width. - [ ] Clicking Artists on a fresh launch opens `ArtistsView` (filter field and sort picker present), and the row is highlighted. - [ ] Clicking Artists while deep in a show (breadcrumb at `Couch Tour › Artists › … › date`) lands on Artists with `appModel.path == [.artists]` — not appended on top of the show — and one Back returns to Home. - [ ] ⌘2 still lands on Artists and produces the identical view state (both routes go through `AppModel.jump(to: .artists)`). - [ ] Clicking Artists while already on `.artists` is a no-op in effect — no duplicate stack entry, no view reload. - [ ] The other four rows (Home, Search, Library, History, Settings), the FAVORITE ARTISTS list, and the sync footer are byte-for-byte unchanged; no other Swift file is modified. - [ ] No Android file is modified; Android's "Browse artists" entry on Home still works. - [ ] `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` is green at 448, and the Debug `xcodebuild` in step 7 succeeds. - [ ] A `Dnnn` entry (ID from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`) is appended to `DECISIONS.md`, marking D203's "no sidebar" claim superseded and recording the Artists row, its position, its icon, and the `jump`-not-`append` choice. - [ ] A new `UAT.md` item with a fresh `uat-NNN` id covers the checks below. ## Needs a human to check - Look at the sidebar and confirm the Artists row reads as a peer of Home rather than as a sixth thing crammed in — the nav is 5 rows today and becomes 6, and the sidebar also holds the FAVORITE ARTISTS list below it. Does a 6th row push that list down too far, or look crowded under the 11pt tracking-wide "FAVORITE ARTISTS" label? - Is `music.mic` the right symbol, or would `person.2` / `music.note.list` read better next to `books.vertical` and `clock`? The agent picked it; it is a taste call. - Click Artists from deep inside a show and confirm landing on Artists feels right, and that the row's highlight not staying lit while you are inside a single artist doesn't bother you. Both alternatives (row stays lit while any `.artists` is in the path; highlight follows the artist) are one-line changes if you prefer them. - That the Artists list, filter field and sort picker still look right in the center pane now that there is a direct route to them. ## Context - `SidebarView.swift` was **added** by the Ledger redesign (`2a6b2cc`, #133, D214) — `git show --stat 2a6b2cc` lists it as `183 +++++`, new file, no deletion. There is no pre-redesign version of this sidebar to restore a row from; before the redesign the app ran D203's hub model with one `NavigationStack` and no sidebar at all. So this is not "put back what was removed" — it is "the new nav surface shipped one destination short." - **D203 says the sidebar is gone** ("The sidebar is gone entirely — not trimmed, not replaced with a tab strip", `DECISIONS.md:3148`), and `Navigation.swift:3` still repeats it. It is wrong about the shipping app: `ThreePaneRootView.swift:23` mounts `SidebarView` as the left pane of the 3-pane layout. That doc drift is why the row was never missed in review — the code reads as if there is no sidebar to add to. Step 5 records the correction. - The row's destination already exists end to end: `Route.artists` (`Navigation.swift:18`), `case .artists: ArtistsView()` (`ThreePaneRootView.swift:104-105`), `crumbTitle == "Artists"` (`Navigation.swift:38`, tested at `NavigationTests.swift:23`). Nothing new is needed to make it render. - The existing visible entry, `HomeView.swift:317-326`, is a `NavigationLink(value: Route.artists)` labelled "Favorite artists" with a chevron. It lands on the same screen this row will. Its label is wrong (the destination is the full artist list, Phish/Favorites/All, not just the favorites) — a real but separate wording defect, listed in Out of scope and worth #356's audit to file. - `AppModel.jump(to:)` (`AppModel.swift:142`) is documented as "Jumps to a top-level destination — the ⌘1–⌘4 menu items, and Home's own tiles", with the replace-don't-append rule. Artists is a top-level destination in exactly that sense, so `jump` is the existing intended mechanism, not a new one. - **Android is not affected** and does not need a parity change: `MainActivity.kt:218` declares the `"artists"` route, `ArtistsScreen` (`:1165`) implements it, and Home's "Browse artists" row (`:627-636`) links to it. The four-tab bottom bar is pinned by UAT `uat-027` ("Bottom nav bar with 4 tabs (Home, Search, Library, Settings)"). Adding a fifth tab to a phone bottom bar is a product/taste call this issue does not make. - This is one of the five regressions #356 already names from the Ledger redesign; #356 lists #348 explicitly and is not re-filed. Related macOS findings in the same batch: #347 (the sidebar's hardcoded mockup favorites at `SidebarView.swift:16-23` — same file, do not bundle), #349 (search drops artist results), #354 (Android chip miswiring). ## Out of scope - **Android.** No `MainActivity.kt` change, no fifth bottom-bar tab, no Android UAT item. Android's Artists entry is already discoverable from Home. - **The "Favorite artists ›" link in `HomeView.swift:317-326`.** It keeps working and is left exactly as is. Its label is misleading (it goes to the full artist list) — a wording fix, and #356's audit should file it. - **#347's hardcoded `fallbackFavoriteArtists`** (`SidebarView.swift:16-23`) — same file, separate issue. Do not fix it here, and do not let its removal change what the new row does. - **Normalizing the sibling rows' `append` behavior.** Search, Library and History push onto `appModel.path` and can stack a destination on top of a deep path. That wart predates this issue; the Artists row uses `jump` because it is a top-level destination, and rewriting the other three rows' semantics is a separate change with its own UAT. - **The rest of #356's findings** (#347, #349, #355, #354), the double traffic lights, unlabeled icon buttons, or the `0 shows` sidebar count. - Any change to `ArtistsView` itself, `Route`, `Navigation.swift`, or the breadcrumb. The destination is already correct; only the nav chrome was missing. - Renaming the sidebar's "FAVORITE ARTISTS" section or restyling the nav rows. This issue adds one row and changes nothing else about the pane's appearance.

column2: macOS: search never shows artist results; Relisten venue hits mislabeled as Songs
column3: > **Original request:** > > Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29, on 0.84-beta and still present in `main`. > > **Repro:** Search "moe". Results show tabs All 22 / Tracks 2 / Shows 0 / Songs 20, and there is no row for the artist moe. > > **Causes** (`macos/CouchTour/SearchView.swift`): > 1. `SearchHits.artists` is computed and passed through `filteredHits`, but the result list (around lines 239-253) only loops `tracks`, `shows` and `slices`. Artist hits are never rendered, and there is no Artists tab. `RelistenAPI.search("moe")` does return `moe.` (verified live). > 2. Relisten venue hits (for example "Moe's Alley") are counted under **Songs** and laid out in the track columns: the artist name under ARTIST, "Venues" under DATE, the venue name under TITLE, and "0 shows". > > **Fix:** add artist rows (and an Artists tab) that navigate to `.artist(...)`. Give venue slices their own tab and row layout with correct counts. Check Android parity. > > Android check (UAT 2026-09-29): Android search renders ARTISTS and VENUES sections correctly, so the missing artist rows are macOS-only. Both platforms show "0 shows" on every search artist and venue row, because Relisten's `/v3/search` returns `show_count: 0`. Hide the count, or join it against the `/v3/artists` list, which has real counts. ## Problem / goal Search results are wrong on macOS and half-wrong on Android. Three distinct defects: 1. **macOS never renders artist hits.** `SearchView` computes `filteredHits.artists`, passes it through, and uses it only to populate the filter-chip menu. No row and no tab. The data is already there — no new fetch required. 2. **Venue hits are filed under Songs on macOS.** `SliceKind` already distinguishes `.song` from `.venue` and `SliceKind.heading` already returns "Songs"/"Venues", but macOS has one `songs` tab that lumps both together, and `searchSliceRow` writes the literal heading string into the DATE column. A venue row therefore reads "GD / Venues / The Marketplace / 0 shows" in track columns. 3. **"0 shows" is rendered on both platforms, for artists and venues.** Verified live: `GET https://api.relisten.net/api/v3/search?q=moe` returns artist objects with **no `show_count` field at all** (only `/v3/artists` carries it), and the `Venues` bucket has no count field of any kind. `RelistenSearchVenue` therefore cannot produce a count, and `RelistenAPI.swift:716` builds the venue `PeriodRef` without one, so it defaults to 0. Song slices *do* have a real count (`shows_played_at`). Goal: artist hits get their own tab and navigate to `.artist(...)`; venue hits get their own tab and a sane row layout; no row anywhere ever says "0 shows". ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/SearchView.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/RelistenAPI.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/RelistenParsingTests.swift` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Relisten.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/RelistenParsingTest.kt` Steps: 1. **Counts: never render "0 shows".** Mandatory, both platforms, one `> 0` guard each — this is the existing precedent in `macos/CouchTour/Browse/ArtistsView.swift:92` (`if artist.showCount > 0`), `macos/CouchTour/Browse/PeriodsView.swift:45`, and `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlaybackService.kt:544`.    - macOS `SearchView.swift:505` (slice count) — guard it.    - Android `MainActivity.kt:2929` (artist subtitle) — make it `null`/omitted when `showCount == 0`.    - Android `MainActivity.kt:2966` (slice subtitle) — split so the artist name and the count are independent; drop the `· N shows` clause when the count is 0. 2. **Counts: join artist hits against `/v3/artists` when it is already in memory.** Both platforms already hold a 15-minute-TTL cache of the real artist list — `RelistenCatalogSource.artists()` (`RelistenAPI.swift:813`, `cachedArtists`) and Android `RelistenCatalogSource.cachedArtists` (`Relisten.kt:450`) — and macOS already primes it at startup in `ThreePaneRootView.swift:91`. Match search artist hits by slug to that list and use the real `showCount`.    - Best-effort and non-blocking: read the cache, never add a network fetch to the search path.    - If the list isn't loaded (or the artist isn't in it), omit the count entirely rather than showing 0.    - Venue and song slices get no join — Relisten genuinely has no count for a search venue hit. Songs keep their real `shows_played_at` count; venues render without a count. 3. **macOS: add an `artists` tab to `SearchTab`** (`SearchView.swift:19-24`) with a tab item and count from `filteredHits?.artists.count`, and render `hits.artists` in the `.all` band and in the `.artists` tab. Include artists in the `allCount` sum at `SearchView.swift:112-120` so the All tab total stays truthful. 4. **macOS: add a `venues` tab.** Split `SearchTab.songs` into `.songs` (slices where `kind == .song`) and `.venues` (slices where `kind == .venue`), each with its own count. Both bands appear in `.all`. 5. **macOS: add `searchArtistRow(artist:)`**, laid out in the same fixed-column ledger as the other rows but with the artist name spanning the ARTIST column and the count in the trailing column (guarded per step 1). Tap appends `appModel.path.append(.artist(artist))` — the same mechanism `ArtistsView.swift:88` and the existing slice row use. No play button: an artist has no single stream. 6. **macOS: fix the slice row layout.** Stop writing `slice.kind.heading` into the DATE column (`SearchView.swift:494-497`). Leave DATE empty for slices; put the artist in ARTIST and the slice label in TITLE as today, and render the count (when > 0) in the TIME · LIKES column so the venue name isn't displaced into the wrong cell. With the venue tab split (step 4), the row itself reads the same for both kinds — the tab carries the distinction. 7. **Android: parity check, guards only.** ARTISTS and VENUES sections already render correctly (`MainActivity.kt:2924-2934`, `2959-2976`). Only the zero-count guards from step 1 are needed. Do not restructure Android's layout. 8. **Document the data gap.** In `RelistenAPI.swift` (near `toSearchHits()`, ~line 715) and `Relisten.kt` (near line 372), add a short comment recording *why* the venue `PeriodRef` has no `showCount` — `/v3/search`'s `Venues` bucket has no count field — so the next reader doesn't re-derive it from scratch. 9. **DECISIONS.md:** log the decision with the next ID from `mahler next-id couch-tour D`. Record: (a) artists and venues get separate macOS tabs rather than headers inside the All band; (b) the count policy is *omit when unknown*, joining `/v3/artists` for artists and hiding it for venues, because the two backends differ in whether they know the number; (c) `SearchHits` stays flat — no new grouping type. Note the existing drift against D206 if you touch it. Test: what proves it - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` — new cases in `RelistenParsingTests.swift` (XCTest, `@testable import CouchTourKit`, class doc comment citing the decision ID) pinning that a search artist hit carries a zero/unknown count rather than a fabricated one, and that a venue `SliceHit`'s `period.showCount` is 0 because the payload has no count — document it as the reason the UI omits it, mirroring the existing `testAVenuesShowsParseTheSameWayWithTheVenuePopulatedUnlikeASearchHit`. - `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` — `RelistenParsingTest.kt` pins the same absence on the Android side. - Update the test counts in `README.md` when you add tests. - UI is untestable from `swift test` (the app target has no test target) — the manual pass below is the only check of the layout itself. ## Done when - [ ] macOS search for "moe" shows an **Artists** tab containing a `moe.` row; clicking it opens the artist screen (periods list), not a show. - [ ] macOS search shows a **Venues** tab separate from **Songs**; the Songs tab contains no venue rows and vice versa. - [ ] The All tab count equals the sum of every visible row across all tabs (artists and both slice kinds included). - [ ] No row on either platform renders the text "0 shows" for any query, on either tab. - [ ] On macOS, a search artist row shows a real count (e.g. moe. → 179-ish) sourced from `/v3/artists`, and omits it when unavailable. - [ ] macOS venue rows no longer print "Venues" (or "Songs") in the DATE column; DATE is empty and the count, when known, sits in the TIME · LIKES column. - [ ] Song slices still show their real count from `shows_played_at`. - [ ] Android search still renders ARTISTS and VENUES sections and navigates correctly; only the zero-count rendering changed. - [ ] `swift test` and `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` are green; `README.md` test counts updated. - [ ] DECISIONS.md has a new sequential `Dnnn` entry covering the tab layout and the omit-when-unknown count policy. - [ ] `scripts/check-fixtures.sh` passes (no fixture was edited). ## Needs a human to check - Open the macOS search results and look at them. Are the new Artists and Venues tabs legible in the ledger layout — column alignment, truncation of long artist/venue names, dark and light mode? - Confirm "0 shows" is gone on Android too (search "moe" on the phone). - Confirm the artist row's count looks right for a few artists you know (moe., Goose). - Judgment call only you can make: whether the Venues tab earns its own tab, or whether venues would read better as a second section inside Songs rather than a fifth tab. ## Context - **Root cause of the zero counts is upstream, not the UI.** Live `GET /v3/search?q=moe` returns `Artists[0]` with no `show_count` key, and a `Venues[0]` with only `slim_artist`/`artist_uuid`/`name`/`location`/`uuid`. `RelistenArtist.showCount` (`RelistenAPI.swift:41`) tolerantly decodes `?? 0`, so the model looks like it has data and doesn't — it has zeros. Only `/v3/artists` has real counts. - **The repo fixture is misleading.** `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/Fixtures/relisten_search.json:7` carries `"show_count": 187` on the artist, which does not match the live `/v3/search` payload. Fixtures are byte-compared against their Android counterparts by `scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, so do **not** edit the fixture to make a test pass — write the new assertions so they hold with or without the field. - Android has the identical venue bug in the mapper (`Relisten.kt:372` builds the venue `PeriodRef` with no `showCount`), but Android's section layout is correct, so only the rendering guards are needed there. - `SliceKind.heading` (`Catalog.swift:637-642`) already produces "Songs"/"Venues" — the string just needs a home where it isn't mistaken for a date. - Navigation precedent: `appModel.path.append(.artist(artist))` → `Route.artist` → `PeriodsView` via the single `navigationDestination` in `ThreePaneRootView.swift:100-125`. - ROADMAP.md:40 advertises search across "artists, shows, songs, and venues" as shipped (D169). macOS currently surfaces neither artists nor venues as distinct results — this issue makes the claim true. - Precedents for the count policy, both already merged: `ArtistsView.swift:92`, `PeriodsView.swift:45` (macOS, `> 0` guard) and `PlaybackService.kt:560-562` (Android, with the comment "a real showCount of 0 must not read the same as one with none"). - The macOS app target has no test target — `swift test` covers `CouchTourKit` only. Anything in `SearchView.swift` is verified by reading and by UAT, not by CI. ## Out of scope - The tag picker D206 describes for `SearchView` (an "All"-prefixed tag row, and picking a tag emptying the Artists/slice sections). It was never built and `UAT.md:43` marks it checked. File a separate issue. - Surfacing `SearchHits.failed` on macOS, which `filteredHits` carries and no view reads (Android shows it at `MainActivity.kt:2908-2919`). Separate issue. - Sorting slices by `SearchSortMode`. D210 scoped sorting to shows and tracks only. - Any change to the search fan-out, debounce, minimum-length, backends, or `Route`/`SearchHits` shape beyond what steps 1-6 need. - Fixing the unrelated hardcoded `PHISH` in `searchTrackRow` (`SearchView.swift:310-314`, `389-394`), which labels every track row "Phish" and navigates to the Phish show regardless of the hit. Worth its own issue.

column2: macOS: sidebar shows hardcoded mockup artists (Goose, WSP…) as favorites when list is empty
column3: > **Original request:** "macOS: sidebar shows hardcoded mockup artists (Goose, WSP…) as favorites when list is empty" ## Problem / goal `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift:16` has `fallbackFavoriteArtists`, hardcoded design-mockup data: Goose 412, Grateful Dead 2313, pgroove 276, Phish 1884, TAB 308, WSP 1102. It renders whenever `favoritedArtists` is empty. That covers every launch until `ThreePaneRootView.loadFavorites()` finishes, and permanently whenever the Relisten fetch fails (`try?` returns `[]`) or the user has no favorites. It came in with the Ledger redesign (D214, #133). It is the only place in either client where mockup data leaked into shipping code. Fix, per the report's three options: delete the fallback, replace the void with a muted "Star artists to pin them here" hint, and distinguish *still loading* from *loaded and empty* so the hint doesn't flash on every launch. Decisions made by the sort run (technical, recorded here so the builder doesn't re-ask): - **Empty state is a hint, not nothing.** A 236pt sidebar with a bare "FAVORITE ARTISTS" header and   no rows reads as broken. Copy follows the existing `ContentUnavailableView` voice used in   `ListeningView.swift:143` ("Shows you've played will show up here."): **"Star artists to pin them   here"**, in `colors.textSubtle`, 12pt, two lines, non-interactive, horizontally padded to match the   row inset (10pt) and offset to the badge column. No star icon — the section already has a header.   Wording is easy to retune; note it in `UAT.md` for the owner. - **Loading vs empty is a real distinction.** Add `isFavoritesLoaded: Bool` to `SidebarView` and a   matching `@State` in `ThreePaneRootView` set to `true` when `loadFavorites()` returns (including   when it returns empty because the fetch failed). While loading, render neither hint nor rows — just   the header and hairline. The header itself stays put; don't hide it during load, otherwise the   sidebar jumps. - **Sidebar favorites rows are pure state in CouchTourKit, not inline in the view.** The app target   has no unit-test harness (`swift test` covers only `CouchTourKit`, per AGENTS.md), so any   behavior we want pinned has to live in the package. Add   `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/SidebarFavorites.swift` with a   `SidebarFavoritesState` enum (`.loading` / `.empty` / `.artists([ArtistRef])`) and a pure   `sidebarFavoritesState(artists:isLoaded:)`; `SidebarView` switches on it. - **`showCount == 0` means "unknown", not "zero shows."** `PHISH` is a constant with   `showCount: 0` (`Catalog.swift:773`), which is why the sidebar renders "Phish 0". Add   `formatShowCount(_ n: Int) -> String?` to `Format.swift` — `nil` for `n <= 0`, decimal-grouped   otherwise — and have the sidebar render nothing in the count column when it's `nil`. Don't invent   a real Phish count; that needs a phish.in call and is out of scope. - **Favorites resolution in `loadFavorites()` is unchanged.** `mergeArtists` + the `favorites.keys`   filter stays exactly as it is; this issue only changes what's rendered when the result is empty. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ThreePaneRootView.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/SidebarFavorites.swift` (new) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Format.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/SidebarFavoritesTests.swift` (new) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/FormatTests.swift` - `UAT.md` - `README.md` - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: - Delete `SidebarView.fallbackFavoriteArtists` and the `favoritedArtists.isEmpty ? …` branch in   `sortedArtists`; the sidebar renders only what it is given. - Add `SidebarFavoritesState` + `sidebarFavoritesState(artists:isLoaded:)` to CouchTourKit. The   function must be total and offline: `.artists` sorted case-insensitively by name (keep today's   sort, it is what the rows render), `.loading` whenever `isLoaded == false` regardless of input,   `.empty` when loaded and the input is empty. - `SidebarView`: take `isFavoritesLoaded: Bool`; switch on `sidebarFavoritesState` — `.loading`   renders header + hairline only, `.empty` renders the hint text, `.artists` renders the rows.   Replace the inline count formatting with `formatShowCount` and render no text when it returns   `nil`. - `ThreePaneRootView`: add `@State private var favoritesLoaded = false`, pass it to `SidebarView`,   set it to `true` at the end of `loadFavorites()` on every path (including the   `try?` → `[]` failure path) so a failed fetch lands in `.empty` and never stays in `.loading`. - Add tests: `SidebarFavoritesTests` covering loading-with-artists, loaded-empty, loaded-non-empty   ordering, and that the list is returned verbatim (no injected artists); `FormatTests` cases for   `formatShowCount(0)`, `(-1)`, `1884`, `2313` grouping. - Log the empty-state and loading decision in `DECISIONS.md` with a fresh `Dnnn` from   `mahler next-id couch-tour D` — do not hand-pick an ID. - Add a `UAT.md` item for the empty sidebar and the "no 0 counts" check; bump the macOS package test   count in `README.md`. - Run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` and   `xcodebuild -project macos/CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`   (regenerate with `cd macos && xcodegen generate` first if the project file is a symlink into the   main checkout). Test: `swift test` in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` is green with the new cases, and it fails if anyone re-adds mock data (there is no constant left holding Goose/GD/WSP, and `sidebarFavoritesState(artists: [], isLoaded: true)` returns `.empty`). ## Done when - [ ] `grep -rn "widespread-panic\|perpetual-groove\|fallbackFavorite" macos app` returns nothing. - [ ] `SidebarView` has no hardcoded `ArtistRef` values; the only artists it can render come from       `favoritedArtists`. - [ ] With no favorites, the sidebar shows the "FAVORITE ARTISTS" header, the hairline, and the       hint — and no artist rows. - [ ] On a cold launch the hint does not appear before the real favorites do (header stays put, no       jump). - [ ] A `0` (or negative) show count renders as no text at all in the sidebar row, never "0". - [ ] Non-empty favorites still render in the same order and styling as before, and clicking a row       still navigates to that artist. - [ ] `swift test` in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` passes, including the new       `SidebarFavoritesTests` and `formatShowCount` cases. - [ ] `xcodebuild … -destination 'platform=macOS' build` succeeds. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new sequential entry; `UAT.md` has a new item; `README.md`'s macOS       package test count is bumped. - [ ] Branch pushed with `Fixes #347` in the commit/PR body. ## Needs a human to check - The exact empty-state wording and its visual weight in a 236pt sidebar (the builder's default is   "Star artists to pin them here" in `textSubtle`). - That the sidebar looks right on cold launch, with no flash or layout jump while favorites load. - That no sidebar row shows a "0" — specifically the Phish row, which is the reason the issue   mentions it. ## Context Original report, kept for the record: > Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29. This is why Goose appeared in the owner's prod favorites without ever > being starred. > > `macos/CouchTour/SidebarView.swift:16` has `fallbackFavoriteArtists`, hardcoded design-mockup data: > Goose 412, Grateful Dead 2313, pgroove 276, Phish 1884, TAB 308, WSP 1102. It renders whenever > `favoritedArtists` is empty. That covers every launch until `ThreePaneRootView.loadFavorites()` > finishes, and permanently whenever the Relisten fetch fails (`try?` returns `[]`) or the user has no > favorites. It came in with the Ledger redesign (D214, #133). > > **Fix:** > - Delete the fallback. > - Show nothing, or a "Star artists to pin them here" hint. > - Show the favorites that are known before the catalog loads (Phish is always resolvable), or a >   loading state. > > Related: the sidebar shows Phish with "0" shows, because `PHISH.showCount` is 0. Related issues: #348 also edits `SidebarView.swift` (adds an Artists entry) — coordinate through the `Files:` overlap. #351 (favorites don't sync between devices) and #345 (sandboxed vs local data store) can make a favorites list look empty; this issue makes that case render honestly instead of showing mock artists, but does not fix the sync/store causes. ## Out of scope - A real show count for Phish in the sidebar (would need a phish.in call; `PHISH.showCount` stays 0   and the row renders no count). - Resolving starred Relisten artists when the catalog fetch fails — offline favorites still won't   appear, they'll just show the hint now. - Adding an "Artists" browse entry to the sidebar (#348). - Favorites sync between devices (#351) and the sandboxed/local data-store split (#345). - Any Android change; the fallback exists only in the macOS client.

column2: macOS: Home's Next Tour Stops and On This Date blank after relaunch (failed load cached as empty)
column3: > **Original request:** "Found in beta UAT 2026-09-29. Reproduced 3/3 cold launches of the 0.86-beta built from `main`, and on the 0.84-beta. > > **Repro:** favorite at least one artist, quit, relaunch, wait 12s or more. Home shows "No upcoming tour stops" and "No shows on this date · 0 shows", even for Phish, which has 5 shows on 9/29. Un-starring and re-starring a favorite (which triggers `reloadDiscovery` with a new key) brings both sections back immediately. > > **Why it stays empty.** `OnThisDate.showsOnDate` (`CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift`) catches every per-artist error and returns `[]`. `OnThisDate.load` then caches that result under the day-plus-favorites key for the rest of the session, and `NextStop.load` does the same. So one failed or cancelled launch-time load blanks the shelves until the favorites change or the app restarts. The launch-time failure itself isn't pinned down yet; suspect the `HomeView` `.task` is cancelled or re-run during startup (sync kicks off at the same moment in `ThreePaneRootView`). > > **Fix:** > - Don't cache empty results or results with errors. > - Surface or retry failures instead of turning them into `[]`. > - Find what fails at launch. > - Check the Android side (`MainActivity.kt` `loadOnce`) for the same pattern." ## Problem / goal The macOS Home screen's "Next Tour Stops" and "On This Date" sections show empty state ("No upcoming tour stops" / "No shows on this date") after a cold launch, even when data exists (e.g., Phish has shows on the current date). The root cause is that both `OnThisDate.load` and `NextStop.load` cache empty results from failed or cancelled launch-time network requests. Once cached, the empty result persists for the session until favorites change or the app restarts. The same caching pattern exists on Android in `OnThisDate.kt` and `NextStop.kt`, where per-artist errors are caught and converted to empty lists, which are then cached. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/OnThisDate.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/NextStop.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/HomeView.swift` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDate.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NextStop.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` Steps: 1. **macOS: Fix `OnThisDate.load` to not cache empty results**    - Change the cache to only store non-empty results    - Return the empty result without caching it when the fetch yields no shows    - Add a `resetCache()` call path for explicit invalidation (already exists) 2. **macOS: Fix `NextStop.load` to not cache empty results**    - Same pattern: only cache when `shows.isNotEmpty`    - Return empty result without caching on failure 3. **macOS: Surface errors instead of swallowing them in `showsOnDate`**    - Change `showsOnDate` to throw on total failure (all artists failed) rather than returning `[]`    - Keep per-artist degradation (one artist failing doesn't fail the whole request)    - Update `OnThisDate.load` to catch and log errors, not cache on error 4. **macOS: Surface errors in `currentTours` / `NextStop.load`**    - Same pattern: throw on total failure, degrade per artist    - Update `NextStop.load` to catch and log errors, not cache on error 5. **macOS: Update `HomeView.reloadDiscovery` to handle errors**    - Show an error state in the UI instead of blank shelves when loads fail    - Add retry button or auto-retry logic 6. **Android: Fix `OnThisDate.load` to not cache empty results**    - Only cache when `shows.isNotEmpty()`    - Return empty list without caching on failure 7. **Android: Fix `NextStop.load` to not cache empty results**    - Only cache when `shows.isNotEmpty()` 8. **Android: Surface errors in `showsOnDate` and `currentTours`**    - Throw on total failure (all artists failed)    - Keep per-artist degradation 9. **Android: Update `MainActivity` UI to handle error state from `loadOnce`**    - The `loadOnce` already returns `Result<T>?`; ensure error state shows retry option instead of blank 10. **Investigate launch-time task cancellation**     - Check `ThreePaneRootView` sync startup interaction with `HomeView .task`     - Ensure discovery loads aren't cancelled by sync initialization Test: what proves it - Cold launch with favorites → both sections populate within 12s (not blank) - Network failure at launch → sections show retry/error state, not blank cached empty - Toggle favorite off/on → sections refresh correctly (cache invalidation works) - Unit tests: `OnThisDateTests.testOnThisDateCacheInvalidation` and `NextStopTests.testNextStopCacheInvalidation` should verify empty results aren't cached - Android unit tests: `OnThisDateTest` and `NextStopTest` cache tests should verify same ## Done when - [ ] macOS `OnThisDate.load` does not cache empty results - [ ] macOS `NextStop.load` does not cache empty results - [ ] macOS `showsOnDate` throws on total failure, degrades per artist - [ ] macOS `currentTours` throws on total failure, degrades per artist - [ ] macOS `HomeView` shows error/retry state for failed discovery loads - [ ] Android `OnThisDate.load` does not cache empty results - [ ] Android `NextStop.load` does not cache empty results - [ ] Android `showsOnDate` throws on total failure, degrades per artist - [ ] Android `currentTours` throws on total failure, degrades per artist - [ ] Android `MainActivity` shows error/retry state for failed discovery loads - [ ] Launch-time sync/task cancellation root cause identified and fixed (or documented as known limitation with workaround) - [ ] All existing unit tests pass (macOS: `swift test` in CouchTourKit; Android: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`) - [ ] New unit tests added for "empty result not cached" behavior ## Needs a human to check - Cold launch UX: verify sections populate within reasonable time on real network - Error state UI: verify retry button works and doesn't look broken - Cross-device sync interaction: verify sync startup doesn't cancel discovery loads ## Context - The issue was found in beta UAT (0.86-beta and 0.84-beta) - The problem affects both macOS and Android platforms - The caching is in-memory only (process death clears it) - Un-starring/re-starring a favorite works because it changes the cache key - Related to D162 (daily cache for discovery rows) and D164 (Next Stop caching) ## Out of scope - Persistent disk caching for discovery rows (current in-memory cache is intentional per D162) - Offline support (explicitly not planned per README) - Changing the per-artist degradation strategy (it's correct: one artist failing shouldn't fail all) - The `loadOnce` composable pattern on Android (it correctly preserves error state; only the data layer caching needs fix)

column2: macOS: sandboxed (Sparkle) and locally-installed builds use different data stores — favorites/settings swap or vanish
column3: > **Original request:** "macOS: sandboxed (Sparkle) and locally-installed builds use different data stores — favorites/settings swap or vanish" ## Problem / goal The macOS app has two installation paths that produce different sandbox states, causing data to live in two separate locations: - **Sparkle updates (CI builds)**: Built with `com.apple.security.app-sandbox: true` entitlement (per `macos/project.yml` D104). Data lives in container paths:   - `UserDefaults` → `~/Library/Containers/<bundle>/Data/Library/Preferences/`   - `phishin.db` → `~/Library/Containers/<bundle>/Data/Library/Application Support/...`   - Sync cursors (`SyncTokenStore`) → same container `UserDefaults` - **Local installs (`install.sh`, `install-beta.sh`)**: Re-sign with `codesign --force --deep --sign -` (no `--entitlements`), which strips the sandbox entitlement. Data lives in standard paths:   - `UserDefaults` → `~/Library/Preferences/`   - `phishin.db` → `~/Library/Application Support/...`   - Sync cursors → standard `UserDefaults` Moving between a Sparkle update and a local install silently swaps or loses: - Favorite artists (`Favorites` — UserDefaults) - Liked Relisten tracks (`LikedTracks` — UserDefaults) - Playback settings (`PlaybackSettings` — UserDefaults: skip filler, volume leveling) - Theme settings (`ThemeSettings` — UserDefaults) - Sync watermarks/cursors (`SyncTokenStore` — UserDefaults) - Listening history & resume positions (`ProgressStore` — phishin.db GRDB) History *can* be recovered via cross-device sync, but favorites/likes/settings/sync cursors are not synced and are simply lost or replaced. **Observed on the owner's Mac:** Prod unsandboxed prefs have favorites `[phish]` and a 20-row DB current today. The prod container has no favorites and an 11-row DB last written 2026-08-25. For the beta, the container holds `[moe, phish]` and the unsandboxed plist holds `[phish, moe, grateful-dead]`. Replacing the Sparkle 0.84-beta with a locally built `main` beta made the sidebar show Grateful Dead again. ## Plan **Decision (D-entry to be logged):** Keep App Sandbox enabled (the intended default per D104). Fix local install scripts to preserve entitlements, and add a one-time migration on first sandboxed launch that merges data from the unsandboxed stores into the sandboxed ones. Never discard either side. Files: - `macos/scripts/install.sh` - `macos/scripts/install-beta.sh` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/ProgressStore.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Favorites.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/LikedTracks.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PlaybackSettings.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/ThemeSettings.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Sync.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Migration.swift` (new) - `DECISIONS.md` Steps: 1. Update `install.sh` and `install-beta.sh` to re-sign with `--entitlements` pointing at the generated entitlements file (`Generated/CouchTour.entitlements` / `Generated/CouchTourBeta/CouchTour.entitlements`) so local installs stay sandboxed. 2. Create `Migration.swift` in CouchTourKit with a one-time `migrateFromUnsandboxedIfNeeded()` that:    - Detects if unsandboxed stores exist and sandboxed stores are empty/newer    - Merges `UserDefaults` keys: `favorite_artist_keys`, `liked_relisten_track_ids`, `skip_filler_tracks`, `level_volume`, `app_theme_mode`, `sync.lastSeq`, `sync.lastPushWatermark`, `sync.lastSyncedAt`    - Merges `phishin.db` rows (INSERT OR REPLACE on `queueKey`, preferring higher `updatedAt`)    - Runs once per bundle (tracked via a `migration_done_v1` UserDefaults flag in the sandboxed container) 3. Call `migrateFromUnsandboxedIfNeeded()` early in `AppModel.init()` before constructing `ProgressStore`, `Favorites`, `LikedTracks`, `PlaybackSettings`, `ThemeSettings`, `SyncTokenStore`. 4. Log a D-entry in `DECISIONS.md` recording the decision to keep sandboxing and the migration approach. 5. Hold prod Sparkle updates until this lands (as noted in the issue). Test: what proves it - Build locally with `install.sh`, add favorites, change settings, play some shows → verify data in `~/Library/Containers/dev.mike.couchtour.mac/Data/...` - Simulate a Sparkle update by running the signed app from the container path → verify all data persists - Simulate the reverse: populate unsandboxed stores, run sandboxed app → verify migration merges data correctly (unit test in `MigrationTests.swift`) - Verify beta target (`dev.mike.couchtour.mac.beta`) migrates its own separate unsandboxed stores independently ## Done when - [ ] `install.sh` and `install-beta.sh` re-sign with `--entitlements` preserving sandbox - [ ] `Migration.swift` created with one-time merge logic for all affected stores - [ ] `AppModel.init()` calls migration before initializing stores - [ ] Unit tests for migration logic (merging UserDefaults keys, merging phishin.db rows, idempotency) - [ ] D-entry logged in `DECISIONS.md` - [ ] Manual verification: local install → add data → Sparkle-style launch → data intact ## Needs a human to check - Verify on the owner's Mac that after the fix, a local install followed by a Sparkle update (or vice versa) preserves favorites, liked tracks, settings, sync pairing, and listening history without loss or duplication. ## Context - D104: App Sandbox enabled by design for future Mac App Store readiness - `project.yml` declares entitlements for both `CouchTour` and `CouchTourBeta` targets - Beta target already uses separate bundle ID (`dev.mike.couchtour.mac.beta`) and separate GRDB directory (`dev.mike.couchtour.beta`) — migration must handle each bundle independently - Keychain items (`SyncTokenStore.deviceToken`, `PhishInSession` token) are already namespaced by service name and unaffected by sandbox state - Android side unaffected (no sandbox concept) ## Out of scope - Changing the sandbox decision (D104 stands) - Syncing favorites/likes across devices (separate feature) - Migrating data from Android (separate "import from phone" feature) - Any changes to the Sparkle CI workflow (it already produces sandboxed builds)

column2: Correctness bug scan: CouchTourKit (loudness shift, date bounds, progress-save error handling)
column3: > **Original request:** Correctness Bug Scan — logic errors, off-by-one and boundary conditions, incorrect error handling or silently-swallowed exceptions, race conditions between concurrent runs, and edge cases (None/empty/malformed input) found by close reading or targeted tests. Not style, structure or refactoring — that's the health pass. Part of #327 ## Problem / goal Correctness bugs in `CouchTourKit`, the macOS package that holds all the app's testable logic. Three concrete defects were found by close reading during planning, seeded here so this is a fix-with-regression-test rather than an open-ended hunt: **F1 — `LoudnessMeter.slideBlock()` copies overlapping memory with a non-overlapping primitive (`Loudness.swift:184-192`).** ```swift let keep = blockSize - stepSize channelBlockBuf[ch].withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer { buf in     buf.baseAddress!.advanced(by: 0)         .update(from: buf.baseAddress!.advanced(by: stepSize), count: keep) } ``` `blockSize` is 0.4 s of samples and `stepSize` is 0.1 s (`Loudness.swift:130-132`), so this copies `[stepSize, blockSize)` onto `[0, keep)` **within the same buffer** — the two regions overlap across 0.2 s of samples. `UnsafeMutablePointer.update(from:count:)` is documented as requiring the source and destination regions not to overlap; this is undefined behaviour and the correct primitive is `memmove`. It may happen to produce the right answer with the current compiler and still stop doing so after any optimiser change. When it bites, the corrupted 0.4 s block feeds `emitBlock()`, which feeds the gated integration, which produces a wrong LUFS — and that number becomes the volume-leveling gain. **F2 — `formatShowDate` accepts impossible months and days (`Format.swift:72-94`).** The numeric branch checks only `y > 1900 && y < 2100` and then formats whatever it was given, so `"2020-99-99"` is returned as a well-formed-looking `"2020-99-99"` and the `DateFormatter` fallback below it is never reached for that input. Month and day need the same bounding the year has. **F3 — `ProgressRecorder.saveTick` reports success for a write that failed, and then never retries it (`ProgressRecorder.swift:26-66`).** The method advances `lastSaveTime`, `lastSavedQueueKey`, `lastSavedTrackIndex` and `lastSavedPositionMs` *before* the write, then calls `try? store.put(row)` — discarding the error — and returns `true`, which its own doc defines as "a record was actually written to the store". So a failed write is indistinguishable from a successful one, and because the dedupe guard at the top now matches the position that was never stored, the *next* tick at that same position short-circuits and returns early. The listening position is dropped with no log and no retry. The state update must happen only after a successful write, the error must be surfaced (at minimum logged), and the return value must mean what it says. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Loudness.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Format.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/ProgressRecorder.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/QueueKey.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/LoudnessTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/FormatTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/ProgressRecorderTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/QueueKeyTests.swift` - `README.md` Steps: - Fix F1 by replacing the `update(from:count:)` call with `memmove` (or an equivalent explicitly overlap-safe move) over the same byte range. Keep `blockPos = keep`. Add a `LoudnessTests` case that feeds a synthetic signal long enough to force several `slideBlock()` calls and asserts the resulting LUFS against a value computed the slow way (or against a known-good constant for a full-scale sine), so a regression in the shift shows up as a wrong number rather than passing silently. - Fix F2 by bounding month to 1...12 and day to 1...31 in the numeric branch, letting anything outside fall through to the existing `DateFormatter` attempts and then to the raw string. Do not change what the valid path returns. - Fix F3 by moving the `lastSave*` assignments to after a successful `store.put(row)`, catching and logging the error instead of `try?`, and returning `false` when the write failed. Add a `ProgressRecorderTests` case with a store that throws, asserting `saveTick` returns `false` and that an immediately following call at the same position *does* attempt the write again. - Then read `QueueKey.swift` for the same defect classes (off-by-one, empty/malformed input, silently-swallowed errors) and fix what you find, with a test. Compare it against Android's `Queue.kt` — the two are ports and any disagreement about which keys parse is itself a finding. - Update the macOS test count on `README.md:119`.
