column2: Correctness bug scan: Android pure-logic modules (dates, keys, formatting, discovery)
column3: > **Original request:** Correctness Bug Scan — logic errors, off-by-one and boundary conditions, incorrect error handling or silently-swallowed exceptions, race conditions between concurrent runs, and edge cases (None/empty/malformed input) found by close reading or targeted tests. Not style, structure or refactoring — that's the health pass. Part of #327 ## Problem / goal Correctness bugs in the Android client's **pure-logic modules** — the date, key, format and discovery helpers that have no Compose or Media3 dependency and are therefore fully testable with the existing Robolectric suite. Five concrete defects were found by close reading during planning. They are seeded here so this is a fix-with-regression-test rather than an open-ended hunt: **F1 — `phishInRanges` merges non-adjacent year spans, double-fetching shows (`OnThisDate.kt:106-127`).** The greedy batcher accumulates into `minOf(last.first.first, span.first)..maxOf(last.first.last, span.last)` and never checks that the spans it is merging are actually *consecutive*, nor that `periods` arrived in ascending order. The KDoc says "consecutive periods accumulate" — nothing enforces it. `periods` comes straight from `src.periods(artist)` in whatever order the API returns. An out-of-order or overlapping input yields overlapping `year_range=` batches, the same show is fetched by two batches, and `showsOnAnniversary` returns it twice — a duplicate card in the Home "On this date" row. **F2 — `OnThisDate.load` is a check-then-act race (`OnThisDate.kt:216-222`).** `cached` is `@Volatile`, which makes the read visible but not the read-modify-write atomic. Two concurrent Home compositions both miss the cache and each fire the full fan-out — up to ~19 network requests apiece, on a path that is explicitly budgeted (`RELISTEN_YEAR_BUDGET`) precisely because it is expensive. **F3 — `monthDay` validates hyphen positions but not digits (`OnThisDate.kt:55-56`).** `date.length == 10 && date[4] == '-' && date[7] == '-'` accepts `"abcd-ef-gh"`, so malformed catalog data flows into `showsOnAnniversary` as a legitimate month/day and can match other malformed rows. `yearOf` inherits the same hole. **F4 — `formatCompactDuration` silently drops seconds past an hour (`Format.kt:43-54`).** Its own KDoc promises `"1:06", "1:35", "2:41", "0:45"` — m:ss. For `h > 0` it returns `"%d:%02d".format(h, m)`, so a 1 h 5 min 30 s track renders `"1:05"`, indistinguishable from 65 seconds. Either the format or the doc is wrong; pick one, check every call site, and make the code and the doc agree. **F5 — `formatShowDate` gives up where the macOS port succeeds (`Format.kt:59-70`).** Android matches `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, then tries `LocalDate.parse` (which only accepts ISO), then returns the raw string. The macOS port (`Format.swift`) additionally accepts `YYYY/MM/DD`, zero-pads single-digit months and days, and falls back through `"MMMM d, yyyy"` / `"MMM d, yyyy"`. The same catalog string therefore renders differently on the two platforms. Bring Android up to the macOS behaviour — these are ports of one function and the divergence is the bug. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDate.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Format.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Queue.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/FillerTracks.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/OnThisDateTest.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/FormatTest.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/QueueTest.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/FillerTracksTest.kt` - `README.md` Steps: - Fresh worktree setup first: `echo "sdk.dir=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" > local.properties`. - Fix F1: sort the derived spans ascending before batching and only merge a span into the current batch when it is contiguous with (or overlaps) it *and* the combined show count is within `cap`. Keep the existing "a single period larger than `cap` becomes its own batch" behaviour and the always-hyphenated output id. - Fix F2: make `OnThisDate.load` deduplicate concurrent callers. A `kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Mutex` around the miss path, re-checking the key inside the lock, is enough and matches the coroutine idiom already in this file — do not introduce a new concurrency primitive. Keep `cached` internal so the existing test reset still works. - Fix F3: require digits in `monthDay`, not just hyphen positions. - Fix F4: decide whether hour-long durations should render `h:mm:ss` or stay `h:mm`, read every call site before choosing, apply it, and correct the KDoc so the two agree. - Fix F5: extend `formatShowDate` to match `Format.swift`'s accepted inputs and zero-padding, **and** reject out-of-range months and days the way #330 is adding them (`"2020-99-99"` must not come back as a well-formed-looking date — Android has the same hole today via its `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` regex). Do not change `Format.swift`. - Then read the remaining files in the list above — `Queue.kt` and `FillerTracks.kt` — for the same defect classes (off-by-one, empty/malformed input, silently-swallowed exceptions) and fix what you find there. Two starting points already noticed: `parseQueueKey` rejects the two-part key `recordingShowKey` produces, and `filterPlaybackTracks` falls back to the unfiltered list when every track is filler — confirm each is intended before changing it. - Add a regression test for every fix, in the matching existing test file. A fix without a test that fails before it does not count. - Update the Android test count on `README.md:110`. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` — green, with the new tests failing against the unfixed code. ## Done when - [ ] `phishInRanges` produces non-overlapping, ascending batches from an unsorted or gapped period list; a test feeds it out-of-order periods and asserts no year appears in two batches. - [ ] Two concurrent `OnThisDate.load` calls with the same key perform one fan-out, proven by a test counting fetches through the injectable `source` seam. - [ ] `monthDay("abcd-ef-gh")` returns null; a test covers it. - [ ] `formatCompactDuration`'s output and its KDoc agree for a duration over an hour, and a test pins the chosen behaviour. - [ ] `formatShowDate` accepts every input `Format.swift`'s port accepts and returns the same string for each; tests cover `YYYY/MM/DD`, a single-digit month/day, and an out-of-range month or day. - [ ] Any further defect found in `Queue.kt` or `FillerTracks.kt` is either fixed with a test or has a comment recording why the current behaviour is correct. - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes and `README.md:110` states the new Android test count. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing. Every change is in pure functions covered by the local Robolectric suite; no UI or playback surface moves. If F4 changes what a duration looks like on screen, note the before/after in the commit message so it can be eyeballed in the next beta. ## Context Java is not on `PATH` in this environment — always build with Android Studio's bundled JDK, as in the Test line above. Tests are local (Robolectric + MockWebServer); run them after any change. `Format.kt` and `OnThisDate.kt` have line-for-line ports under `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/`. Where the two disagree, that disagreement is itself a finding — but fix it only on the side named in the plan, so #330 (macOS) and #328 (sync) never edit the same behaviour from both ends. Scope is deliberately bounded to the files listed. A defect found outside them should be filed as its own issue with `mahler add couch-tour "…"`, not fixed here — the `Files:` list is what the scheduler uses to keep concurrent builds off each other. ## Out of scope - `MainActivity.kt`, `PlaybackService.kt`, `PlayerViewModel.kt` and every Compose surface — too large to scan safely in one run, and `PlaybackService.kt` is claimed by #267. - `PlaybackSettings.kt` and `SettingsScreen.kt` (#267, #269), and `TvBrowse.kt` (#226). - `Loudness.kt` / `SourceLoudness.kt` — the volume-leveling chain is mid-flight in #267/#269. - The macOS and sync sides — #330 and #328. - Room migrations and any `PhishInDb` schema change. - Style, structure or refactoring — that is the health pass (#197).

column2: Correctness bug scan: sync backend merge & cursor arithmetic (+ first test harness)
column3: > **Original request:** Correctness Bug Scan — logic errors, off-by-one and boundary conditions, incorrect error handling or silently-swallowed exceptions, race conditions between concurrent runs, and edge cases (None/empty/malformed input) found by close reading or targeted tests. Not style, structure or refactoring — that's the health pass. Part of #327 ## Problem / goal Correctness bugs in the sync backend (`sync/src/`), the one component where a logic error silently corrupts data on **every** paired device at once rather than just misdrawing one screen. A close read of `sync/src/index.ts` during planning found four concrete defects. They are seeded below so this issue is a fix-with-regression-test, not an open-ended hunt: **F1 — a push containing the same `queueKey` twice merges by array order, not by `updatedAt`.** `applyIncomingChanges` builds `existingByKey` from a *snapshot* of the DB (`index.ts:381-390`) and then filters each incoming change against that snapshot alone. Two entries in the same `changes[]` array with the same `queueKey` therefore both survive the LWW filter, both get a seq slot, and both become `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` statements in one `env.DB.batch()`. D1 applies a batch in order, so **the last one in the array wins regardless of its `updatedAt`** — an older position can overwrite a newer one. The surviving row also carries the *lower* of the two allocated seqs, leaving a seq the pull query will never return. Both clients chunk their own pushes and are unlikely to produce a dup today, but the server must not be corruptible by a client that does. **F2 — the returned cursor is computed from a stale read of `seqs`, so a concurrent push makes the client re-pull forever.** `handleSync` reads `cursor.next` at `index.ts:305`, *before* `applyIncomingChanges` performs the atomic `UPDATE seqs SET next = next + ? ... RETURNING next`. It then reports `seq: Math.max(cursor.next - 1 + appliedCount, since)` (`index.ts:349-355`). If another device in the same group pushes between the read and the bump, the rows this response returns carry seqs *higher* than the cursor it reports. The client stores the low cursor, and pulls the same rows again on its next sync — every sync, for as long as pushes keep interleaving. Two devices listening at once is the normal case for this app, not an exotic one. The returned cursor must come from state read after the bump (e.g. the max `seq` of the rows actually being returned). **F3 — `trackIndex` and `positionMs` accept any safe integer, including negatives.** `parseProgressFields` (`index.ts:243-248`) validates type but not range. A negative `trackIndex` is written to `progress` and handed straight back to both clients, which index a track list with it. `positionMs` and `deletedAt` have the same gap. **F4 — `purgeOldTombstones` reports a row count from a different read than the delete.** `index.ts:494-515` computes `COUNT(*)` and `MAX(seq)` in one statement and deletes with the same predicate in a separate `env.DB.batch()`. A tombstone crossing `cutoff` between the two is deleted but not counted (or vice versa), so `rowsPurged` — the only observability this cron job has — can be wrong. Confirm, then either make the count come from the delete or document why the drift is acceptable. **There is no test harness in `sync/` at all.** `npm run typecheck` and a live staging smoke test in `sync-deploy.yml` are the entire safety net, so none of the above can be proven fixed. Adding one is part of this issue. ## Plan Files: - `sync/src/index.ts` - `sync/package.json` - `sync/vitest.config.ts` - `sync/test/sync.test.ts` - `.github/workflows/sync-deploy.yml` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: - Add `vitest` + `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` as devDependencies and a `vitest.config.ts` using `defineWorkersConfig` with the existing `wrangler.toml`, so tests run against real Miniflare D1 rather than a mock. **This choice is already made — do not substitute a hand-rolled mock**; F1 and F2 are both about what D1 actually does under batched and interleaved writes, and a mock would assert the bug rather than catch it. Apply `schema.sql` in a `beforeEach`. Add `"test": "vitest run"` to `package.json`. - Fix F1: dedupe `incoming` by `queueKey` *before* the LWW filter, keeping the entry with the highest `updatedAt` (ties → last occurrence, matching the documented "whichever arrives later wins" rule), so exactly one statement and one seq are allocated per key. - Fix F2: stop deriving the response cursor from the pre-bump `cursor.next`. Return the max `seq` among the rows selected for the response, falling back to `since` when there are none. - Fix F3: reject negative `trackIndex`, `positionMs` and `deletedAt` in `parseProgressFields` with the existing `ValidationError` → 400 path. Keep the existing message style (`changes[i].field must be ...`). - Investigate F4 and either fix it or leave a comment saying why the drift is tolerable. Do not skip it silently. - Write one regression test per fix: a dup-key push resolves to the newest `updatedAt`; a push interleaved with a second group member's push returns a cursor no lower than any seq it returned, and a follow-up sync with that cursor returns nothing; negative `trackIndex`/`positionMs`/`deletedAt` each 400; the existing happy paths (pair → claim → sync round trip, 410 on a stale cursor, `since = 0` exemption) still pass. - Wire `npm test` into `sync-deploy.yml` so it gates the deploy, in the same job as the existing `typecheck`. - Log one `DECISIONS.md` entry for adopting `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` as the sync test harness. Allocate the ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` — do not grep the file. - Add a short "sync backend tests" line to the `## Tests` section of `README.md`, in the voice of the Android and macOS lines already there. Test: `cd sync && npm install && npm run typecheck && npm test` — all green, with a failing-before/passing-after test for each of F1, F2 and F3. ## Done when - [ ] `cd sync && npm test` runs a real vitest suite against Miniflare D1 and passes. - [ ] A push containing two entries with the same `queueKey` stores the one with the higher `updatedAt`, allocates exactly one seq, and a test proves it. - [ ] The `seq` returned by `POST /sync` is never lower than the seq of any row in the same response, including when another device's push interleaves; a test proves the follow-up sync returns zero rows. - [ ] Negative `trackIndex`, `positionMs` or `deletedAt` each produce a 400 with a `changes[i].<field>` message; tests cover all three. - [ ] F4 is either fixed or has a comment in `purgeOldTombstones` explaining why the count drift is acceptable. - [ ] `sync-deploy.yml` runs `npm test` and fails the deploy when it fails. - [ ] `DECISIONS.md` has a new sequential `Dnnn` entry for the test-harness choice. - [ ] `README.md`'s `## Tests` section mentions the sync suite. - [ ] `cd sync && npm run typecheck` still passes. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing. Every change here is server-side and covered by the new suite; the existing staging smoke test in `sync-deploy.yml` still exercises the live pairing path on merge. ## Context `sync/` is a Cloudflare Worker + D1 service (`https://couch-tour-sync.mkastellec.workers.dev`). Never deploy by hand — `.github/workflows/sync-deploy.yml` deploys to staging, smoke-tests, migrates and promotes to prod on push to `main`. Prior hardening passes (D150–D154, #203) covered input validation, request-size caps, the D1 100-bound-parameter limit, push draining, rate limiting and error shaping. This issue is the layer under that: the merge and cursor arithmetic those guards protect. The `progress` table is listening history. Nothing here may drop or rewrite rows outside the documented LWW rule. ## Out of scope - The Android and macOS sync clients (`Sync.kt`, `Sync.swift`) — covered by #329 (Android) and #330 (macOS). - `schema.sql` changes and any D1 migration. - Rate limiting, auth, token rotation and pairing, unless a concrete correctness defect is found in them — those were #203's ground. - Style, structure or refactoring — that is the health pass (#197), not this one. - Deploying. Job ends at the push.

column2: macOS: cast/AirPlay button is missing whenever no show is loaded (no button on Home)
column3: > **Original request:** google cast support in desktop client, with button always visible. Can use native airplay wiidget, so long as cast devices and groups show up > > **Environment** > - App Version: 0.83 > - Screen: Home > - Device: Macmini9,1 > - macOS: Version 26.6.2 (Build 25G83) > - Channel: Production ## Problem / goal On macOS the Cast/AirPlay control only exists inside the "something is playing" branches, so on Home with an empty player — exactly where this was filed from — there is no cast button at all and the AirPlay destination picker is unreachable too. `macos/CouchTour/CastRoutePicker.swift` already does everything the feedback asks of the control itself: one popover listing live-discovered Google Cast receivers (`CastRoutePickerMenu`, `CastRoutePicker.swift:34`) **and** the native system AirPlay picker (`AirRoutePickerView`, wrapping `AVRoutePickerView`, `AirRoutePicker.swift:5`; embedded at `CastRoutePicker.swift:155`). D196 shipped it that way. What is missing is a *home* for it that survives an empty player. Today it is mounted in two places, both conditional: - `PlayerRailView.swift:379` — inside the `if let show = player.show` branch (`:79`), so   `fallbackRailContent` (`:422`) renders instead and the button vanishes. This is the reported bug. - `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:416` — in the sheet's footer, unconditional, fine as-is. The sheet   covers the window, so the toolbar is not reachable while it is open. Android already matches the request: `CastButton()` is in the shared `Header` composable (`MainActivity.kt:4387`), so it is top-right on every screen. Goal: exactly one always-available Cast + AirPlay control in the macOS window chrome, on every center-pane screen (Home, search, artist, show, playlists), in every playback state, with Cast receivers/groups and the native AirPlay picker both reachable from it. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/ThreePaneRootView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlayerRailView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/CastRoutePicker.swift` - `DECISIONS.md` - `UAT.md` Steps: 1. **Mount the control in the window toolbar, not the content.** `ThreePaneRootView.swift:36-54`    already declares the center-pane `NavigationStack`'s `.toolbar` (back button, breadcrumb, search    field, feedback, expanded-player). That toolbar is on the `NavigationStack`, so anything in it    appears on *every* center-pane route and in every playback state — the macOS counterpart of    Android's shared `Header`. Add:    ```swift    ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) {        CastRoutePickerButton()    }    ```    Declare it so it lands in the same top-right position as on Android. SwiftUI orders    `.primaryAction` items right-to-left in declaration order, so put this `ToolbarItem` **before**    the `searchField` / `FeedbackButton` items if you want it furthest right; match what looks right    and say which you chose in the DECISIONS entry. 2. **Remove the player-rail copy — move, don't duplicate.** Delete `CastRoutePickerButton()` from    `PlayerRailView.swift:377-382`; keep `volumeControl` in that slot with the same `.padding(.top, 12)`    / `.padding(.bottom, 26)`. Two live pickers on screen at once (rail + toolbar) is the "third    copy" the backlog-pruning pass explicitly ruled out, and both start/stop `CastDiscovery` on    appear/disappear, so duplicates are also a discovery-lifecycle hazard. 3. **Label the control for VoiceOver and hover.** `CastRoutePickerButton`'s label is an    `HStack` whose text only appears while casting, so unlabelled it is an icon-only button with no    accessible name. Add `.accessibilityLabel("Cast and AirPlay destinations")` and    `.help("Cast and AirPlay destinations")` to the `Button` in `CastRoutePicker.swift:10-25`. This    applies to the toolbar instance and the `ExpandedNowPlayingView` one for free; do not write the    string twice. 4. **Always visible, unlike Android.** Do **not** gate the button on `castDiscovery.devices`    being non-empty. Android hides it until a receiver appears (README "Casting"), which is correct    there because it is a Cast-only control. On macOS this control is also the audio-output/AirPlay    picker, which is useful with zero Cast receivers on the network, and the owner asked for it    always visible. The popover already handles the empty case ("Searching for Cast devices on local    network…" at `CastRoutePicker.swift:91-95`). No change needed there — just don't add the gate. 5. **Do not change the picker itself.** Discovery, connection, the cast banner, `Disconnect Cast`,    and `AirRoutePickerView` all work; this issue is placement only. 6. **Log the decision.** Allocate a fresh ID with `mahler next-id couch-tour D` and append a `Dnnn`    entry to `DECISIONS.md` (append; do not edit D196) recording:    - the Cast + AirPlay control is window chrome: it lives in the center-pane toolbar and is      present in every playback state, with the player-rail copy removed as a move rather than a      duplication;    - unlike Android, it is not hidden when no Cast receiver is discovered, because it is also the      system audio-output picker;    - reference D196 as the entry that shipped the protocol + picker, and #311 as the placement fix. 7. **Add a UAT item** with the next free id (the series currently ends at `uat-069`) covering the    checks in "Needs a human to check" below. Test: what proves it - Build: `cd macos && xcodegen generate` (only if the `.xcodeproj` is a symlink into the main   checkout — see AGENTS.md), then   `xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`.   Paste the output in the PR body; the Mac app target is not in CI. - `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` is still green at 448. No test changes are expected —   nothing in `CouchTourKit` is touched and the app target has no test target, so placement is a   build + UAT concern. Do not add a test to hit a count; do not change the README test counts. - Source-level checks an agent *can* run:   - `grep -n "CastRoutePickerButton" macos/CouchTour/*.swift` returns exactly the toolbar call in     `ThreePaneRootView.swift` and the one in `ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` — no hit in     `PlayerRailView.swift`.   - the toolbar call site is **not** nested inside any `if let show` / `if player.…` — visually     confirm the indentation level of the new `ToolbarItem` matches the sibling toolbar items at     `ThreePaneRootView.swift:41-53`. ## Done when - [ ] The Cast/AirPlay button is present in the macOS window toolbar on **every** center-pane       screen — Home, search, artist, show, playlists — with nothing playing, and while playing. - [ ] It is the only such control on screen while playing: the player rail's footer shows the volume       control only, and no `CastRoutePickerButton` remains in `PlayerRailView.swift`. - [ ] Tapping it opens the popover listing discovered Google Cast receivers (with model name and a       checkmark on the active one), the "Casting to …" banner plus **Disconnect Cast** while a       session is live, and the system AirPlay picker at the bottom. - [ ] The button is visible when no Cast receiver exists on the network; the popover says it is       searching and the AirPlay picker still works. - [ ] The button has an accessibility label and a `.help` tooltip, and casting state is still shown       in the label (filled `tv.and.mediabox` + device name) exactly as before. - [ ] The expanded Now Playing sheet still shows its own copy (`ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift:416`),       since it covers the toolbar. - [ ] A `Dnnn` entry in `DECISIONS.md` (allocated via `mahler next-id couch-tour D`) and a new       `UAT.md` item exist; `swift test` is green at 448 and the app target builds. ## Needs a human to check - Cold-launch Couch Tour on the Mac with **nothing** playing, on Home: the cast/AirPlay button is   in the top right of the window. (This is the reported bug — confirm it is fixed by using it.) - From a second device, cast to a Chromecast/Google TV group **with nothing playing first**, then   start playback: the button then shows the filled cast icon and the device name, and playback   moves to the receiver. - Open the picker with an AirPlay speaker (HomePod / Apple TV) on the network and a Cast receiver   present: both sections list their devices, and the system AirPlay picker still works from the   popover. - VoiceOver on the toolbar button reads a sensible name rather than nothing. - Toolbar ordering looks right next to search, feedback and the expanded-player button (a taste   call the owner should eyeball once). ## Context - D196 (`DECISIONS.md:2834`) shipped Desktop Cast & AirPlay: Bonjour discovery, the cast sender   protocol, `AirRoutePicker.swift`, and the `CastRoutePickerButton` popover. column2: periodic scans for feature parity between macos and android apps
column3: ## Goal The macOS and Android clients drift apart feature by feature. Parity work so far has been one-shot (`docs/plans/DESKTOP-PARITY-PLAN.md`, per-feature parity issues). This issue does a **baseline parity audit now**. Making it repeat is mahler#606 (project-defined maintenance passes). Once that ships, this spec becomes the recurring `parity` pass, and this issue closes after the baseline. ## What the scan produces 1. A report at `docs/PARITY_AUDIT.md`: a table of user-facing features (rows) × macOS / Android (columns), each cell *present*, *partial* (with a note) or *missing*. Cover navigation destinations, search result types, playback controls, library/favorites, account views, downloads/offline, Cast/AirPlay, settings and feedback. 2. One new issue per real gap (label `mahler`, a `type:`, and a `size:`), in the standard body shape. Skip gaps that are deliberate platform differences (e.g. a menu bar item only on macOS). List those in the report as intentional. Link, don't re-file, gaps that already have an open issue. 3. A checklist comment on this issue linking the report and every issue filed or linked. ## How - Walk each client's entry points (Android `MainActivity.kt` navigation and screens, macOS `ThreePaneRootView.swift` / `SidebarView.swift` and their destinations) and list what the user can reach and do. - Compare against `docs/plans/DESKTOP-PARITY-PLAN.md` to mark what that plan closed and what regressed since. - Coordinate with #356 (Ledger redesign audit): findings it already filed count as linked, not new. ## Done when - `docs/PARITY_AUDIT.md` is committed, and the checklist comment is posted with every gap filed or linked.

column2: Volume leveling 4/5: macOS decode-ahead measurement + MTAudioProcessingTap gain + Settings toggle
column3: > **Original request:** > ## Goal > The same feature as #267 on macOS: background measurement, per-item gain, and a Settings toggle. >  > ## Scope > - **Measurement (in `CouchTourKit`, so `swift test` covers it):** a `LoudnessMeasurer` actor that range-fetches 30 s from the middle of up to 3 MP3 tracks per uncached `levelingKey`, writes each segment to a temp file under Caches (not `~/Documents`), decodes it with `AVAudioFile` into float PCM for the meter, stores the result in the cache, and deletes the temp files. Inject the network and the decoder so tests can use fixture PCM and a stub URLProtocol. Cancellation and failure work as in #267. > - **Gain application (app target, `Player.swift`):** each `AVPlayerItem` gets an `AVMutableAudioMix` whose input parameters use an `MTAudioProcessingTap` for a linear gain, because `AVPlayer.volume` caps at 1.0 and can't boost. Set the gain when the item is created, and update it in place if a measurement lands mid-play. The app-level `volume` stays a separate multiplier on top. > - **Settings:** a "Level volume across sources" toggle, off by default, with the same help text as Android. >  > ## Done when > `swift test` passes with the new measurer tests and the app target builds. Per CLAUDE.md, **check that the build actually sees the worktree's sources** (D206/D207). UAT.md gets the macOS versions of the AUD/SBD comparison items, and the README test count is updated. >  > ## Shared design (from #18, owner chose strategy (a)) > - **Granularity is the source, not the track.** One gain per *leveling key*: `show:<date>` for a phish.in show (its single mix), `relisten:<artist>/<date>/<sourceId>` for a Relisten tape. This matches the existing queue-key grammar (`Queue.kt` / `QueueKey.swift`) — but it has to be derivable **per track**, because playlist queues mix tracks from different shows/sources. > - **Measurement:** ITU-R BS.1770-4 integrated loudness (K-weighting, 400 ms blocks with 75% overlap, -70 LUFS absolute gate, -10 LU relative gate) plus sample peak, over a *sample* of the source: up to 3 tracks, 30 s from each, taken from the middle of the track and pooled into one gated measurement. Decode-ahead means the measurement happens from HTTP Range requests against the MP3 URL (never FLAC — same master, much bigger), in the background, not from the live playback pipeline. > - **Gain rule:** `gainDb = clamp(-18 LUFS - measured, -12, +12)`, then capped at `-1 dBFS - samplePeakDb` so a boost never clips. It's a single static gain for the whole source — no compressor, no limiter — which is what keeps dynamic range intact. Unknown loudness means 0 dB. > - **The cache is local-only and never synced.** It's derived data that can always be re-measured, and each row carries an `algorithmVersion`, so a change to the meter makes old rows stale instead of wrong. > - **Cast gets no leveling.** The receiver decodes the audio, so there's nothing for the app to apply gain to. Say so in the Settings help text. Part of #18 Depends on: #265 Depends on: #266 ## Problem / goal Implement volume leveling on macOS, matching the feature on Android. This includes background measurement of tracks via decode-ahead, applying per-item gain using `MTAudioProcessingTap`, and adding a Settings toggle to enable/disable it. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/LoudnessMeasurer.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/LoudnessMeasurerTests.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/Player.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PlaybackSettings.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlaybackSettingsView.swift` - `UAT.md` - `README.md` Steps: 1. Add `levelVolume` toggle to `PlaybackSettings.swift` (default false). 2. Add the toggle UI in `PlaybackSettingsView.swift` with help text explaining that Cast gets no leveling. 3. Implement `LoudnessMeasurer.swift` in `CouchTourKit`. It should take a `levelingKey` and a list of tracks, select up to 3 tracks, make HTTP Range requests (30s from the middle) for MP3s, decode with `AVAudioFile` into float PCM, measure loudness/peak using the meter (#265), cache the result (#266), and delete temp files. Make sure network and decoder are injectable for tests. 4. Implement `LoudnessMeasurerTests.swift` using fixture PCM and stub `URLProtocol`. 5. Update `Player.swift` to initialize an `AVMutableAudioMix` with `MTAudioProcessingTap` for each `AVPlayerItem`. 6. Calculate the `gainDb = clamp(-18 LUFS - measured, -12, +12)`, capped at `-1 dBFS - samplePeakDb`. Apply linear gain via the tap in `Player.swift`. Update this gain in place if a measurement completes mid-play. 7. Update `UAT.md` with macOS versions of the AUD/SBD comparison items for manual testing. 8. Update `README.md` test count. Test: `swift test` passes for new measurer tests. App target builds successfully (confirming build sees the worktree's sources per D206/D207). ## Done when - [ ] `PlaybackSettings` has `levelVolume` toggle, exposed in `PlaybackSettingsView` with correct help text. - [ ] `LoudnessMeasurer` successfully downloads, decodes, measures, and caches up to 30s segments from 3 tracks per leveling key. - [ ] Temporary audio files are cleaned up correctly after measurement. - [ ] Unit tests for `LoudnessMeasurer` pass with injected networking and decoding. - [ ] `Player.swift` applies linear gain dynamically using `MTAudioProcessingTap` and `AVMutableAudioMix`. - [ ] The app builds successfully and sees worktree sources. - [ ] `UAT.md` includes manual testing steps for macOS volume leveling. - [ ] `README.md` test count is updated. ## Needs a human to check - Real playback with volume leveling enabled sounds balanced and doesn't clip, tested across different AUD/SBD sources. ## Context See #18 and #267. This relies on the meter from #265 and cache from #266. ## Out of scope - Cast volume leveling (handled remotely, not in scope). - FLAC measurement (use MP3 URL for measurement).

column2: Volume leveling 1/5: BS.1770 loudness meter + gain rule + per-track leveling key (both platforms)
column3: > **Original request:** Add an option for source/show-level volume leveling — not traditional per-track loudness normalization, but matching the average sound level across quiet and loud recordings so different sources/shows play back at comparable volume. Part of #18 ## Problem / goal Pure, platform-neutral loudness math has to exist on both clients before any measurement pipeline, cache table, or gain-application work can be built on top of it (#266-269). Today neither `PlayableTrack` model carries enough source identity to build a "leveling key" for a Relisten track, and neither platform has BS.1770 loudness measurement code at all. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Loudness.kt` (new) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Loudness.swift` (new) - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt` (`PlayableTrack`: add a source-id field + `levelingKey`) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift` (same, Swift side) - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Relisten.kt` (populate the new field from the chosen `RelistenSource`) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/RelistenAPI.swift` (same, Swift side) - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/LoudnessTest.kt` (new) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/LoudnessTests.swift` (new) - `README.md` (test counts) Steps: 1. Kotlin `Loudness.kt`: `LoudnessMeter` — feed interleaved float PCM (any sample rate 22.05–96kHz, mono or stereo); K-weighting filter coefficients derived from the sample rate (not a fixed 48kHz table); 400ms blocks with 75% overlap; BS.1770-4 gating (-70 LUFS absolute gate, -10 LU relative gate); tracks running sample peak in dBFS across all fed audio. 2. Pooling: `LoudnessMeter` accumulates blocks across multiple `feed()` calls (segments) and produces one integrated measurement over all of them when queried — this is what lets #267/#268 feed several 30s track samples into one meter per source. 3. `levelingGainDb(lufs, peakDb)`: `clamp(-18 - lufs, -12.0, 12.0)`, then capped at `-1.0 - peakDb` so a boost never clips; unmeasured loudness (`null`/`nil`) returns `0.0`. 4. Add a source-id field to `PlayableTrack` (Kotlin + Swift). `RelistenSourceTrack.toPlayableTrack` (`Relisten.kt:274`) and its Swift equivalent (`RelistenAPI.swift:570`) don't currently receive the chosen source's uuid or the artist slug — thread them through from `toShowDetail`/the call site the same way `RecordingId`/`recordingQueueKey` already do for queue keys (`chosen.uuid`, `artist.slug`). 5. Add `PlayableTrack.levelingKey: String` (computed). phish.in tracks (no source id) → `show:<showDate>` via the existing `showQueueKey`; Relisten tracks → `relisten:<artistSlug>/<showDate>/<sourceId>` via the existing `recordingQueueKey`/`RECORDING_PREFIX` in `Queue.kt` (and the Swift equivalents in `QueueKey.swift`) — byte-identical to the existing queue-key grammar, per CLAUDE.md's sync-key convention. 6. Swift `Loudness.swift`: port the same math (`LoudnessMeter`, `levelingGainDb`) with the same block/gate constants, so a value computed by one platform matches the other within the test tolerance for the same signal. 7. `LoudnessTest.kt` / `LoudnessTests.swift`, same vectors on both platforms: 997Hz sine at -20dBFS, stereo, 48kHz → -23.0 ±0.1 LUFS; the same signal at 44.1kHz; pure silence → no measurement (`null`/`nil` lufs); gain clamps at ±12dB; the peak cap prevents clipping; `levelingKey` is correct for a phish.in-style track (showDate only) and a Relisten-style track (artistSlug/date/sourceId). 8. Update the README's Android and macOS test counts. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` and `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` both pass, including the new `LoudnessTest`/`LoudnessTests` suites with the vectors above. ## Done when - [ ] `LoudnessMeter` exists on both platforms and computes BS.1770-4 integrated LUFS + sample peak dBFS from interleaved float PCM at any sample rate 22.05–96kHz, mono or stereo. - [ ] `LoudnessMeter` pools multiple discontinuous segments fed via separate calls into one gated measurement. - [ ] `levelingGainDb(lufs, peakDb)` implements `clamp(-18 - lufs, -12, 12)` capped at `-1 - peakDb`; unmeasured (`null`/`nil`) lufs returns `0`. - [ ] `PlayableTrack` (Kotlin + Swift) carries enough source identity for a Relisten track to compute a `levelingKey`, populated in `Relisten.kt`/`RelistenAPI.swift`. - [ ] `PlayableTrack.levelingKey` returns `show:<date>` for phish.in tracks and `relisten:<artistSlug>/<date>/<sourceId>` for Relisten tracks, matching the existing queue-key grammar exactly. - [ ] Both test suites pass, including the shared vectors (997Hz sine -20dBFS @ 48kHz → -23.0±0.1 LUFS; same @ 44.1kHz; silence gated to no measurement; gain clamp; peak cap; `levelingKey` correctness). - [ ] README's Android and macOS test counts are updated. - [ ] Neither `Loudness.kt` nor `Loudness.swift` has any I/O or player dependency (ExoPlayer/AVFoundation) — pure math only; measurement/caching/gain-application land in #266-268, not here. ## Needs a human to check Nothing — this is pure math with fixed, objective test vectors; correctness is fully verifiable by the test suite, no listening or product judgment required. ## Context - Part of #18 (source/show-level volume leveling), which the owner already resolved on strategy: client-side decode-ahead measurement, cached locally, dynamics preserved (no compressor/limiter). - Sibling sub-issues: #266 (cache table — needs only the key *format*, fixed here, so it can build in parallel), #267 (Android measurement + gain plumbing + Settings toggle), #268 (macOS equivalent), #269 (default-on decision, clear-cache action, docs after beta UAT). - Existing key grammar to match exactly: `Queue.kt` / `QueueKey.swift` — `showQueueKey`, `recordingQueueKey`/`RECORDING_PREFIX` (`"relisten:"`), `RecordingId`. - `PlayableTrack` today: `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt:290`, `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift:474` — no source-id field yet. ## Out of scope - The actual measurement pipeline (HTTP Range requests against MP3 URLs, background scheduling) — #267 (Android), #268 (macOS). - The `source_loudness` cache table/migrations — #266. - Applying gain to playback (AudioProcessor / MTAudioProcessingTap) and the Settings toggle — #267/#268. - Default-on decision, clear-cache action, and docs/DECISIONS.md/README/ROADMAP updates for #18 itself — #269 (and #18's own remaining checklist items). - Cast leveling — explicitly out of scope per the shared design (the receiver decodes audio, so there's nothing to apply gain to).

column2: sync/: add staging Worker + smoke-test gate, auto-promote to prod on merge
column3: ## Context `sync/` (the Cloudflare Worker + D1 backend, D119-D127) deploys straight to the single production Worker (`couch-tour-sync.mkastellec.workers.dev`) via a manual `npm run deploy`. There is no staging environment and no gate — CLAUDE.md's own description is "day-to-day work runs locally with no Cloudflare account needed... then smoke-tested against the real deployment (D124-D127)," i.e. the first real test today happens *in* production. Unlike the native apps, this is a stateless API with existing `tsc --noEmit` coverage and no UI a human needs to click through — it's a good fit for auto-deploy-on-green rather than a manual gate (owner confirmed 2026-09-13; see the companion issue for why the native apps are staying manual for now). ## Goal Every merge to `main` that touches `sync/**` auto-deploys to a staging Worker, runs a smoke test against it, and only then auto-promotes to production. No manual step. ## Concrete changes 1. **`sync/wrangler.toml`**: add an `[env.staging]` block with its own D1 database (create    `couch-tour-sync-staging`, migrate `schema.sql` into it) and its own Worker name (e.g.    `couch-tour-sync-staging`), separate from the prod binding. 2. **`sync/src/index.ts`**: add `GET /health` — unauthenticated, returns 200 and does a    trivial D1 read (e.g. `SELECT 1`) so the smoke test proves the DB binding is actually live,    not just that the Worker booted. No CORS headers, matching the existing policy (D149). 3. **New GH Actions workflow** (or extend an existing one), triggered on push to `main`    touching `sync/**`:    - `npm ci && npm run typecheck`    - `wrangler deploy --env staging` (+ `wrangler d1 execute ... --env staging` against      staging if `schema.sql` changed)    - smoke test against staging: `GET /health`, plus one full `/pair/start` → `/pair/claim`      round trip to exercise the real auth/pairing path, not just reachability    - only on success: `wrangler deploy` (prod) + `db:migrate:remote` if schema changed    - on any failure: stop, no prod deploy — the workflow going red is the notification 4. **Secrets**: check whether a Cloudflare API token with Workers + D1 edit scope already    exists as a repo secret for GH Actions; add one (scoped, not the account-wide token) if not. 5. **`CLAUDE.md`**: update the `sync/` section to describe the new pipeline and retire the    "smoke-tested against the real deployment" manual step. ## Out of scope Native app (Android/macOS) promotion — that stays the manual beta gate for now; see the companion issue. ## Verify `npm run typecheck` plus the new workflow's own smoke-test step passing against staging before it touches prod.

column2: Android Security & Surface Area Audit
column3: > **Original request:** Security & Surface Area Audit — credential boundaries (`.env` leaks, unpooled URLs), subshell executions (`subprocess.run` argument sanitization), permission boundaries, denial list checks, dependency scans. Part of #222 ## Problem / goal Audit the Android (`app/`) client for permission boundaries, denial list checks, and dependency scans. Scan for credential leaks and subshell executions. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` - `gradle/libs.versions.toml` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MediaItems.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Cast.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/SecurityValidatorTest.kt` Steps: 1. **Permissions**: review every `<uses-permission>` in `AndroidManifest.xml` against the code that uses it. Drop `WAKE_LOCK` (nothing in `app/src/main/` acquires a wake lock; the foreground service keeps the device awake on its own) and `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` (only the Cast framework's own reconnection service consumes it; the manifest is not the place to keep it for a dependency). Keep `INTERNET`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, and `CAMERA` (declared optional, QR pairing only). 2. **Dependency scan**: no dependency-audit Gradle plugin is configured (confirmed: `settings.gradle.kts` has only `dependencyResolutionManagement` with the two standard repos, and `app/build.gradle.kts` declares no audit plugin). Scan `gradle/libs.versions.toml` against the published CVE list for the pinned versions — the ones to check are `okhttp 4.12.0`, `media3 1.10.1`, `play-services-cast-framework 22.1.0`, `room 2.6.1`, `androidx-security-crypto 1.1.0-alpha06`, `workManager 2.11.2`, `coil 2.7.0`, `camerax 1.4.1`, `mlkitBarcode 17.3.0`, `zxingCore 3.5.3`. Update any with an open CVE and record the audited baseline versions as a comment block at the top of `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. 3. **Credential boundaries**: confirm no `.env` or hardcoded secret exists anywhere under `app/src/main/`. The only credentials in the app are the phish.in JWT (stored in `Auth.kt` via `EncryptedSharedPreferences` under the `androidx.security.crypto` master key) and the sync device token (`Sync.kt`, same scheme). Both are confirmed encrypted at rest; no plaintext fallback path exists. The release keystore path/password come from `local.properties`, which is gitignored — verify `app/build.gradle.kts` never logs or embeds them. 4. **URL boundary / unpooled URLs**: every outbound URL in `app/src/main/` must pass through an `OkHttpClient` (phish.in: `PhishInApi` in `Api.kt`; Relisten: `RelistenApi` in `Relisten.kt`; sync: `SyncApi` in `Sync.kt`) or be a hardcoded, app-controlled constant (`FeedbackButton.kt` issue tracker, `Catalog.kt` share URLs). Track-level audio URLs from the API (`Track.mp3Url`, `PlayableTrack.url`) are the one untrusted input that reaches the player — they already flow through `String.requireHttps()` in `MediaItems.kt:307`, which rejects anything not starting with `https://` (including `file://`, `content://`, and `http://`) and returns `"https://invalid"` instead. Extend that coverage: audit `Uri.parse()` call sites (`Waveform.kt:56` image load, `PlaybackService.kt:416` artwork, `MediaItems.kt:206` artwork, `FeedbackButton.kt:39` external link) and confirm each is either a hardcoded constant or already normalized through `requireHttps()`. 5. **Subshell executions**: there are none in `app/src/main/`. The only `ProcessBuilder`/`exec` in the whole `app/` tree is in `app/build.gradle.kts:31`, where it runs a fixed `git tag`/`gh release` command to derive a version name — no user-controlled input reaches it. Confirm by grep and record the result. 6. **Denial list checks**: the existing `requireHttps()` guard is the denial list. Add a unit test in `SecurityValidatorTest.kt` covering the waveform-image and artwork `Uri.parse` paths (a `file://` waveform URL and a `content://` artwork URL must not reach the image loader/player), and a test asserting `requireHttps` is idempotent on already-`https://` input. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests dev.mike.couchtour.SecurityValidatorTest` passes, including the new URL-path coverage cases. Dependency versions in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` are checked against the published CVE list; any with an open CVE are updated and the audited baseline recorded as a comment block at the top of `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. ## Done when - [ ] `AndroidManifest.xml` declares only permissions the code actually uses; `WAKE_LOCK` and `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` are removed - [ ] `gradle/libs.versions.toml` is scanned against the published CVE list; any vulnerable dependency is updated and the audited baseline recorded as a comment block at the top of `gradle/libs.versions.toml` - [ ] No `.env` file, hardcoded secret, or plaintext credential path exists anywhere under `app/src/main/` - [ ] Every outbound URL in `app/src/main/` is either app-controlled or normalized through `requireHttps()`; the four `Uri.parse` call sites are audited and safe - [ ] No subshell execution in `app/src/main/`; the one in `app/build.gradle.kts` takes no user input - [ ] `SecurityValidatorTest.kt` covers the waveform/artwork URL paths and `requireHttps` idempotency - [ ] Full suite green: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context Client apps should only request permissions they strictly need. ## Out of scope - macOS audit (#248) - Implementing new privacy features

column2: Part 2 of #209: Analyze and mitigate run duration outliers
column3: > **Original request:** Token Economy/Quota & Performance Hygiene — prompt context bloat in recipes/rules, run duration outliers, excessive polling overhead, DB query efficiency. Part of #209 Depends on: #242 ## Problem / goal Identify the root cause of "run duration outliers" referenced in the performance hygiene goal (e.g., Cloudflare Worker CPU limits, CI job timeouts, or specific application workflows) and mitigate them. Run duration outliers — operations that intermittently or periodically take far longer than expected — waste resources across three subsystems. All three have been audited: 1. **CI workflows** — None of the four workflows in `.github/workflows/` set `timeout-minutes`. A hung job (e.g. a deadlocked test, a stalled Gradle daemon, or a network hang in xcodebuild) runs until GitHub's 360-minute default, silently burning CI minutes with no signal to anyone. 2. **Cloudflare Worker** — `handleSync` in `sync/src/index.ts` performs up to five separate D1 round trips per request (token auth, seq cursor read, optional token-rotation update, chunked key-existence lookups, batched row writes, outgoing change SELECT, final seq read) with no elapsed-time logging. A sync near the 500-row server cap could approach Cloudflare's 50ms CPU limit and there's no way to tell which requests are slow until the client reports a timeout. 3. **Android SyncApi client** — `Api.kt` (phish.in) and `Relisten.kt` received D176's `TimingEventListener` (connection-reuse + elapsed-time logs), but `Sync.kt` (the sync backend client) did not. Sync runs via WorkManager every 15 minutes and at app launch — exactly the conditions D176 identified for a pooled keep-alive connection going stale while the app is backgrounded and triggering a 30s read timeout before failing. The D176 diagnostic coverage was never completed to the sync client. D175 (Iteration 38) already fixed a concrete app-workflow outlier — `resolveLocalPlaylistTracks` was doing N sequential HTTP fetches, now concurrent — and D176 (Iteration 39) added instrumentation to PhishInApi/RelistenApi and resume timing to `PlayerViewModel`. This issue audits all three remaining domains and mitigates the most concrete gap (CI timeouts) while instrumenting the other two for future diagnosis. ## Plan Files: - `.github/workflows/test.yml` - `.github/workflows/macos-tests.yml` - `.github/workflows/build-debug-apk.yml` - `.github/workflows/macos-release.yml` - `sync/src/index.ts` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Sync.kt` Steps: - Add `timeout-minutes` to each CI workflow job at the job level (same indentation as `runs-on`): test.yml (10 min — tests run in under 1 min per CLAUDE.md), macos-tests.yml (15 min — swift test), build-debug-apk.yml (30 min — Gradle assemble), macos-release.yml (45 min — xcodebuild + Sparkle signing + git retry loop all under 25 min normally) - Add elapsed-time `console.log` at the end of Worker `handleSync` in `sync/src/index.ts`, logging total ms alongside incoming change count and outgoing row count — placed after the DB reads but before the return so it captures the full request cost including the push-then-pull round trip - Add `.eventListenerFactory { TimingEventListener("SyncApi") }` to the SyncApi OkHttpClient in `Sync.kt`, matching the D176 instrumentation on PhishInApi — the `runCatching` wrapper inside `TimingEventListener` (ApiTiming.kt:30) keeps existing `SyncApiRequestTest`/`SyncSessionTest` unaffected since they don't use Robolectric and `android.util.Log` throws in that environment Test: `npm run typecheck` in `sync/` for Worker timing code; `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` (JAVA_HOME set to Android Studio's JBR) for the SyncApi timing listener — `SyncApiRequestTest` and `SyncSessionTest` exercise the real OkHttpClient against MockWebServer and pass with the listener attached because `TimingEventListener` swallows `Log` calls via `runCatching`; validate workflow YAML with `gh workflow view` or yamllint ## Done when - [ ] All four CI workflow jobs (`test`, `macos-test`, `build`, `build-macos`) set `timeout-minutes` - [ ] Worker `handleSync` logs elapsed time, incoming change count, and outgoing row count - [ ] Android `SyncApi` OkHttpClient has `TimingEventListener("SyncApi")` attached - [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes in `sync/` - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes (SyncApiRequestTest, SyncSessionTest green with the new listener) - [ ] All four workflow YAML files parse without error ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context D175 fixed the 30-second Android resume for local playlists by replacing `associateWith` (sequential `await` per show) with `coroutineScope { refs.map { async { ... } }.awaitAll() }` (concurrent fan-out). D176 added `TimingEventListener` to `PhishInApi`/`RelistenApi` and resume-timing/error logs to `PlayerViewModel.resume()` — but the diagnostic coverage stopped there: SyncApi's OkHttpClient never got the listener, the Worker has zero elapsed-time logging, and the CI workflows inherited GitHub's 360-minute default timeout with no override. This issue closes those three gaps. The D176 theory (stale pooled connection → 30s read timeout → retry succeeds in ~200ms) has not yet been confirmed on Mike's device; that confirmation and any resulting retry/timeout tuning is explicitly out of scope here (would be a follow-up once the logging has had a chance to fire on a real outlier). ## Out of scope - Excessive sync polling overhead (Part 1 of #209, #242) - Test suite execution time creep (#199 / #213) - OkHttp read-timeout tuning or retry-on-timeout for stale pooled connections — D176's logging must first confirm the theory on Mike's device; this issue stops at completing the diagnostic coverage to SyncApi - macOS SyncAPI timing instrumentation — no existing timing infrastructure on the Swift side; would be a larger change beyond this batch - Cloudflare Worker CPU-limit optimization (query tuning, batching changes) — that is DB query efficiency, tracked in #241

column2: Part 3.3 of #200: Audit and optimize Sync backend DB query efficiency
column3: > **Original request:** Token Economy/Quota & Performance Hygiene — prompt context bloat in recipes/rules, run duration outliers, excessive polling overhead, DB query efficiency. Part of #210 ## Problem / goal Audit and optimize database query efficiency for the Sync backend (D1). The `progress` table is the feature — it holds every device's listening position and history and grows without bound — so the two queries that scan it on a schedule (the daily tombstone purge) and the one that lists a group's devices are the places a missing index or a redundant round trip shows up first. ## Plan Files: - `sync/schema.sql` - `sync/src/index.ts` Steps: 1. Audit every D1 query in `sync/src/index.ts` against `sync/schema.sql` and confirm which are already index-backed and which are not. Findings:    - `POST /sync` pull (`SELECT * FROM progress WHERE groupId = ? AND seq > ? ORDER BY seq ASC`) — served by `progress_seq (groupId, seq)`. Already optimal.    - `applyIncomingChanges` existence lookup (`... WHERE groupId = ? AND queueKey IN (...)`) — `(groupId, queueKey)` is the PK. Already optimal; the 90-key chunking is the real bound (D1's 100-param limit), not the index.    - `authenticate` (`... WHERE tokenHash = ? OR (previousTokenHash = ? AND previousTokenExpiresAt > ?)`) — `tokenHash` is UNIQUE-indexed and `previousTokenHash` is indexed. Already optimal.    - `handleDevicesList` (`SELECT id, name, platform, createdAt, lastSeenAt FROM devices WHERE groupId = ? AND revokedAt IS NULL`) — **not indexed on `groupId`**, so it scans the whole `devices` table per group. Add a covering index.    - `purgeOldTombstones` (`SELECT groupId, MAX(seq) ... FROM progress WHERE deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND deletedAt < ? GROUP BY groupId`, then a per-group `DELETE ... WHERE groupId = ? AND deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND deletedAt < ?`) — **full table scan of `progress` on every cron run**, and it is the one query whose cost grows with total history. Add an index on `deletedAt`. 2. In `sync/schema.sql`, add:    - `CREATE INDEX devices_group_revoked ON devices(groupId, revokedAt, id, name, platform, createdAt, lastSeenAt);` — covering for `handleDevicesList`, so the device list is an index-only read.    - `CREATE INDEX progress_deletedAt_seq ON progress(deletedAt, groupId, seq);` — serves both the purge candidate scan (the `deletedAt < ?` predicate) and the `MAX(seq)`/`GROUP BY groupId` per group, and covers the follow-up `DELETE` per group. 3. In `sync/src/index.ts`, eliminate the redundant second seq read in `handleSync`. The cursor is read once before the push (`SELECT next, retentionFloorSeq FROM seqs WHERE groupId = ?`); after `applyIncomingChanges` bumps `next` by the number of applied rows, `currentSeq` is `cursor.next - 1 + appliedCount` — the trailing `SELECT next FROM seqs WHERE groupId = ?` is a second round trip for a value already derivable. Have `applyIncomingChanges` return the count of applied rows and compute `currentSeq` from it. When no changes were applied the counter did not move, so `currentSeq = cursor.next - 1`. 4. Apply and verify locally before touching production:    - `cd sync && npm run typecheck` (must pass).    - `npm run db:migrate:local` (must apply the new indices cleanly).    - `npm run dev`, then exercise against local D1: a push/pull round trip returns the same `seq` as before the change (regression), `GET /devices` lists paired devices, and a tombstone older than 180 days is purged with `retentionFloorSeq` raised first.    - Confirm the new indices are used: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the devices-list query and on the purge candidate query should show the new indices rather than `SCAN TABLE`. ## Done when - [ ] `sync/schema.sql` contains `devices_group_revoked` and `progress_deletedAt_seq` indices, and no D1 query in `sync/src/index.ts` does a bare `SCAN TABLE` that an index would prevent. - [ ] `handleSync` no longer issues a second `SELECT next FROM seqs` after the push; `currentSeq` is derived from the pre-push cursor and the applied-row count. - [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes. - [ ] `npm run db:migrate:local` applies the updated schema without error. - [ ] A push/pull round trip against `wrangler dev` returns the correct `seq` and `changes`, and `GET /devices` plus the purge path still behave as before (regression). - [ ] A `DECISIONS.md` entry is added per repo conventions (the sync iteration log requires it). ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context This is Part 3.3 of #200 (Part 3 of #210), scoped to the Cloudflare Worker Sync backend only. Parts 3.1 (#239, Android Room) and 3.2 (#240, macOS GRDB) cover the clients and touch entirely different files; nothing here depends on them and they do not depend on this. The schema change is additive (new indices, no column or table changes, no data migration), so it applies cleanly to an existing production D1 database via `npm run db:migrate:remote` followed by `npm run deploy` — no downtime, since `CREATE INDEX` does not block reads on D1. The `progress` table is the whole point of the backend: it stores listening position and history so the app can never lose it. Indices here are cheap insurance against that table growing, and the purge query is the one whose cost scales with total history rather than with group size. The `authenticate` per-request `UPDATE ... SET lastSeenAt` is deliberately left alone — it is a single-row write by PK and changing it would alter the device-list freshness contract, which is out of scope for a query-efficiency pass. ## Out of scope - Application polling optimizations (handled in Part 2, #209). - Prompt context bloat (handled in Part 1, #208). - Android (Room) queries (#239) and macOS (GRDB) queries (#240). - Changing the `lastSeenAt` write-on-every-authenticated-request behavior, or the last-write-wins conflict-resolution logic itself.

column2: Part 3.2 of #200: Audit and optimize macOS DB query efficiency
column3: > **Original request:** Token Economy/Quota & Performance Hygiene — prompt context bloat in recipes/rules, run duration outliers, excessive polling overhead, DB query efficiency. ## Problem / goal Audit and optimize the macOS client's GRDB queries. The `progress` table grows for the life of an install, and the current hot reads scan or sort it; playlist track reads sort after an index lookup, and sync fetches all changed rows before sorting them in Swift. Make the hot paths index-backed and move ordering into SQLite without changing persisted data or sync semantics. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/ProgressStore.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Sync.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/LocalPlaylist.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/ProgressStoreTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/SyncTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/LocalPlaylistTests.swift` - `DECISIONS.md` - `README.md` Steps: 1. Inventory every GRDB read in `ProgressStore`, `LocalPlaylistStore`, and the sync push path. Populate an in-memory database with representative progress and playlist rows, then capture `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the current queries so the audit distinguishes proven scans/sorts from small-table queries that need no index. 2. Add additive, non-destructive GRDB migrations using `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`:    - In `ProgressStore.swift`, add `idx_progress_live_updated_at ON progress(updatedAt DESC) WHERE deletedAt IS NULL`, `idx_progress_in_progress_updated_at ON progress(updatedAt DESC) WHERE finished = 0 AND dismissed = 0 AND deletedAt IS NULL`, `idx_progress_artist_updated_at ON progress(artist, updatedAt DESC) WHERE deletedAt IS NULL`, and `idx_progress_changed_since_updated_at ON progress(updatedAt)`.    - In `LocalPlaylist.swift`, add `idx_local_playlist_tracks_playlist_position ON local_playlist_tracks(playlistId, position)`.    - Use new migration names (`v10_progressIndexes` and `v10_localPlaylistIndexes`); do not fold them into migrations that existing installs have already run, alter columns, drop tables, or perform a destructive migration. 3. Make `ProgressStore.changedSince(_:)` return rows ordered by `updatedAt` ascending, then remove the `.sorted { $0.updatedAt < $1.updatedAt }` step from `SyncSession.syncOnce`. Keep `chunkToPush`, the 400-row batch limit, and the same-timestamp boundary behavior unchanged. 4. Add tests that prove the indexes exist and are used: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` assertions for progress history, Continue Listening, artist history, distinct artists, and changed-since queries; an assertion that playlist tracks use the composite `(playlistId, position)` index without a temporary sort; a migration-preservation test with pre-existing rows; and an out-of-order sync-backlog test proving rows are pushed in ascending `updatedAt` order. 5. Run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test`, update the macOS test count in `README.md` to the actual result, and append a `DECISIONS.md` entry with the next available `Dnn` identifier recording the index choices and query-plan evidence. Test: Query-plan assertions reject bare `SCAN progress` or `SCAN local_playlist_tracks` steps that do not use an index, and reject `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` for the named hot paths; existing progress, playlist, migration, and sync chunk-boundary tests continue to pass; the full Swift package suite passes. ## Done when - [ ] The audit records `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` evidence for every GRDB read in the three source files, with no bare table scan or temporary sort left on a growing-table hot path. - [ ] The five named additive indexes exist after migration, and the progress indexes are present on an existing database that already contains listening-history rows. - [ ] `ProgressStore.changedSince(_:)` returns ascending `updatedAt` order and `SyncSession.syncOnce` no longer sorts the fetched array in Swift. - [ ] `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows the new indexes for progress history/Continue Listening/artist/changed-since queries and the composite index for playlist track reads. - [ ] Existing Continue Listening, history, artist filtering, tombstone, playlist CRUD/order, sync batching, and same-timestamp chunk-boundary behavior is unchanged. - [ ] `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes, `README.md` reports the resulting macOS test count, and `DECISIONS.md` contains the new decision entry. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing ## Context Part of #210 The macOS package is plain SwiftPM and uses GRDB 6.29. `ProgressStore` and `LocalPlaylistStore` share one `DatabaseQueue` and the existing `phishin.db`; the `progress` table is the feature and must never be destructively migrated. The current `progress` table has no secondary indexes, while `SyncSession.syncOnce` fetches changed rows and then performs an in-memory sort. This issue is macOS-only: Android Room is #239 and the D1 backend is #241. ## Out of scope - Application polling optimizations (handled in Part 2) - Prompt context bloat (handled in Part 1) - Android (Room) and Sync backend (D1) queries - Changing the database filename, table/column model, sync wire protocol, batch limit, or same-timestamp loss-prevention rule - UI behavior or app-target changes

column2: macOS: Side-by-side source snippet comparison
column3: > **Original request:** > 2. A quick way to compare snippets of the same track across all available tapers/sources side by side, rather than switching sources one at a time to listen. ## Problem / goal Switching sources completely replaces the player's current item, making A/B testing of audio quality slow and frustrating. We need a macOS "Compare Sources" mode that lets the user rapidly toggle between short snippets of the current track from different sources at the exact same timestamp, without losing their main queue state in AVFoundation. ## Plan Files: - `macos/CouchTour/Player.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlayerRailView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/CompareSourcesView.swift` (new) Steps: 1. Add comparison mode state to `Player`: `isComparingSources`, `comparisonSources: [RecordingRef]`, `comparisonPlayers: [String: AVPlayer]`, `activeComparisonSourceId: String?`, and `originalQueueState` (to restore after comparison). 2. Implement `enterCompareSourcesMode(sources: [RecordingRef], currentTrack: PlayableTrack, positionMs: Int64)` in `Player`:    - Store current queue state (tracks, currentIndex, positionMs, isPlaying, queueKey, recording)    - For each source, fetch the ShowDetail for the current show with that recordingId    - Find the matching track (by title/position) in each source's track list    - Create an `AVPlayer` per source pre-loaded at the current timestamp    - Set `isComparingSources = true`, populate `comparisonPlayers`, start playing the first source 3. Implement `switchComparisonSource(to recordingId: String)` in `Player`:    - Pause current comparison player, seek new one to same position, play it    - Update `activeComparisonSourceId` 4. Implement `exitCompareSourcesMode(confirmSelection: Bool)` in `Player`:    - If `confirmSelection` and a different source was chosen, reload the main queue with the new source at the same track/position    - Otherwise restore original queue state exactly    - Clean up comparison players, reset comparison state 5. Create `CompareSourcesView` (popover/sheet) showing a list of sources with play/pause buttons, current timestamp display, and Confirm/Cancel actions. 6. In `PlayerRailView` and `ExpandedNowPlayingView`, add a "Compare Sources" button/menu item next to the TAPE chevron (only when `hasRealAlternates` is true). 7. Wire the Compare Sources action to call `player.enterCompareSourcesMode(...)` and present `CompareSourcesView`. Test: what proves it - Unit test: `Player` comparison mode state transitions (enter/switch/exit) work correctly - Integration test: switching sources in comparison mode seeks to the same timestamp - Manual verification: latency of switching audio streams during comparison on macOS ## Done when - [ ] The macOS Source picker (TAPE section) includes a "Compare Sources" action when alternates exist - [ ] Activating it plays a fast-switching audio preview of the current timestamp across different sources - [ ] The user can click each source to instantly switch the active preview audio - [ ] Confirming the choice switches the actual playback source in the main player - [ ] Cancelling restores the original source and queue position exactly - [ ] Comparison mode works in both PlayerRailView and ExpandedNowPlayingView ## Needs a human to check - The latency of switching audio streams during comparison on macOS. ## Context Part of #172. Related to issue #24 (Advanced Source Selection & Taper Intelligence) in ROADMAP.md.
