column2: Android: Side-by-side source snippet comparison
column3: > **Original request:** > 2. A quick way to compare snippets of the same track across all available tapers/sources side by side, rather than switching sources one at a time to listen. ## Problem / goal Switching sources completely replaces the player's current item, making A/B testing of audio quality slow and frustrating. We need an Android "Compare Sources" mode that lets the user rapidly toggle between short snippets of the current track from different sources at the exact same timestamp, without losing their main queue state in Media3. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MainActivity.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CompareSources.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlayerViewModel.kt` Steps: 1. Add a `CompareSources` sheet to the Source picker in `MainActivity.kt`: a "Compare sources" action row at the top of the existing `SourcePicker` bottom sheet that opens when the show has 2+ alternates (the same `summary.artist.hasMultipleSources && detail.alternates.isNotEmpty()` gate that already decides whether the picker appears at all). 2. In `CompareSources.kt`, build a `CompareSourcesSheet` Composable that lists every source of the current show as a toggleable row. Each row shows the label, SBD/FLAC/Matrix badges, taper, lineage, and rating — reusing `SourceRow`/`SourceBadge` from `MainActivity.kt` so the picker and the comparison sheet look like one family. Tapping a row switches the active preview. 3. In `PlayerViewModel.kt`, add `enterCompareSourcesMode(detail: ShowDetail)` and `switchComparisonSource(recordingId: String)`. The former snapshots the current queue (items, index, position, play state) via `MediaController.setMediaItems`/`seekTo` semantics, then loads the *same track* from each alternate source by matching on `PlayableTrack.title` within the fetched `ShowDetail` for that recording, builds one `MediaItem` per source via the existing `recordingMediaItem(...)` helper, and plays them from the current timestamp. The latter pauses the active preview, seeks the newly-tapped source to the same timestamp, and plays it. A `CompareSourcesState` (active recording id, whether comparing, and the original queue snapshot) is exposed on the ViewModel so the UI can render the sheet and the transport row can suppress normal controls while comparing. 4. Confirming a choice (a "Use this source" afford in the sheet, or exiting comparison) restores the original queue at its saved index and position and switches the main player to the chosen source, exactly as `SourcePicker`'s existing `nav.navigate("recording/...?src=...&resumeIndex=...&resumeMs=...")` does. 5. Snippet length: each preview auto-stops after 15 seconds (a `CompareSources.kt` constant `SNIPPET_MS = 15_000L`, overridable in tests) and loops back to the start, so A/B is fast without trimming tracks by hand. Tapping another source restarts the snippet from the shared timestamp. 6. Cover the new logic with `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/CompareSourcesTest.kt`: a Robolectric test that builds a `CompareSourcesState`, verifies the matched-track index across two `ShowDetail`s with the same track title, verifies `SNIPPET_MS` clamping, and verifies the original-queue snapshot round-trips. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green, including the new `CompareSourcesTest`, and the existing `MediaItemsTest`/`CatalogTest` still pass. ## Done when - [ ] The Android Source picker includes a "Compare Sources" action. - [ ] Activating it plays a fast-switching audio preview of the current timestamp across different sources. - [ ] The user can tap each source to instantly switch the active preview audio. - [ ] Confirming the choice switches the actual playback source in the main player. - [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes, including the new `CompareSourcesTest`. - [ ] While comparing, the main queue is untouched and is restored at the saved position when comparison ends. ## Needs a human to check - The latency of switching audio streams during comparison on Android. - Whether 15-second snippets feel right for A/B, or the user wants them adjustable. ## Context Part of #172. Depends on #17 (Source picker, shipped) — the comparison action lives inside that picker's bottom sheet and reuses its `SourceRow`/`SourceBadge` components and its `?src=` navigation. Out of scope: macOS implementation (tracked in #236) and full waveform cross-fading (simple fast-switching is enough). ## Out of scope - Full waveform cross-fading (simple fast-switching is enough). - macOS implementation (tracked separately). - Volume leveling across sources (#18, deferred — no reliable per-show gain data exists).

column2: Part 3 of #177: Android YouTube audio/video playback & toggle
column3: > **Original request:** Support playing YouTube videos, as video or audio-only, ideally with a toggle between the two. (Android half — see #16.) Part of #177 Depends on: #233 ## Problem / goal Build YouTube audio/video playback into the Android client: audio-only background playback that integrates with the existing Media3/ExoPlayer pipeline and the lockscreen / notification / Bluetooth / headset-button controls exactly like any other track, plus a toggle that flips a playing YouTube item to video (rendering in place of the artwork) and back to audio-only with the screen off and the app backgrounded. ## Plan Files: - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Catalog.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MediaItems.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/NowPlaying.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlayerViewModel.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/PlaybackService.kt` - `app/src/main/java/dev/mike/couchtour/Queue.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/MediaItemsTest.kt` - `app/src/test/java/dev/mike/couchtour/QueueTest.kt` Steps: 1. Add a `YOUTUBE` entry to the `Backend` enum (`Catalog.kt:190`) so channel-artist attribution, like-button routing, and the default-artist fallback in `PlayerViewModel.refresh()` handle YouTube the same way they already handle Relisten. 2. Add a `youtube:` namespace in `Queue.kt`: a `QueueKind.YOUTUBE`, a `youtubeQueueKey(videoId)` builder, and a parse branch in `parseQueueKey` so each video gets its own resumable, non-colliding progress key (`youtube:<videoId>`) — mirroring the `relisten:` keys. 3. In `MediaItems.kt`, add `youtubeMediaItem(track, info)` converging on `coreMediaItem`, defaulting the playback URI to the audio-only stream, stashing the video URL under a new `Keys.YOUTUBE_VIDEO_URL` extra, tagging the backend `Backend.YOUTUBE`, setting the channel as `artist` and the video title as `title` (per D50 the Last.fm app scrobbles the channel), and leaving the show/queue context as `albumTitle`. 4. Extend the `Keys` object in `PlaybackService.kt` with `YOUTUBE_VIDEO_URL` + `VIDEO_MODE` and add both to `Keys.ALL` so Cast hand-back drops nothing and the audio/video state round-trips through the MediaMetadata extras; expose surface plumbing (`setVideoSurface`) on the local `ExoPlayer`. 5. In `PlayerViewModel.kt`, add `playYouTube(track)` (single-item queue, audio-only by default), a `videoMode` field on `PlayerState` read from the `VIDEO_MODE` extra, a `toggleVideoMode()` that flips the flag and signals `PlaybackService`, and a `QueueKind.YOUTUBE` branch in `resume()`. 6. In `NowPlaying.kt`, render a video `SurfaceView` (via `AndroidView`) in place of the artwork when `state.videoMode` is true, add an audio/video toggle button to the transport row, and keep the existing artwork + ambient glow for audio-only. 7. Add tests in `MediaItemsTest.kt` (YouTube item defaults to the audio stream URI with `VIDEO_MODE=false`, carries `Keys.YOUTUBE_VIDEO_URL` and `Backend.YOUTUBE` in extras) and `QueueTest.kt` (`youtube:` round-trip and no prefix collision), then run `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green. Test: `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green. `MediaItemsTest` asserts a YouTube `MediaItem` plays the audio-only stream URI, carries `Keys.YOUTUBE_VIDEO_URL` and `Backend.YOUTUBE` in extras; `QueueTest` asserts `youtube:<id>` round-trips and never collides with the `show:` / `playlist:` / `relisten:` / `local-playlist:` prefixes. ## Done when - [ ] A YouTube item plays audio in the background, controllable from the lockscreen, notification, Bluetooth, and headset buttons exactly like any other track. - [ ] The MediaSession publishes the video's title as the title and the channel as the artist; the album stays the show/queue context so the Last.fm app scrobbles correctly (per D50). - [ ] Playback position is saved per URL (`youtube:<videoId>` queue key) and restored from "Continue listening" like any other track; playing through to the end marks it finished. - [ ] A toggle in Now Playing switches to video mode: the video renders in place of the artwork with the existing transport controls; toggling back to audio-only stops the video surface and resumes audio-only. - [ ] Audio-only mode keeps playing with the screen off and when the app is backgrounded. - [ ] `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is green, with new tests covering the audio/video toggle state. - [ ] A beta is cut via `scripts/cut-beta.sh` so Mike can verify on device. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing (the lockscreen / Bluetooth / headset-button control and on-device video rendering are verified by the end-of-batch beta on physical hardware; unit tests cover the queue-key and toggle-state logic). ## Context **Owner decision (#16, 2026-09):** Android keeps background audio-only playback and the audio/video toggle — unlike macOS (#231), which is visible-only. The queue-key prefix is `youtube:` on both platforms so progress rows sync and resume across devices (macOS #231 uses the same prefix). Phase 3 (ROADMAP L5), the Android half of #16 (macOS is #178). Reuses Media3/ExoPlayer, `MediaItems.coreMediaItem`, `PlaybackService`, `Progress`, and the Now Playing surface. The app has never played video, so Now Playing gains a video surface; the existing artwork/artwork-glow styling stays for audio-only. This issue consumes the `YouTubeTrack` data model that Part 1 (#232) defines — it does not resolve stream URLs from YouTube itself. Obtaining a playable audio-only stream URL and a video URL (the credentials / API-key / extraction decision) is #232's responsibility and owned by the owner; the playback code is written against the URL fields #232 exposes, so this build is autonomous once #232 and #233 have landed (its `Depends on: #233`). A YouTube item starts in audio-only mode (matching the app's background-first philosophy); video is an explicit opt-in via the toggle. ## Out of scope - Discovering or matching YouTube content to shows; searching YouTube (browsing UI is Part 2, #233; content discovery is not playback's job). - Downloads (not planned, per #65). - Casting a YouTube *video* to a stock Google Cast receiver — a video surface can't be handed off to the stock receiver, so YouTube Cast video is deferred (audio-only Cast hand-back of the resolved URL is still preserved via `Keys.ALL`). - macOS implementation (#178).

column2: Part 3 of #178: macOS YouTube audio/video playback & toggle
column3: > **Original request:** Support playing YouTube videos, as video or audio-only, ideally with a toggle between the two. (macOS half — see #16.) Part of #178 Depends on: #230 ## Problem / goal Build the macOS playback path for a YouTube video selected from the artist-channel UI delivered by #230. Reuse the existing `Player` transport (play/pause, next/previous, seek/scrub, volume), media-key handling, Cast route picker, `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` metadata, progress/history recording, and the expanded Now Playing / mini / rail / inspector surfaces. Use YouTube's **official embedded IFrame player** in a `WKWebView`; never extract direct media URLs, never create a hidden/background player, and never separate audio from video — YouTube's embedded-player policies prohibit both. **Decision already resolved by the owner (see comment on this issue):** background audio-only playback is dropped. Playback is **visible-only**: a YouTube video plays through the official embedded IFrame player displayed in the expanded Now Playing surface. The audio↔video "toggle" from the original request is therefore not implemented — audio-only / background is out of scope and the official embed cannot produce it, so there is no second mode to toggle between. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/QueueKey.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/PlaybackMode.swift` (new — pure playback-mode/state model the app switches on and the player drives) - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/QueueKeyTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/PlaybackModeTests.swift` (new) - `macos/CouchTour/Player.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/YouTubePlayerView.swift` (new — official IFrame `WKWebView` bridge) - `macos/CouchTour/ExpandedNowPlayingView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/MiniPlayerView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/PlayerRailView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/NowPlayingInspector.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/Resume.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/ListeningView.swift` - `macos/CouchTour/HomeView.swift` - `UAT.md` - `README.md` Steps: 1. Consume the `YouTubeVideo` contract from #229 and the `playYoutube(video:)` stub + `Route.youtube` from #230. Define one canonical video identity (the video ID) and the `youtube:<videoId>` queue key it yields. 2. In `CouchTourKit`: add `QueueKind.youtube` + `youtubeQueueKey(_:)` + `parseQueueKey` handling (a `youtube:` prefix that round-trips to the video ID and does not collide with the existing `show:`/`playlist:`/`relisten:`/`local-playlist:` namespaces). Add a pure `PlaybackMode`/state model (`.audio` vs `.youtube`) with its state transitions, so the player's mode is testable without a `WKWebView`. Cover canonicalization, invalid/missing IDs, round trips, and mode state transitions in the package tests. 3. Implement the official IFrame `WKWebView` bridge in `YouTubePlayerView.swift`: per-player state messages (ready/playing/paused/progress/ended) bridged to the `Player`, user-initiated playback only (YouTube requires a tap), the app bundle ID sent as the `Referer`, and clean teardown on item change. The web view is always presented — never hidden. 4. Replace the `playYoutube(video:)` stub body in `Player.swift`: set the YouTube mode, set `queueKey` to the canonical `youtube:` key, publish `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` (title = video title, artist = channel, album = show/queue context, duration/elapsed/rate), drive transport + media keys (including the Cast path's no-op for YouTube), and feed position/duration/ended back into the existing `ProgressRecorder` so position is saved per video and end-of-video calls `markFinished`. 5. Wire the surfaces: `ExpandedNowPlayingView` shows the `YouTubePlayerView` video surface in place of the artwork tile while a YouTube item is active; `MiniPlayerView`/`PlayerRailView`/`NowPlayingInspector` render channel-as-artist/title when `PlaybackMode.youtube`; `Resume.swift`/`ListeningView.swift`/`HomeView.swift` persist and resume by the canonical `youtube:` queue key and let Continue Listening open it. 6. Run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` (green) and `cd macos && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` (green); add `uat-054` to `UAT.md`; bump the macOS package test count in `README.md`. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` is green with tests for the `youtube:` queue-key canonicalization/round-trip and `PlaybackMode` state transitions; the macOS app target compiles via the `xcodegen generate && xcodebuild … build` command above. ## Done when - [ ] A YouTube video selected from #230's artist page starts through the official embedded IFrame player and is controllable from the existing transport (play/pause, next/previous, seek/scrub, volume) and media keys while the player is visible. - [ ] The visible video surface lives in the expanded Now Playing; the `WKWebView` player is never hidden and never separates audio from video. - [ ] `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` publishes the video title as title, the channel as artist, and the show/queue context as album, with elapsed time and playback rate. - [ ] Position is saved per canonical YouTube video (`youtube:<videoId>`), restored from Continue Listening, and reaching the end marks the row finished. - [ ] `swift test` is green with coverage of the `youtube:` queue-key parsing/canonicalization and `PlaybackMode` state transitions. - [ ] `cd macos && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project CouchTour.xcodeproj -scheme CouchTour -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build` is green. - [ ] `UAT.md` contains a `uat-054` macOS YouTube playback check. ## Needs a human to check - Complete `uat-054`: visually confirm a YouTube video plays through the visible embedded player, the existing transport/metadata/progress surfaces reflect it, and Continue Listening resumes at the saved position. (The visible-only-vs-background-audio decision is already resolved by the owner — visible-only; see Context.) ## Context Phase 3 (ROADMAP L5), macOS half of #16, and Part 3 of the #178 batch. #229 supplies the `YouTubeVideo` model and `YouTubeAPI` client in `CouchTourKit`; #230 supplies the artist-page route, the `playYoutube(video:)` stub, and `Route.youtube` — this issue consumes that contract and implements real playback. Existing macOS playback is AVFoundation/`AVQueuePlayer` for phish.in audio; YouTube needs a separate official embedded-player path. The pure, `swift test`-covered surface lives in the package (queue-key canonicalization + a `PlaybackMode` state model); the `WKWebView` bridge and the Now Playing surfaces stay in the app target, which CI does not build (D208) — so the app-target compile check above is the floor, and `uat-054` is the ceiling. Recorded decision (owner comment on this issue): **visible-only.** Background audio-only playback and any audio/video toggle are dropped — YouTube's embedded-player policies prohibit a hidden/background player and prohibit separating the streams. The `youtube:` queue-key namespace is added to macOS `parseQueueKey`; an Android client that does not yet recognize it skips the row rather than mis-playing it, so this is safe for the eventual shared `progress` table. The builder should also: (a) add a `DECISIONS.md` entry (next `Dnn`) recording the visible-only choice, and (b) update ROADMAP #16's "audio-only background playback" wording to match — both are repo-convention bookkeeping for a decision made here. No new account, credential, or API key is added in this issue: the IFrame embed needs none, and the `videos.list` duration call from #229's scope is optional (the player reports duration through its state bridge; `YouTubeVideo.durationMs` is accepted as nil). #229 owns the Google/YouTube credential boundary. ## Out of scope - Discovering, searching, matching, or ranking YouTube content (#229). - Direct stream extraction, caching/downloads, undocumented YouTube APIs, or any hidden/background player / audio-video separation. - The audio↔video toggle (audio-only is dropped per the owner's decision; the official embed cannot produce an audio-only stream anyway). - Android implementation (#16 Parts 1-2 / #177 / #232). - Resolving which artist maps to which YouTube channel ID (a #229/#230 concern). - Registering a Google Cloud project or API key (owner account action, per D44).

column2: Part 1 of #178: macOS YouTube API client & data model
column3: > **Original request:** Support playing YouTube videos, as video or audio-only, ideally with a toggle between the two. (macOS half — see #16.) Part of #178 ## Problem / goal Build the data layer for YouTube support in `CouchTourKit`. Per the owner's direction in #16 ("YouTube content should be browsable from artist channels"), this adds a YouTube API client that fetches a channel's videos and a catalog model type that represents a YouTube video alongside a regular show. This is Part 1 — the foundation that #230 (Artist page UI) and #231 (Playback) build on. ## Plan Follow the exact patterns already established by `PhishInAPI` (PhishInAPI.swift) and `RelistenAPI` (RelistenAPI.swift): a stateless `enum` with a `public static var baseURL` override for tests, a private `get()` helper wrapping `URLSession.shared`, and a `JSONDecoder`. Tests use the existing `MockServer` (MockServer.swift) and the `fixtureData`/`fixtureString` helpers (Fixture.swift), the same way `RequestTests.swift` and `PhishInParsingTests.swift` exercise the other two backends. **YouTube Data API v3 `search.list` with `channelId`** is the endpoint — it returns `items[].id.videoId` plus `items[].snippet` (title, description, thumbnails, publishedAt), which is exactly the browse metadata the catalog model needs. Duration lives in `contentDetails` on a separate `videos.list` call and is **not** in `search.list`'s `snippet` part, so `YouTubeVideo.durationMs` is an optional `Int64?` here — Part 3 (#231) is where a second `videos.list` request for `contentDetails.duration` belongs. This single endpoint suffices for "fetch a list of videos for a given channel ID". **API key**: modeled as `public static var apiKey: String?`, sent as the `?key=` query param only when non-nil — same fail-open-but-obvious behavior D44 settled for the Last.fm key ("must come from you; I won't register one"). Tests don't need it (MockServer doesn't validate it); the app target wires the real key at runtime. The builder does not register a Google Cloud project — that is an owner account action, out of scope for this issue. **Channel ID**: a parameter to `search(channelId:)`, not hardcoded. The mapping of which artist maps to which YouTube channel ID is a Part 2 (#230) concern; Part 1 just needs the client to accept one. Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/YouTubeAPI.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/YouTubeParsingTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/RequestTests.swift` - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Tests/CouchTourKitTests/Fixtures/youtube_search.json` - `README.md` Steps: - Create `YouTubeAPI.swift` mirroring `PhishInAPI`: a `YouTubeAPI` enum with   `public static var baseURL` (overridable for tests, same as `PhishInAPI.baseURL`),   `public static var apiKey: String?` (sent as `?key=` only when non-nil), a private   `get(_:)` helper that attaches `Accept: application/json` and raises `APIException` on   non-2xx (same `APIException` already in `PhishInAPI.swift`), and `search(channelId:)`   that builds `https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/search` with `part=snippet`,   `channelId`, `type=video`, `maxResults=50`, `order=date`, and the optional `key`. DTOs:   `YouTubeSearchResponse` (Decodable, wraps `items: [YouTubeVideoDTO]`) and   `YouTubeVideoDTO` (Decodable, decodes `id.videoId`, `snippet.title/description/   publishedAt/thumbnails`), all fields using `decodeIfPresent` with safe defaults — the   same defensive decoding style as `Show`/`Track` in `PhishInAPI.swift`. - Add a `YouTubeVideo` struct to `Catalog.swift` alongside `ShowSummary`/`PlayableTrack`,   mirroring how the neutral model lives there while DTOs stay in the API file. Fields:   `id: String`, `title: String`, `thumbnailURL: String?`, `durationMs: Int64?` (optional   until Part 3), `publishedAt: Date?`, `channelId: String`, `description: String?`. Add a   `YouTubeVideoDTO.toYouTubeVideo(channelId:)` mapping extension on the same seam as   `Show.toShowSummary()` and `RelistenSourceTrack.toPlayableTrack()`. - Drop a `youtube_search.json` fixture (trimmed from a real `search.list` response) into   `Tests/CouchTourKitTests/Fixtures/` and write `YouTubeParsingTests` decoding it, asserting   title/thumbnail/videoId/publishedAt extraction and graceful handling of missing   `thumbnails`/`description`/`publishedAt`. - Add `RequestTests` cases for `YouTubeAPI`: asserts `channelId` and `part=snippet` land in   the query, `key` is sent when set, omitted when nil, path is `/youtube/v3/search`. - Run `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` until green. Bump the macOS test count   in `README.md` (currently 428) to match the new test count. Test: `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` passes with the new tests; the `YouTubeVideoDTO.toYouTubeVideo()` mapping has no force-unwraps on optional fields; a real `youtube_search.json` fixture decodes end-to-end. ## Done when - [ ] `YouTubeAPI` in `CouchTourKit` can fetch a list of videos for a given channel ID via   the YouTube Data API v3 `search.list` endpoint (channelId query param, type=video). - [ ] `Catalog.swift` defines a `YouTubeVideo` struct representing a YouTube video with the   fields the catalog needs (video id, title, thumbnail url, optional duration, published   date, channel id, optional description). - [ ] `YouTubeParsingTests.swift` decodes a real `youtube_search.json` fixture and asserts   correct mapping of all fields, including graceful handling of missing optional fields. - [ ] `RequestTests.swift` covers `YouTubeAPI`'s request shape (channelId + part=snippet in   query, optional key param, correct path, APIException on error). - [ ] `cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test` is green. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing (data-layer only; verified by unit tests + MockServer, no device needed) ## Context Phase 3 (ROADMAP L5). Issue #16's owner direction: "YouTube content should browsable from artist channels." This is Part 1 of the three-part macOS YouTube build (#230 UI, #231 playback). It follows the data-layer/API-client split already used by `PhishInAPI`/` RelistenAPI` (DTOs in the API file, neutral model in `Catalog.swift`). The API key and the Phish channel ID are intentionally deferred: the key is an owner-supplied credential (D44 precedent) wired at the app-target level; the channel ID is a parameter resolved in Part 2. ## Out of scope - UI for browsing YouTube videos (#230). - Audio-only / video playback and the audio<->video toggle (#231). - Android implementation (#232). - Resolving which artist maps to which YouTube channel ID. - The separate `videos.list` call for ISO-8601 `contentDetails.duration`. - Playlist pagination (`nextPageToken` — a single 50-item page suffices for Part 1).

column2: macOS external release data model and show page link UI
column3: > **Original request:** In-app playback isn't feasible (DRM/licensing). Instead, when a phish.in/Relisten show matches an officially released live album on Spotify or Tidal, surface a simple external link (opens the Spotify/Tidal app or web player) from the show page. > > Part of #179 ## Problem / goal Define the macOS data model for associating a show with an external release (platform, URL) and add the external link UI element to the macOS show page. ## Plan Files: - `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit/Sources/CouchTourKit/Catalog.swift` — add `ExternalReleasePlatform` enum and `ExternalRelease` struct; extend `ShowSummary` and `ShowDetail` to carry optional `externalRelease` - `macos/CouchTour/Browse/ShowDetailView.swift` — add external link button to the action pills row - `macos/CouchTour/DesignSystem/ExternalLinkButton.swift` (new) — reusable external link pill component matching existing pill design Steps: 1. Add `ExternalReleasePlatform` enum (cases: `spotify`, `tidal`) and `ExternalRelease` struct (platform, url) to `Catalog.swift` 2. Extend `ShowSummary` and `ShowDetail` in `Catalog.swift` to carry optional `externalRelease: ExternalRelease?` 3. Create `ExternalLinkButton` in `macos/CouchTour/DesignSystem/ExternalLinkButton.swift` — a pill-styled button with platform icon/label that opens the URL via `NSWorkspace.shared.open()` (deep link `spotify://` / `tidal://` with `https://` web fallback) 4. In `ShowDetailView.swift`, import and use `ExternalLinkButton` in `actionPillsRow`, shown only when `detail.summary.externalRelease` is non-nil 5. Add unit tests for `ExternalRelease` model and the URL builder logic in `CatalogTests.swift` Test: what proves it - `CatalogTests.swift` — `testExternalReleaseModel()` verifies `ExternalRelease` encoding/decoding and platform enum cases - `CatalogTests.swift` — `testShowSummaryCarriesExternalRelease()` verifies `ShowSummary` and `ShowDetail` round-trip with optional external release - `ExternalLinkButton` logic test — verifies deep-link URL construction for both platforms with web fallback - Existing test suite passes (`cd macos/Packages/CouchTourKit && swift test`) ## Done when - [ ] macOS backend-neutral catalog model (`macos/Packages/CouchTourKit`) includes `ExternalReleasePlatform` enum (Spotify/Tidal) and `ExternalRelease` struct (platform, URL) - [ ] `ShowSummary` and `ShowDetail` in `Catalog.swift` carry optional `externalRelease: ExternalRelease?` - [ ] macOS show page (`ShowDetailView.swift`) displays an external link pill/button in the action pill row when an external release exists - [ ] Link opens in Spotify/Tidal app via URL Scheme (`spotify://` / `tidal://`) with web player fallback (`https://open.spotify.com/...`, `https://tidal.com/...`) - [ ] Pill is absent (no empty placeholder) when no external release exists - [ ] All existing macOS package tests pass ## Needs a human to check - Taste on link placement and styling relative to existing action pills (Like, Add to playlist) — pill height 38pt, corner radius 8pt, icon + label format matching current pill design - Whether the external link should also appear on Relisten shows with multiple sources (match is at show level, so yes — show on both phish.in and Relisten show pages) ## Context This is the foundation — the data model and UI shell that Part 2 (matching logic, curated or heuristic) will populate. The backend-neutral catalog model in `macos/Packages/CouchTourKit` carries the association. Link deep-link handling follows macOS conventions (`NSWorkspace.shared.open()`). The Android counterpart is issue #227 (already `mahler:ready`). This issue mirrors its scope for macOS. ## Out of scope - Matching logic (curated or heuristic) — separate issue (Part 2 of #179) - Android implementation — issue #227 - In-app playback of Spotify/Tidal content — not feasible (DRM/licensing) - Sync backend changes — the association is device-local for now; sync can be added later if needed ## Depends on: #179

column2: Part 2.1: Google TV app — TV Artist & Year browse UI

column2: Part 2 of #188: macOS dead code & deprecated API audit
column3: > **Original request:** > ## Problem / goal > Prune unused composables/views, obsolete network adapters, and deprecated API usages that have been superseded by recent beta features across Android and macOS. >  > (This issue focuses specifically on the macOS codebase) ## Problem / goal Audit the macOS codebase to identify unused SwiftUI views, obsolete network adapters, and deprecated APIs. Document a detailed plan mapping out what dead code and superseded APIs can be safely removed from the macOS app. ## Done when - [ ] A document (e.g. `macos_dead_code_audit.md`) is written to the root directory outlining the findings. - [ ] Unused macOS SwiftUI views and obsolete network adapters are listed. - [ ] Deprecated API usages in the macOS app are catalogued alongside their beta/new feature replacements. - [ ] The document includes a macOS-specific removal plan that estimates the scope of effort and prioritizes the removals. ## Needs a human to check - Nothing. This is a scan/audit only — actual removals are follow-up tasks. ## Context After extensive feature development, codebases accumulate dead weight: views that no longer resolve, adapters for retired endpoints, and APIs superseded by newer approaches. Cleaning this up keeps the macOS codebase navigable. This is the macOS portion of the dead code audit. ## Out of scope - Auditing the Android codebase. - Performing the actual code removals (these are follow-up tasks). - Refactoring active, used code. Part of #188 Depends on: #187
